about: Every player-facing string of the five apps (docs/plan.md slice 18, "The copy pipeline", and slice 35 for the desktop app; docs/ui.md, "Parity"): one entry per key, which tools/copytext.py writes into the string catalogs of the iPhone and the watch apps, the strings.xml files of the Android phone and Wear OS apps, and the desktop app's helper/dist/lib/copy.js (its page's words) and helper/src-tauri/src/copy.rs (what its Rust draws itself: the tray, the window's frame, the macOS menu, the system's dialogs). A key is lower-case words joined by dots (pump.card.title); `text` holds the English, with placeholders as {name} typed in `args` (int or string; an int shows its digits grouped by the locale) and no other brace, a % only beside an argument ({percent}%), and a #name# token the system fills (the Ongoing Activity's #t#) as written in every form; `plural` gives the one and other forms of a string that counts its first argument, an int; `screens` names the screens of contract/design/screens.json that show it (their surfaces decide the platforms, which `platforms` may narrow); `max` caps a watch string's length, and every string a watch screen shows has one: the characters the 40 mm watch has room for, a placeholder counted as two characters whatever it holds; `legal` marks a text whose wording the product must carry (the safety note, the not-a-medical-device line), which the deny-list does not judge and tools/lint.lua lists (LEGAL_KEYS); `note` speaks to a translator; `plist` ties a text to the Info.plist usage string it must equal, a target's in apple/project.yml (`target`, `key`) or the desktop app's helper/src-tauri/Info.plist (`file`, `key`), which the desktop app's catalogs leave out; `translate: false` marks a name no language changes (the app's own); `spellcheck: false` marks a text that shows a code, which Android lint's English spell check would flag, and `noPlural: true` a string that formats a count whose words take no plural form (a rested amount, a target that is never 1), which Android lint's PluralsCandidate would flag: each is tools:ignore on that one string. Never hard-code a user-visible string in Swift, Kotlin or the desktop app's JavaScript and Rust, the cores' included: tools/copytext.py --lint fails on one (a literal that is an entry's text names its key; a literal no player reads carries `// copy-lint: not shown (<why>)`), on a key literal the app's own copy lacks, on a key the iPhone or the watch ships that no Swift reads, and on a key the desktop app ships that neither its page nor its Rust names.

app.name.note: The app's name: under its icon, in the system's settings, as the watch's start screen title and in its widget, on a shared record's card and as the wordmark on the phone's first start. Never translated.

bar.book.note: Action bar label and its screen's title: the book of the move ladders and the move library; also Your moves' row that opens the Book's Moves to find a move (2026-10-22). One short word: the bar has four tabs (five on the desktop app, slice 56).

bar.games.note: The desktop app's fifth root's tab label, its title and its item in the macOS app menu's View (Cmd-5): the Games tab, the games found on this computer and the offers after a match (docs/plan.md slice 56). A noun. One short word: the bar has five tabs on the desktop app. The phones have no such tab.

bar.hero.note: Action bar label and its screen's title: the player's hero, its body and its stats. One short word: the bar has four tabs (five on the desktop app, slice 56).

bar.log.note: Action bar label and its screen's title: the Saga, the player's game days told as chapters, each with its moves, records and unlocks (the Log until 2026-10-15; the code keeps the name log). One short word: the bar has four tabs (five on the desktop app, slice 56).

bar.menu.note: Name of the round gear button on a main screen, read by VoiceOver and TalkBack, and the title of the page it opens: settings, help and the app's pages.

bar.pump.note: Action bar label and its screen's title: the Pump screen, where a pump waits and runs. A noun. One short word: the bar has four tabs (five on the desktop app, slice 56).

best.ding.note: The first word of the best-day moment, in caps over its banner: the game's sound of a level gained, here for a new most moves in one day.

best.label.note: Caps label under the best-day moment's big number.

best.old.note: Under Moves in one day: the most moves of one day before today and the day that set it ({date}: Tue 14 Oct).

best.share.note: The best-day moment's gold button: opens the Share window on today's day card.

best.title.note: The best-day moment's title: today the player did more moves than on any day before. Shown once a game day; nothing is awarded.

bill.more.note: The receipt's last move line when more moves were done than it lists: after the + in its counts' column, where the moves' names start, and before their moves (+ 12 more lines … 47 moves).

bill.new.note: On a receipt line beside a move with a red seal: its new record ({value}: 31, a hold's 1:42).

bill.seal.best.note: Under the receipt's wax seal on a game day with more moves than any day before.

bill.span.note: Under The Quest Bill: the game day's date (Tue 14 Oct) and its hours, from 04:00 to 04:00 in the player's clock.

bill.strip.text: My game day, a bar a pump
bill.strip.note: Caps line under the receipt's barcode, which draws each of the day's pumps as a bar.

bill.title.note: The receipt card's title, in Cinzel caps: a bill for the day's moves.

bill.total.note: Over the receipt's total, in Cinzel caps: every move of the day was done.

bill.unlocked.note: On a receipt line: the move's step reached for the first time that day, in its quality ({quality}: Rare, Epic and so on).

card.days.note: Caps label under the week card's days with a move.

card.records.note: Caps label under the day card's number of records.

card.saga.note: The day card's title beside the app's mark, in Cinzel caps.

card.site.note: The app's web address, small at the foot of a shared card. Keep it as written.

character.focus.action.note: TalkBack's action on Hero's focus Chip ("Double-tap to change your focus"): it opens the window to pick what the pumps lean toward.

character.focus.ask.title.note: The focus window's title when the app asks once, after a pump, at the level where the choice opens: {level} is that level (10). QP is the hero's level. The game's ui.focus.titleAsk.

character.focus.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint on Hero's focus Chip (Balanced focus): tapping it opens the window to pick what the pumps lean toward. Apple's hints start with a verb in the third person.

character.focus.keep.note: The primary button when the app asks for the focus: it keeps the default mix, Balanced (the game's ui.focus.keep).

character.focus.recommended.note: The first row of the focus window: {focus} is Balanced, the mix the game recommends (the game's ui.focus.recommended).

character.focus.title.note: Title of the window where the player picks what the pumps lean toward (the game's ui.focus.title).

character.map.label.note: The accessibility label of the switch that picks what the body map shows (This week or Rungs).

character.map.title.note: Hero's section label over the body map (2026-10-29: its shades had no key): each muscle drawn in the quality colour of the best step of the moves that train it, Starter's grey the first, an untrained one dark.

character.meta.focus.note: Hero's focus Chip in the chips row, beside the source and the streak: the focus the pumps lean toward, as the game names it (Balanced focus; Strength, Endurance, Flexibility), Balanced before one is chosen. A button that opens the focus window.

character.muscle.best.chart.note: The chart's name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: Chest: best step over time.

character.muscle.best.title.note: Chart title: the muscle's best step by date.

character.muscle.fallback.note: A muscle's name when the sheet's words lack it: Muscle 4.

character.muscle.pro.text: Your muscles over time come with QuestPump Pro.
character.muscle.pro.note: A muscle's detail without Pro: its charts come with the subscription. QuestPump Pro is a product name.

character.muscle.raise.note: How to raise a muscle's quality: the step on the one 12-step scale where the next quality starts, the open ladder listed above it that stands highest (its family's name, Push; never a locked one), and that quality's word (Rare).

character.muscle.raise.top.note: A muscle at the highest quality: nothing above it. {quality} is its word (Legendary).

character.muscle.untrained.note: Not trained yet: a muscle with no rung yet (its best rung's value, its chart's value before the first rung), the Book's filter chip for the moves never done, the Book's tooltip line and the You card on a move's page for a move never done.

character.muscle.week.note: The accessibility value of a muscle button: its moves this game week (after its quality word).

character.muscle.weeks.chart.note: The chart's name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: Chest: moves per week.

character.muscle.weeks.title.note: Chart title: the muscle's moves in each game week.

character.name.action.note: TalkBack's action on the hero's name ("Double-tap to change your title"): it opens the title window.

character.name.fallback.note: The hero's name when the sheet carries none, or when only the app's own pumps fill the tab.

character.name.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint on the hero's name when the sheet is the app's own and a title is earned: tapping it opens the window to pick the title shown with the name.

character.open.action.note: TalkBack's action where a tap opens a page ("Double-tap to open its page"): a muscle of the body map and its tooltip, a muscle page's ladder line, a ladder page's step a move switched off holds.

character.open.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint where a tap opens a page: a muscle of the body map and its tooltip (the muscle's page), a muscle page's ladder line and a ladder page's step a move switched off holds (the move's page). Apple's hints start with a verb in the third person.

character.quality.note: A loot quality with its numeral (Rare 4): a muscle's best rung, on its badge and its chart.

character.raised.by.note: Small caps label on a stat's page over the ladders whose moves add to it.

character.source.note: Hero's source chip for a sheet from the game: {computer} is the name of the computer the helper runs on (Mia's MacBook), {ago} how long ago the sheet came, in the phone's short relative style (2 min ago). A tap opens the helper's page.

character.source.app.note: Hero's source chip when the sheet is the app's own and holds pumps of more than one device: on the computer always (the pumps done in QuestPump on any device: this computer, the phone, the watch), on the phone once a watch's or the computer's pumps are in it (until then This phone), never the game's. A click opens This computer on the computer, the helper's page on the phone.

character.source.phone.note: Hero's source chip when the sheet is the app's own and holds only this phone's pumps (once a watch's or the computer's are in it, Your app pumps). A tap opens the helper's page. Android's; the iPhone's is character.source.phone.ios.

character.source.phone.ios.note: Hero's source chip when the sheet is the app's own and holds only this phone's pumps (once a watch's or the computer's are in it, Your app pumps). A tap opens the helper's page. The iPhone's twin of character.source.phone. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

character.stat.chart.note: Chart title and its name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: Strength over time. {name} is a stat, a rating or Level.

character.stat.fallback.note: A stat's name when the sheet's words lack it: Stat 2.

character.stat.gain.chart.note: The gain chart's name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: Strength gained per week.

character.stat.gain.title.note: Chart title: the stat's points gained in each game week.

character.stat.level.note: The QuestPump level, one of the values the stat detail can show beside the stats and ratings.

character.stat.level.value.note: The level with the share of the next one earned: QP 3 · 40%. QP stays as it is.

character.stat.pro.text: Your level and stats over time come with QuestPump Pro.
character.stat.pro.note: The one line on a stat's page without Pro: its charts come with the subscription. QuestPump Pro is a product name.

character.stat.week.note: A stat's gain this game week under its value: +6 this week. {gain} is the signed number the app formats.

character.streak.tokens.note: Hero's streak chip beside the source chip while a streak runs and rest tokens are held (the game's tip.hud.streak): {days} is the streak's game days, {count} the rest tokens held, each covering one game day without a pump. Shown only while a streak runs; with no token held character.streak shows instead. {days} comes formatted (one counted number a plural: Xcode infers the plural's argument only then).

character.switcher.fallback.note: A character's name in the switcher when the sheet carries none: Character 2.

character.title.none.note: The title window's first row: the name stands alone.

character.title.title.note: Title of the window where the player picks the title shown with the hero's name.

character.tooltip.record.note: A muscle's tooltip on the body map: the move that gave it its colour and that move's record (Pike push-up · record 9; a hold's in seconds, 45 s).

character.trained.by.note: Small caps label on a muscle's page over the ladders whose moves train it.

charts.axis.date.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the name of a chart's time axis; VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.axis.week.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the name of a weekly chart's time axis; VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.empty.text: Do a pump to start this chart.
charts.empty.note: A chart with no points yet (a new player, or a sheet that never changed).

charts.legend.star.note: A chart legend's words after the gold star glyph: a day (or a game week) the chart stars for its new records. Pro's weeks' steps legend says log.calendar.record.

charts.minutes.note: Minutes played in a chart's values, and the Shortest session row's value on Games on this phone.

charts.name.minutes.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis and series of the minutes-played chart.

charts.name.moves.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis and series of a chart that counts moves; VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.name.points.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis of a stat's gain chart (stat points); VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.name.quality.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis and series of a muscle's best-rung chart (its loot quality); VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.name.records.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the series of a chart's record stars, each a day (or a game week) named by its records (2 records).

charts.name.reps.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis of a record chart that counts repetitions; VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.name.rung.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis and series of a ladder's step chart; VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.name.seconds.note: VoiceOver's audio graph: the value axis of a record chart that counts a hold's seconds; VoiceOver also reads it on each mark of the chart.

charts.plot.shown.note: VoiceOver reads it on a ladder's record chart, before what a mark shows, as the legend names it (Record, Your counts).

charts.points.note: Stat points in a gain chart's values: 3 points.

charts.row.note: A row of a chart's values list when the chart has several series: 3 Oct, Record.

charts.steps.from.note: The top shade of the moves' steps in a legend: low moves or more (10+).

charts.steps.none.note: The lowest shade of the moves' steps, in a chart's legend and axis: no moves.

charts.steps.range.note: A shade of the moves' steps in a legend: from low to high moves (1–3).

charts.summary.counts.note: TalkBack's summary of a record chart: how many counts the player typed, the latest and its date. A count is the number of reps or seconds the player typed after a move.

charts.summary.first.note: TalkBack's summary of a chart: the first value and its date (12 on 3 Oct).

charts.summary.lastweek.note: TalkBack's summary of a weekly chart: last game week's amount.

charts.summary.now.note: TalkBack's summary of a chart, its first part: the value now. Parts are joined by semicolons.

charts.summary.records.note: TalkBack's summary of a chart, its last part: the record days its stars mark in the last 90 days, in the platform's list (records on 3 Oct and 12 Oct).

charts.summary.thisweek.note: TalkBack's summary of a weekly chart: this game week's amount (this week 12 minutes).

charts.weekof.note: A game week in a chart's values, named by its first day: Week of 12 Oct. {date} is the platform's date.

coach.chronicle.label.note: Caps over the coach's weekly story, and the share card's line under its title.

coach.chronicle.legendary.note: Caps over the monthly edition of the coach's story, which names each family's next colour. Legendary is a rarity colour's name.

coach.chronicle.open.note: Button: opens the coach's weekly story.

coach.chronicles.note: Section label over the coach's weekly stories kept on the phone.

coach.consent.allow.note: Button: gives the consent and turns the coach on.

coach.consent.memory.text: the tone you picked, a few facts the coach remembers on this phone, and its last lines
coach.consent.memory.note: List item after "this phone sends Google:".

coach.consent.moves.text: the move you just did, the count you typed, what the set asked, and your record with how long it stood
coach.consent.moves.note: List item after "this phone sends Google:".

coach.consent.never.android.text: It does not send your name, your account, quest names or quest text, or any health data: no heart rate, no Health Connect data, no pain settings, no felt-unwell stops.

coach.consent.never.ios.text: It does not send your name, your account, quest names or quest text, or any health data: no heart rate, no Apple Health data, no pain settings, no felt-unwell stops.
coach.consent.never.ios.note: Legal text (the privacy disclosure): translate exactly.

coach.consent.notnow.note: Button: declines the consent (the coach can still be turned on from its page).

coach.consent.processor.text: Google processes it for Pluxia GmbH under the Google Cloud terms, in the EU. You can turn the coach off at any time on the Coach screen.

coach.consent.sends.text: When the coach speaks, this phone sends Google:
coach.consent.sends.note: Followed by a list of what is sent.

coach.consent.steps.text: each move group's colour and step, and what the next step still asks
coach.consent.steps.note: List item after "this phone sends Google:".

coach.consent.streak.text: your streak, and whether a pump paid a weekly goal
coach.consent.streak.note: List item after "this phone sends Google:".

coach.consent.title.note: The title of the consent window before the coach's first call.

coach.consent.week.text: once a week, your week's counts: moves, records, steps and the families you trained
coach.consent.week.note: List item after "this phone sends Google:".

coach.cost.note: Label: the mean cost of a line in US dollars.

coach.details.note: Section header: counts and costs of the coach's lines.

coach.failed.note: Label: how many requests to the AI service failed.

coach.heard.note: Label: how many talks the coach spoke after sets.

coach.keep.title.note: Title of the one moment after the free taste: keep the coach, Burnish, with Pro.

coach.lines.note: Section label on the coach's page over today's talks, each with Report.

coach.lines.none.note: On the coach's page when no talk was heard today.

coach.name.note: The coach's name: an enchanted suit of armour that talks after your sets. A name, never translated.

coach.noline.failed.note: A set the coach did not talk about because the request to the AI service failed.

coach.noline.rule.text: No talk: our filter blocked the reply

coach.pro.text: The coach is part of QuestPump Pro.

coach.reason.offensive.note: A reason to report a coach line.

coach.reason.other.note: A reason to report a coach line.

coach.reason.unsafe.note: A reason to report a coach line.

coach.reason.wrong.note: A reason to report a coach talk or Chronicle: wrong about the moves or the numbers.

coach.refused.note: Label: how many lines the app refused for breaking its rules.

coach.report.note: Button on the watch's card: reports a coach talk as wrong (the phone's is the round flag, coach.report.label).

coach.report.label.note: Spoken label of the flag button on a coach talk or Chronicle.

coach.report.note.text: Sends Pluxia these words, your reason and the name of the AI model. Nothing else.

coach.sends.row.note: A row on the coach's page and the title of the window it opens: what the coach sends to Google Gemini.

plural.other: Without Pro, Burnish talks after your first {count} big sets (records and unlocks) and writes your first Chronicle.

coach.taste.note: On the coach's page without Pro, while the free taste lasts. Burnish is the coach's name; QuestPump Pro the paid subscription.

coach.taste.used.note: On the coach's page without Pro once the free taste was heard.

coach.title.note: Section header, row and page title: the Pro coach, which speaks one short line before each pump.

coach.today.count.note: Under the coach's switch with Pro: the coach's calls this game day (every call counts, a talk's and a Chronicle's) of the day's limit, never more than the limit (Lines today: 3 of 45).

coach.today.last.text: That was today's last line. The next one comes after {time}.
coach.today.last.note: On the coach's page once the day's lines are used: {time} is when the next game day starts, 4:00 AM in the phone's time format.

coach.tone.note: Section label over the coach's tone choices.

coach.tone.drill.note: A tone for the coach: firm and clipped, never urging past a stop.

coach.tone.dry.note: A tone for the coach: understated humour.

coach.tone.warm.note: A tone for the coach: a kind mentor.

coach.turnon.note: Button: opens the consent before the coach's first line.

coach.unavailable.text: The coach is not part of this version of the app.

common.back.note: Button during a move: takes the move back to the screen before its Start, as if Start was never pressed; nothing is saved.

common.cancel.note: Button: closes a dialog or a sheet and changes nothing.

common.close.note: Button: closes a sheet or a dialog; on a pump's Ready view on the phones and the computer, the bar's way out of a pump that banks nothing, which ends the pump as End the pump here did (an expedition's round on Android: the expedition) (the game's Close: "Ends this pump").

common.move.fallback.note: A move's name when the app's move list lacks it (a newer game build): Move 212.

common.moves.count.note: A number of moves (a move is one exercise of a pump): a muscle's moves this week, a week's or a day's moves in a chart.

common.seconds.short.note: A count of seconds with the short unit (a hold's record, a timed move): 30 s. Both forms read the same in English; the plural keeps Android's lint from asking for one.

common.seepro.note: Button: opens the offer of QuestPump Pro, the paid subscription. Pro is a product name.

common.tryagain.note: Button: tries the same thing once more.

correct.window.done.note: After Save: the set now reads {value} (15 reps, 0:30, 12 kg × 12, Okay) on this device; the game takes it at its next load. Done (the primary) closes the window.

correct.window.done.none.note: After Save, in correct.window.done's place, where the set as the fold reads it after the write has no number (slice 44's review, 2026-10-18; the phones' since 2026-10-19): a count corrected to 0, which reads as typing 0 does, done without a count, or a counted set's Not counted, whose words would read wrong after Corrected to. The game's done view says the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.doneNone). Done (the primary) closes the window.

correct.window.elsewhere.note: Over Save in one set's correction on the device the set came from (2026-10-19, the program's double-check), where another device's correction of it won and this device's own reading still differs (the entry's ownSide: the engine's ns.OwnSide): {value} the set as it reads now (15 reps), at which the control stands and Save is ready; Save writes the same value again as this device's own correction, so the step rules ask again here. The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.elsewhere).

correct.window.elsewhere.none.text: Corrected to no count on another device.
correct.window.elsewhere.none.note: In correct.window.elsewhere's place (2026-10-19, the program's double-check), where the set as it reads now has no number (a count corrected to 0, done without a count, or a counted set's Not counted), whose words would read wrong after Corrected to, as correct.window.done.none says it; Save is ready at that value and writes it again as this device's own correction. The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.elsewhereNone).

correct.window.empty.text: No set of the last {days} days to correct.

plural.one: No set of the last day to correct.
plural.other: No set of the last {days} days to correct.

correct.window.empty.note: In the list's place when the move has no set the window can list: none in the last {days} game days (correct_days), or none the game still holds. Clear this record follows while the move has a record.

correct.window.gone.text: That set can no longer be corrected.
correct.window.gone.note: Back on the list after Save, when the set left the window meanwhile (its game days ran out, a clear row came, or the game no longer holds it): nothing changed.

correct.window.mastered.lost.text: Step {step} of {ladder} is no longer Mastered.
correct.window.mastered.lost.note: Under Corrected to … and its step lines (2026-10-19): the correction took back the Mastered seal of step {step} of {ladder} (its tree's name: Core), whose moves no longer all reached their top. The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.mastered.lost).

correct.window.mastered.won.note: correct.window.mastered.lost where the correction made every move of step {step} of {ladder} reach its top: the step is Mastered now. The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.mastered.won).

correct.window.other.note: Quiet button under Save in a set's correction: back to the list of sets, nothing changed.

correct.window.saved.note: Over the correction of one set saved with a number: what was saved and when. {value} is the set as saved (22 reps, 0:41, 11 kg × 16), {date} its game day's date and its time as the platform writes them (Tue 14 Oct, 18:04). A set saved with no number takes correct.window.saved.none, a pose's answer correct.window.saved.pose.

correct.window.saved.none.note: Over the correction of a set saved with no number (slice 44's review, 2026-10-18): Done without a count (saved with an empty box, or corrected to 0), Could not do one or Could not hold it (a stored 0), or a counted set's Not counted (pump.count.none), whose words would read wrong after You saved. {date} as in correct.window.saved.

correct.window.saved.pose.note: Over the correction of a pose's answer: {answer} is the answer saved to How close to the goal pose? (Perfect, Good, Okay, Not yet), {date} as in correct.window.saved.

correct.window.sets.text: Your sets of the last {days} days

plural.one: Your sets of the last day
plural.other: Your sets of the last {days} days

correct.window.sets.note: SectionLabel over the sets the window lists: {days} is contract/library.json's correct_days (14), the game days back a set can be corrected.

correct.window.step.back.note: Under Corrected to … (2026-10-19, the program's double-check): the correction took back a climb its set made, a stretch check's lift among them, and {ladder} (its tree's name: Push-ups) now stands at step {step} (the one scale, 1-14). One line for each ladder that moved (the engine's correct_rows `changes.rungs`, ns.CorrectionRows' third return). The game's done view and its /qp undo line say the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.step.back).

correct.window.step.game.text: Your step stays: this set came from the game, so correct it there to change your step.
correct.window.step.game.note: Under Corrected to … where the step rules asked again with the new value would change a step, but the set came from the game (a game pump or a catch-up): only the game asks them again for its own sets.

correct.window.step.later.text: Your step stays: this ladder has moved on since that set.
correct.window.step.later.note: Under Corrected to … where the step rules asked again would change a step the set made, but the ladder changed step again after it (a later climb, a step down, a step mastered): the later change stands, and so does the step.

correct.window.step.up.note: correct.window.step.back where the correction made the ladder climb (a set corrected up to its top on the days it needs): {ladder} now stands at step {step}. The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua correct.step.up).

correct.window.title.note: Heading of the correction window (slice 44): {move} is the move's name (Wall push-up).

crash.always.note: Button: sends this crash report and turns on the Menu's Send crash reports, so later ones go without asking.

crash.body.text: Send us the crash report so we can fix it? It holds what the app was doing and your phone's model and system version. It never holds your pumps, your health data or your name.
crash.body.note: Legal text (the privacy disclosure): translate exactly. The phones' crash window: what the report holds and never holds.

crash.carrier.text: Google Firebase Crashlytics carries it to us and keeps it for 90 days.
crash.carrier.note: The phones' crash window, under the body: who carries the report and how long it is kept. Google Firebase Crashlytics is a product name.

crash.send.note: Button: sends the waiting crash report this once.

crash.sent.text: Thanks! The report is on its way.
crash.sent.note: Shown after Send or Always send.

crash.skip.note: Button: deletes the waiting crash report; nothing is sent.

crash.title.note: Title of the window that asks, at the first start after a crash, whether to send the crash report.

demo.computer.note: The demo helper's computer, named where a paired helper's computer stands: Hero's source chip (Demo computer · 1 day ago), the Menu's Helper page and Pump's status chip (Connected to Demo computer), while the demo helper plays.

desk.addon.add.note: The action of the welcome's Game row, the button of Pump home's card and This computer's addon row while World of Warcraft is on this computer without the QuestPump addon: QuestPump puts the addon into the game folder itself (it downloads the release the addon stores get and checks it). The apps' copy never names the game (contract/copy/words.json, blizzard).

desk.addon.added.note: The addon line once QuestPump added the addon while the game ran: the game loads it at its next start. Gone once that game is closed.

desk.addon.addfailed.note: The addon line when adding the addon failed. {error} is the reason in the system's or QuestPump's words (no download, a check that failed, a folder it may not write into). The button offers it again.

desk.addon.adding.note: The addon line while QuestPump downloads the addon and puts it into the game folder.

desk.addon.current.note: This computer's addon line when no newer addon is out. {version} is the version in the game folder.

desk.addon.failed.note: This computer's addon line when an update of the addon failed; the old addon stays in the game. {error} is the reason in the system's or QuestPump's words. QuestPump tries again at its next check of the release.

desk.addon.missing.text: QuestPump is not in the game yet
desk.addon.missing.note: The line of the welcome's Game row, the heading of Pump home's card and This computer's addon line while World of Warcraft is on this computer without the QuestPump addon.

desk.addon.newer.note: This computer's addon line, beside Update now, when a newer addon is out for an install QuestPump does not keep up to date (another updater's or a hand install). {version} is the version in the game folder, {new} the newer one.

desk.addon.ready.text: {version} · {new} goes in once the game is closed
desk.addon.ready.note: This computer's addon line when a newer addon is downloaded and waits: QuestPump puts it into the game folder once the game is closed and no pump runs on this computer. {version} is the version in the game folder, {new} the newer one.

desk.addon.row.note: This computer's row label for the QuestPump addon in the game folder: its version and whether it is up to date.

desk.addon.update.note: This computer's addon row action while a newer QuestPump addon is out for an install another updater or a hand install made: one click, and QuestPump updates it and keeps it up to date from then on.

desk.addon.updating.note: This computer's addon line while QuestPump downloads a newer addon or puts it into the game folder.

desk.book.share.copied.note: Under the Share window's buttons once the card's picture is on the clipboard.

desk.book.share.copy.failed.text: The card could not be copied.
desk.book.share.copy.failed.note: Under the Share window's buttons when the system refused the clipboard.

desk.book.share.save.failed.text: The card could not be saved.
desk.book.share.save.failed.note: Under the Share window's buttons when the file could not be written (a folder without room or rights).

desk.book.share.saved.note: Under the Share window's buttons once the card's file is written where the player picked.

desk.book.share.video.copied.text: Video copied. Paste it into a chat.
desk.book.share.video.copied.note: Under the Share window's buttons once the reel is on the clipboard as a file.

desk.book.share.video.copy.failed.text: The video could not be copied.
desk.book.share.video.copy.failed.note: Under the Share window's buttons when the reel could not be put on the clipboard.

desk.book.share.video.save.failed.text: The video could not be saved.
desk.book.share.video.save.failed.note: Under the Share window's buttons when the reel's file could not be written.

desk.book.share.video.saved.note: Under the Share window's buttons once the reel's file is written where the player picked.

desk.card.later.note: The match-over card's quiet button: the card goes, and the offer stays on Pump home and in the tray for an hour; a phone or a watch that had its notice takes it back (slice 48's double-check).

desk.crash.body.text: Send us the crash report so we can fix it? It holds what QuestPump was doing and your system's version. It never holds your name or anything from your game. You can read all of it below.
desk.crash.body.note: The desktop app's crash page: what the report holds and never holds.

desk.crash.hide.note: Button: hides the report's text again.

desk.crash.kept.text: Not sent yet. It goes by itself when you are online.
desk.crash.kept.note: After Send while the computer is offline: the report waits on the computer and goes later.

desk.crash.refused.text: This report could not be sent.
desk.crash.refused.note: After Send when questpump.com refused the report (it is dropped).

desk.crash.show.note: Button: shows the report's text exactly as it would go.

desk.done.menubar.text: QuestPump waits in the menu bar.
desk.done.menubar.note: On the first start's last page on a Mac, and once under the note that QuestPump found the player's progress: where QuestPump's icon is.

desk.done.title.note: The heading of the first start's last page on the computer.

desk.done.tray.text: QuestPump waits in the tray: pin it from the ^.
desk.done.tray.note: On the first start's last page on Windows, and once under the note that QuestPump found the player's progress: where QuestPump's icon is. ^ is the arrow that shows the hidden icons.

desk.feedback.capture.live.note: Beside the screen reading's code (live) among the details: what the code means.

desk.feedback.capture.nogame.note: Beside the screen reading's code (nogame) among the details: what the code means.

desk.feedback.capture.nostrip.text: the game runs, but QuestPump's squares are not seen
desk.feedback.capture.nostrip.note: Beside the screen reading's code (nostrip) among the details: what the code means.

desk.feedback.capture.permission.note: Beside the screen reading's code (permission) among the details: what the code means.

desk.feedback.capture.stopped.note: Beside the screen reading's code (stopped) among the details: what the code means.

desk.feedback.diagnostics.note: A row in the Menu's QuestPump group, and a quiet button beside Pump home's and Hero's line when pumps on this computer could not start: copies QuestPump's version, its status and the end of its log, to paste into a message when the player asks for help.

desk.feedback.diagnostics.copied.note: The Copy a report for help row's line (on Pump home and Hero the button's words) once the text is on the clipboard, for three seconds.

desk.feedback.diagnostics.failed.note: The Copy a report for help row's line (on Pump home and Hero the button's words) when the clipboard refused the text, for three seconds.

desk.feedback.error.text: Not sent: QuestPump did not answer. Your text is still in the box. Quit QuestPump, open it again and try again.
desk.feedback.error.note: Under Send when QuestPump on this computer did not answer the page.

desk.feedback.fits.note: Under the text box when typing or pasting went past the limit. {max} is the limit.

desk.feedback.from.text: From QuestPump on this computer, version {version}
desk.feedback.from.note: Above the details: where the message comes from. {version} is QuestPump's version.

desk.feedback.note.later.text: Feedback not sent yet: QuestPump tries again every {minutes} minutes

plural.one: Feedback not sent yet: QuestPump tries again every minute
plural.other: Feedback not sent yet: QuestPump tries again every {minutes} minutes

desk.feedback.note.later.note: The tray menu's line and the page's while a message waits for the next try.

desk.feedback.note.lost.text: Feedback could not be sent at {time}
desk.feedback.note.lost.note: The tray menu's line and the page's when a message that could not be kept also could not go.

desk.feedback.note.lost.game.text: Feedback from the game could not be sent at {time}
desk.feedback.note.lost.game.note: The same for a message the game handed over.

desk.feedback.note.refused.note: The tray menu's line and the page's after a message was turned away.

desk.feedback.note.sent.note: The tray menu's line and the page's after a message went. {time} is the clock time, such as 14:02.

desk.feedback.note.soon.text: Feedback not sent yet: QuestPump tries again in a minute
desk.feedback.note.soon.note: The tray menu's line and the page's while a message waits for the next minute.

desk.feedback.note.ticked.text: Only the details below go with your words, and no name: the version and what the boxes say. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
desk.feedback.note.ticked.note: Under the tick while it is on.

desk.feedback.queued.text: Not sent yet. QuestPump keeps your message and sends it by itself as soon as it can.
desk.feedback.queued.note: Under Send when the message waits on this computer.

desk.feedback.section.note: The caps label over the Menu's last card: Send feedback and Copy a report for help. The app's name, never translated.

desk.feedback.system.note: A detail's label: the computer's system and its version.

desk.feedback.tick.note: A tick: the message also carries the system's version and the screen reading's state, shown under it.

desk.feedback.unsaved.text: Not sent: QuestPump could not save your message on this computer. Your text is still in the box.
desk.feedback.unsaved.note: Under Send when the message could neither go nor be kept.

desk.figures.bundled.note: The films come with this build.

desk.figures.downloading.text: Downloading, {percent}% done: each move shows its still until then
desk.figures.downloading.note: The films are on their way; a move shows its key pose until they are here.

desk.figures.failed.text: Could not download ({error}): each move shows its still, and QuestPump tries again later
desk.figures.failed.note: The films' download failed; {error} is the system's or the server's reason, in English.

desk.figures.kept.note: The films were downloaded once and are kept on this computer.

desk.figures.missing.text: Not in this build: each move shows its still
desk.figures.missing.note: A build without the films and without a release feed to fetch them from (a development build).

desk.figures.row.note: A status line's label on This computer: the move figures' films inside QuestPump on this computer (the game folder's Exercise animations are the addon's own).

desk.hero.source.game.note: Hero's source chip on the computer when the sheet is the game's: {ago} is how long ago the game folded it, in the system's short words (5 min. ago). A click opens This computer.

desk.home.failed.text: Pumps on this computer could not start. Restart QuestPump, or send feedback from the Menu.
desk.home.failed.note: At the foot of Pump home, under Hero's Start a pump and on the first start's place step, when QuestPump on this computer could not read the player's rows to start its pumps (it tries again at its next start after a reset). Beside it on Pump home and Hero the Menu's Copy a report for help; on the place step Continue goes on to the games.

desk.home.fix.firewall.text: Your phone cannot reach this PC
desk.home.fix.firewall.note: Pump home's status chip on Windows while a phone is paired and Windows Firewall keeps it out (2026-10-27: the chip shows only while something needs fixing); a click opens Phones, which offers the one-time step.

desk.home.fix.save.text: Your progress could not be saved
desk.home.fix.save.note: Pump home's status chip while QuestPump could not save the progress into the game folder (it tries again): the chip shows only while something needs fixing (2026-10-27), and a click opens This computer, whose progress line says why.

desk.home.games.note: The caps label over Pump home's recent games on the computer (2026-10-27) while its switch says This week (desk.home.games.span.week; Moves all time, desk.home.games.all, under All time), a row of small tiles that scrolls sideways (2026-10-28): every game running now first (marked Playing), then every game with a move this week or played in the last week, each with its moves done this game week (from Monday's turn) as a number beside its icon, the most first. World of Warcraft's are the moves done in its quest pumps; another game's the moves done in the pumps started from its match offers. Nothing shows before the first game played.

desk.home.games.all.note: The caps label over Pump home's recent games on the computer while its switch says All time (2026-10-28; Moves this week, desk.home.games, under This week): every game running now first, then every game with a move, each with its moves done in all as a number beside its icon, the most first.

desk.home.games.count.note: What a screen reader hears after a recent game's name on Pump home (2026-10-27) under This week: its moves done this game week, the number its tile shows beside its icon.

desk.home.games.count.all.note: What a screen reader hears after a recent game's name on Pump home under All time (2026-10-28): its moves done in all, the number its tile shows beside its icon.

desk.home.games.next.note: Name of the small round button with a chevron at the right end of Pump home's recent games on the computer (2026-10-28), read by a screen reader: it scrolls the row on to the games with fewer moves this week. It shows only while more games lie that way.

desk.home.games.previous.note: Name of the small round button with a chevron at the left end of Pump home's recent games on the computer (2026-10-28), read by a screen reader: it scrolls the row back to the games with more moves this week. It shows only while more games lie that way.

desk.home.games.span.note: Name of the small This week | All time switch at the right of Pump home's recent games' label on the computer (2026-10-28), read by a screen reader: what the games' numbers count.

desk.home.games.span.all.note: The switch's second segment over Pump home's recent games on the computer (2026-10-28): each game's moves done in all, the label then Moves all time. The player's choice is kept on this computer.

desk.home.games.span.week.note: The switch's first segment over Pump home's recent games on the computer (2026-10-28), the default: each game's moves done this game week (from Monday's turn), the label then Moves this week.

desk.home.later.note: The quiet button of Pump home's card that pairs a phone and of the one that offers the addon: the card goes for a week, and the next card offers its part meanwhile.

desk.home.pain.failed.text: Your sore joints were not saved: press Save to try again.
desk.home.pain.failed.note: In the check-in's joints window when the flags could not be written (QuestPump was still reading the player's rows): the switches stay as the player set them.

desk.home.pair.title.note: The heading of Pump home's card that pairs a phone, shown while no phone is paired (returning players too) until its Not now puts it away for a week; one card offers the next part at a time, this one first.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.audio.note: A row on the Acknowledgements on the computer: the name of the code that plays the app's sounds and voice, which opens its licence notice. A name, never translated.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.code.note: Caps label on the Acknowledgements on the computer, over the code the app builds in.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.crates.note: A row on the Acknowledgements on the computer: the libraries of the Rust language the app is built from, which opens their licence texts.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.crates.meta.note: Under the Rust crates row on the Acknowledgements on the computer: the licences they come under. MIT and Apache 2.0 are licence names.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.engine.note: A row on the Acknowledgements on the computer: the names of the code the app's engine runs on, which opens their licence notice. Names, never translated.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.licence.mit.note: A licence's name under a row on the Acknowledgements on the computer.

desk.menu.acknowledgements.licence.mpl.note: A licence's name under a row on the Acknowledgements on the computer.

desk.menu.backup.kept.note: After a backup file came in whose setup differs: the computer kept its own (where you train and the equipment).

desk.menu.backup.notkept.text: The file did not all go in. Restore from it again.
desk.menu.backup.notkept.note: After a backup file was opened but this computer could not save every pump in it (a full or locked disk): restoring the same file again takes in the rest.

desk.menu.backup.place.note: After a backup file from this computer came in with nothing new but its setup (where you train and the equipment).

desk.menu.backup.pumpon.text: A pump started, so the file did not go in. Restore from it again after the pump.
desk.menu.backup.pumpon.note: After a backup file was picked while a pump started on this computer: nothing from it was taken in.

desk.menu.computer.access.acl.text: Windows does not let QuestPump write into your game folder, where it keeps your progress for the game. Allow it once, and Windows asks for an administrator.
desk.menu.computer.access.acl.note: The card's text when the folder's permissions refuse QuestPump.

desk.menu.computer.access.allow.text: Allow writing to the game folder
desk.menu.computer.access.allow.note: The card's button: Windows asks for an administrator once.

desk.menu.computer.access.cfa.text: Windows Security's Controlled folder access blocks QuestPump. Open Windows Security, then Virus & threat protection, Ransomware protection, and Allow an app through Controlled folder access, and add this program: {program}. Then quit QuestPump and open it again.
desk.menu.computer.access.cfa.note: The card's text when Controlled folder access blocks QuestPump. {program} is QuestPump's own program file, its full path. The setting names are Windows Security's own.

desk.menu.computer.access.failed.text: That did not work ({error}). Press the button again, or see QuestPump's log.
desk.menu.computer.access.failed.note: Under the folder card's button when the step failed. {error} is Windows' own reason, in English.

desk.menu.computer.access.title.note: A card's heading on Windows when Windows does not let QuestPump write into the game folder.

desk.menu.computer.admin.declined.text: Windows did not get an administrator's yes: press the button again when you are ready.
desk.menu.computer.admin.declined.note: Under a card's button when the administrator prompt was closed or refused.

desk.menu.computer.admin.waiting.note: Under a card's button while Windows asks for an administrator.

desk.menu.computer.autostart.note: A switch: QuestPump starts when the player logs in to this computer.

desk.menu.computer.folder.note: A status line's label: the game's AddOns folder QuestPump uses.

desk.menu.computer.folder.change.note: The button that opens the system's folder picker.

desk.menu.computer.folder.labelled.note: The folder line: {path} is the folder, {label} the game's version found there, such as _classic_beta_ 1.60.1.

desk.menu.computer.folder.noaddons.text: {path} holds no AddOns folder of the game: choose the game's own folder.
desk.menu.computer.folder.noaddons.note: Under the folder line when the picked folder is no game folder. {path} is the folder picked.

desk.menu.computer.folder.none.note: The folder line when QuestPump found no game folder on this computer (a game without QuestPump shows its own folder instead). Neutral, never a fault: a player without the game needs nothing here. Change… is the button beside it.

desk.menu.computer.folder.noquestpump.text: {path} has no QuestPump yet: get the addon at questpump.com, and QuestPump follows that folder once it is there.
desk.menu.computer.folder.noquestpump.note: Under the folder line when the player picked a game folder without the QuestPump addon in it: QuestPump writes nothing there until the addon is in it. {path} is the AddOns folder picked. questpump.com is the addon's page (a web address is allowed outside the game).

desk.menu.computer.folder.pick.note: The title of the system's folder picker that Change… opens.

desk.menu.computer.folder.running.text: The game running now uses {path}: close it to choose another folder.
desk.menu.computer.folder.running.note: Under the folder line when the player picked a folder while the game runs. {path} is the running game's folder.

desk.menu.computer.folder.unknown.note: The folder line before any folder was found.

desk.menu.computer.game.note: A status line's label: the World of Warcraft QuestPump follows.

desk.menu.computer.game.none.note: The game line while no World of Warcraft runs.

desk.menu.computer.game.running.note: The game line while World of Warcraft runs. {label} is the install's name as the game folder line shows it, such as wow_classic_beta 1.60.1.

desk.menu.computer.game.running.plain.note: The game line while World of Warcraft runs from an install that names itself nowhere QuestPump reads.

desk.menu.computer.mirror.note: A status line's label: the copy of the player's progress QuestPump keeps in the game folder.

desk.menu.computer.mirror.failed.text: Could not be saved into the game folder ({error}); QuestPump tries again
desk.menu.computer.mirror.failed.note: The progress line when the write failed. {error} is the system's reason, in English.

desk.menu.computer.mirror.here.note: The progress line while no game folder with QuestPump is known: the player's progress stays in QuestPump on this computer, and the game gets it once QuestPump finds its folder.

desk.menu.computer.mirror.kept.text: Kept safe for the game at {time}
desk.menu.computer.mirror.kept.note: The progress line once it was written. {time} is the clock time, such as 14:02.

desk.menu.computer.mirror.unfound.text: Could not be saved into the game folder (it cannot be found); QuestPump tries again
desk.menu.computer.mirror.unfound.note: The progress line when the game folder cannot be found.

desk.menu.computer.mirror.waiting.note: The progress line before QuestPump knows the game folder.

desk.menu.computer.move.open.note: The card's button: the Finder shows the Applications folder.

desk.menu.computer.move.title.note: A card's heading on a Mac while QuestPump runs from its download (the disk image).

desk.menu.computer.pack.note: A status line's label: the move figures' download beside QuestPump in the game folder.

desk.menu.computer.pack.installed.note: The animations line when the figures are there and match QuestPump.

desk.menu.computer.pack.missing.text: Missing: install QuestPump again, its download brings them

desk.menu.computer.pack.notseen.note: The animations line before a game folder was found.

desk.menu.computer.screen.failed.windows.text: QuestPump could not start ({error}). See its log, then quit QuestPump from its icon beside the clock and open it again.

desk.menu.computer.screen.how.note: The card's one paragraph, the privacy words before macOS's Screen Recording question.

desk.menu.computer.screen.newer.text: QuestPump in the game is newer than QuestPump on this computer: close the game so this app can update itself, or download the new one from questpump.com/helper
desk.menu.computer.screen.newer.note: The screen reading line when the addon in the game is a newer version.

desk.menu.computer.screen.noaddon.text: QuestPump is not installed in the game running now: no squares can show there
desk.menu.computer.screen.noaddon.note: The screen reading line when the running World of Warcraft (named on the Game line above it) has no QuestPump.

desk.menu.computer.screen.notseen.note: The screen reading line before the game ever showed its squares.

desk.menu.computer.screen.off.text: Off until needed: QuestPump asks to see the game once it finds the game with QuestPump and you pair a phone or turn on a strap or a walking pad
desk.menu.computer.screen.off.note: The screen reading line while the permission is missing and nothing needs it yet: no World of Warcraft with QuestPump is known on this computer, or no phone, watch, strap or walking pad needs it.

desk.menu.computer.screen.older.text: QuestPump in the game is older than QuestPump on this computer: update QuestPump in the game, then type /reload there
desk.menu.computer.screen.older.note: The screen reading line when the addon in the game is an older version.

desk.menu.computer.screen.out.text: Not in view right now (a movie, a loading screen, the menu)
desk.menu.computer.screen.out.note: The screen reading line while the squares are out of sight.

desk.menu.computer.screen.out.hdr.text: Not in view right now (a movie, a loading screen, the menu). Your display uses HDR: if this stays while you play, turn HDR off for the game
desk.menu.computer.screen.out.hdr.note: The screen reading line while the squares are out of sight on an HDR display.

desk.menu.computer.screen.ping.text: {line} · test signal from the game at {time}
desk.menu.computer.screen.ping.note: After the screen reading line when the game sent /qp ping. {line} is the line itself, {time} the clock time, such as 14:02.

desk.menu.computer.screen.reading.note: The screen reading line while the squares are read.

desk.menu.computer.screen.restart.note: The button that quits QuestPump and opens it again, so the permission applies.

desk.menu.computer.screen.restart.failed.text: QuestPump could not restart itself: quit QuestPump from the menu bar, then open it again.
desk.menu.computer.screen.restart.failed.note: Under the restart button when QuestPump could not start itself again.

desk.menu.computer.screen.restarting.note: The restart button's words once pressed.

desk.menu.computer.screen.settings.note: The card's button once macOS asked: it opens System Settings at Screen Recording.

desk.menu.computer.screen.stopped.text: The screen reading stopped: QuestPump tries again by itself; if this stays, quit QuestPump from the menu bar, then open it again
desk.menu.computer.screen.stopped.note: The screen reading line on a Mac when it stopped.

desk.menu.computer.screen.stopped.window.text: The screen reading stopped: start the game again, or quit QuestPump from its icon beside the clock, then open it again
desk.menu.computer.screen.stopped.window.note: The screen reading line on Windows when it stopped.

desk.menu.computer.screen.title.note: A card's heading on a Mac while the Screen Recording permission is missing and a phone is paired or a strap or a walking pad is on.

desk.menu.computer.screen.unseen.text: Not seen for a minute: once you are in the game world, check that QuestPump is turned on in the game's AddOns list
desk.menu.computer.screen.unseen.note: The screen reading line when the squares have been out of sight for a minute.

desk.menu.computer.screen.waiting.text: Waiting for the game to show it
desk.menu.computer.screen.waiting.note: The screen reading line from the game's start until its squares show.

desk.menu.computer.size.note: A row's label on This computer: how big everything in the window shows, as a percentage of its default size, with a minus and a plus beside it. Also the name a screen reader hears for that value.

desk.menu.computer.size.larger.note: The name a screen reader hears for Size's plus button: one step larger.

desk.menu.computer.size.smaller.note: The name a screen reader hears for Size's minus button: one step smaller.

desk.menu.computer.size.value.note: Size's value between its minus and plus: the window's size as a percentage of its default, 80 to 200 (100 is the default). A screen reader reads it as the value.

desk.menu.computer.title.note: A row in the Menu and the title of its page: the game QuestPump reads on this computer, its screen reading, the player's progress kept for the game, the game folder and starting with the computer.

desk.menu.computer.version.note: A status line's label: QuestPump's version on this computer.

desk.menu.computer.version.current.note: The version line after a check found none.

desk.menu.computer.version.development.text: {version} (a development build: it does not update itself)
desk.menu.computer.version.development.note: The version line of a build made by hand.

desk.menu.computer.version.failed.note: The version line when the check failed.

desk.menu.computer.version.installing.note: The version line while an update installs.

desk.menu.computer.version.notinstalled.text: {version} · the update could not be installed
desk.menu.computer.version.notinstalled.note: The version line when an update did not install.

desk.menu.computer.version.ready.held.text: {version} · {new} is ready: it installs once the game is closed
desk.menu.computer.version.ready.held.note: The version line when an update was downloaded and something besides this window holds it: the game runs, a pump runs or holds the window, a match's offer stands, a watched game runs or is in a match, or the addon's own update is under way; the game is the usual one, so the line names it. It installs by itself once nothing holds it and the window is closed. {version} is QuestPump's version, {new} the update's.

desk.menu.computer.version.ready.now.note: The version line when an update was downloaded and only this window keeps it from installing: Restart to update beside it installs it now. {version} is QuestPump's version, {new} the update's.

desk.menu.computer.version.restart.note: This computer's version row action while an update is ready and only this window keeps it from installing: QuestPump closes, installs the update and opens again on this page.

desk.menu.computer.version.unmoved.text: {version} (it updates itself once it runs from Applications)
desk.menu.computer.version.unmoved.note: The version line on a Mac while QuestPump runs from its download. {version} is QuestPump's version.

desk.menu.computer.version.unreplaceable.text: {version} · {new} is out: this account cannot replace QuestPump, so download it from questpump.com/helper
desk.menu.computer.version.unreplaceable.note: The version line on a Mac when this account may not replace the app. questpump.com/helper is the download page.

desk.menu.devices.pad.note: A switch: QuestPump reads a Bluetooth walking pad.

desk.menu.devices.pad.connected.note: The pad line while it is read. {name} is its name.

desk.menu.devices.pad.failed.text: The walking pad could not be read ({error}). Turn it on to try again.
desk.menu.devices.pad.failed.note: The pad line when it could not be read (its switch turned off). {error} is the reason, in English.

desk.menu.devices.pad.nodistance.text: This pad does not share the distance it counts, so QuestPump cannot keep it.
desk.menu.devices.pad.nodistance.note: The pad's second line when the pad sends no distance.

desk.menu.devices.pad.notfound.text: No walking pad found yet. Turn it on and close its own app, which holds the connection while it is open.
desk.menu.devices.pad.notfound.note: The pad line when none was found after a while, still looking.

desk.menu.devices.pad.off.text: Bluetooth is off: turn it on to read your walking pad.
desk.menu.devices.pad.off.note: The pad line while Bluetooth is off.

desk.menu.devices.pad.refused.text: Bluetooth is not allowed for QuestPump. Allow it in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Bluetooth, then turn the walking pad on again.
desk.menu.devices.pad.refused.note: The pad line on a Mac when Bluetooth was refused (its switch turned off).

desk.menu.devices.pad.refused.windows.text: Bluetooth is not allowed for QuestPump. Allow it in your privacy settings, then turn the walking pad on again.
desk.menu.devices.pad.refused.windows.note: The pad line on Windows when Bluetooth was refused.

desk.menu.devices.pad.stopped.note: The pad line while the belt stands. {name} is the pad's name.

desk.menu.devices.pad.unnamed.note: The walking pad's name when it gives none, inside its lines such as Reading {name}.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.both.text: Today: {kept} with your quests, {open} toward your next one.
desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.both.note: The pad's second line: both distances.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.game.text: No game is running, so no walk counts now.
desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.game.note: The pad's second line while no game runs.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.kept.note: The pad's second line: {kept} is the distance kept with today's quests, such as 1.2 km.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.keptgame.text: Today: {kept} with your quests. No game is running, so no walk counts now.
desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.keptgame.note: The pad's second line while no game runs, after a walk today.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.none.text: No walk with your quests yet today.
desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.none.note: The pad's second line before any distance today.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walk.open.note: The pad's second line: {open} is the distance walked since the last quest, in the player's units, such as 300 m.

desk.menu.devices.pad.walking.note: The pad line while the belt runs. {speed} is the belt's speed in the player's units, such as 3.2 km/h.

desk.menu.devices.starting.note: A device's line just after its switch was turned on.

desk.menu.devices.strap.note: A switch: QuestPump reads a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

desk.menu.devices.strap.connected.note: The strap line while it is read. {name} is its name.

desk.menu.devices.strap.failed.text: The strap could not be read ({error}). Turn it on to try again.
desk.menu.devices.strap.failed.note: The strap line when it could not be read (its switch turned off). {error} is the reason, in English.

desk.menu.devices.strap.notfound.text: No strap found yet. Wear it; on a WHOOP, turn on Broadcast Heart Rate in the WHOOP app.
desk.menu.devices.strap.notfound.note: The strap line when none was found after a while, still looking.

desk.menu.devices.strap.off.text: Bluetooth is off: turn it on to read your strap.
desk.menu.devices.strap.off.note: The strap line while Bluetooth is off.

desk.menu.devices.strap.refused.text: Bluetooth is not allowed for QuestPump. Allow it in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Bluetooth, then turn the strap on again.
desk.menu.devices.strap.refused.note: The strap line on a Mac when Bluetooth was refused (its switch turned off).

desk.menu.devices.strap.refused.windows.text: Bluetooth is not allowed for QuestPump. Allow it in your privacy settings, then turn the strap on again.
desk.menu.devices.strap.refused.windows.note: The strap line on Windows when Bluetooth was refused.

desk.menu.devices.strap.unnamed.note: The strap's name when it gives none, inside its lines such as Reading {name}.

desk.menu.devices.title.note: A row in the Menu and the title of its page: a heart-rate strap and a walking pad over Bluetooth.

desk.menu.devices.waiting.text: Waiting for Bluetooth. If macOS asks, allow it; if this stays, quit and reopen QuestPump.
desk.menu.devices.waiting.note: A device's line on a Mac while Bluetooth is neither on nor off yet (its prompt is up).

desk.menu.devices.waiting.windows.text: Waiting for Bluetooth. Turn it on in Settings, Bluetooth & devices; QuestPump goes on by itself.
desk.menu.devices.waiting.windows.note: A device's line on Windows while Bluetooth is neither on nor off.

desk.menu.does.text: What QuestPump does on this computer
desk.menu.does.note: A row in the Menu's QuestPump group: what QuestPump watches, keeps, listens to and sends on this computer, and what it never does.

desk.menu.does.client.text: Whether a match runs, asked of {games} on this computer only.
desk.menu.does.client.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game asked on the loopback is on (slice 48: StarCraft II, Legends of Runeterra): {games} lists their names.

desk.menu.does.crash.text: A crash report, to questpump.com, after QuestPump crashed: by itself while Send crash reports is on, else only when you press Send.
desk.menu.does.crash.note: In What it sends: the crash reports (contract/crash-api.yaml).

desk.menu.does.data.note: A row on What QuestPump does on this computer, over the folder's path: the settings, the pumps and the body.

desk.menu.does.detect.text: Which programs run, to notice the games you play: those in Steam's game folders and the apps marked as games. A found game's name and its program are kept on this computer.
desk.menu.does.detect.note: On What QuestPump does on a Mac, while Notice games I play is on (each game found watched from the day it is found, slice 56) (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §6.1): the games noticed running, from the process list it already looks at, by Steam's game folders on the startup volume and the apps whose Info.plist marks them a game (the games category or Game Mode). Each found game keeps its name, its program's key (the app's path, which can hold the account's folder name) and when it was seen, in settings.json, and nothing leaves the computer. Windows shows desk.menu.does.detect.windows.

desk.menu.does.detect.windows.text: Which programs run, to notice the games you play: those Steam lists as its games, Windows' list of games, and the games Epic, Battle.net, Ubisoft Connect and GOG installed. A found game's name and its program are kept on this computer.
desk.menu.does.detect.windows.note: The same on Windows (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §6.1): Steam's game-process log, Windows' list of games, the installs Epic Games Launcher, the Battle.net Agent, Ubisoft Connect and GOG Galaxy record (contract/copy/words.json's blizzard rule excepts this key: it names a launcher whose records the detector reads). Each found game keeps its name, its program's key (its image name, or steam:<app id>) and when it was seen, in settings.json.

desk.menu.does.drops.text: From a game it takes only that a match began or ended. Your name, your score and the match itself are never kept.
desk.menu.does.drops.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game is on. "Never kept", since a game's log is looked through line by line (desk.menu.does.logs; slice 48's second fix round: "dropped unread" until then).

desk.menu.does.feedback.text: Your feedback, to questpump.com, only when you press Send.
desk.menu.does.feedback.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer.

desk.menu.does.file.text: A file a game reads to report its matches
desk.menu.does.file.note: A row on What QuestPump does on this computer, over the path of a file QuestPump wrote into a game's folder.

desk.menu.does.file.shared.text: A file a game shares with other apps, where QuestPump added its part. It stays when you turn the game off.
desk.menu.does.file.shared.note: A row on What QuestPump does on this computer, over the path of a file other apps keep too, to which QuestPump added only its own part (slice 48: Hearthstone's log.config, which the deck trackers share): it is never written whole or removed, by turning the game off or by uninstalling.

desk.menu.does.game.text: The game's window: QuestPump reads only the small squares the addon shows in its corner.
desk.menu.does.game.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer: the one thing it reads of the game.

desk.menu.does.games.text: The games QuestPump watches, to know when a match ends: {games}.
desk.menu.does.games.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer: {games} lists the names of the games it watches (slice 56: the named and found games not turned off (the Riot games too since 2026-10-28, until then once turned on), the programs the player added; Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, StarCraft II).

desk.menu.does.games.none.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while it watches no game but World of Warcraft (slice 56).

desk.menu.does.gsi.text: News of your games' matches, from this computer only (port {port}).
desk.menu.does.gsi.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game that reports its matches is on. {port} is a port number, written as it is (no digit grouping).

desk.menu.does.idle.text: How long since your last key, click or touch, never which one, to know how long you sat.
desk.menu.does.idle.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, under What it watches (slice 48's sitting clock, docs/computer-games.md §3): the system's idle time alone (macOS CGEventSourceSecondsSinceLastEventType, Windows GetLastInputInfo), never a key's or a click's content.

desk.menu.does.keeps.note: Caps label on What QuestPump does on this computer, over the folders and files with their paths.

desk.menu.does.lan.text: Your paired phone and watch, on your home network (port {port}). Each message is sealed with your pairing code.
desk.menu.does.lan.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer. {port} is a port number (8787), written as it is (no digit grouping).

desk.menu.does.listens.note: Caps label on What QuestPump does on this computer.

desk.menu.does.logs.text: The logs {games} write on this computer: QuestPump looks through them only for the lines that say a match began or ended, and keeps none of it.
desk.menu.does.logs.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game heard by its log is on (slice 48: MTG Arena, Hearthstone, Elite Dangerous; since 2026-10-28 Mechabellum; since 2026-10-29 Path of Exile, Warframe, Escape from Tarkov, Deadlock, Fortnite, Team Fortress 2, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, Fall Guys, Dead by Daylight, Hunt: Showdown 1896 and VALORANT): {games} lists their names. Each line is looked through for a match's start or end alone (MTG Arena's start and end, Hearthstone's game start, end and spectating lines, Elite Dangerous' MissionCompleted, Mechabellum's PushMatchStart and PushGameOver, Path of Exile's generated area, Warframe's mission start and end, Escape from Tarkov's GameStarted and UserMatchOver, Deadlock's lobby and game state, Fortnite's server welcome and lobby, Team Fortress 2's lobby and match end, NARAKA's battle start and end, Fall Guys' round start and show end, Dead by Daylight's trial start and end, Hunt's mission bag lines, VALORANT's game flow states and whether the last game mode was the Range) and MTG Arena's header line, and no line is kept (slice 48's second fix round; the privacy page's games section says the same).

desk.menu.does.mirror.note: A row on What QuestPump does on this computer, over the path of the folder it writes for the game to read at its next load.

desk.menu.does.never.text: It never sends a key or a click to a game and never reads or changes its memory. A game's live data is read only where the game publishes it for other apps.
desk.menu.does.never.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer (slice 48: iRacing's and Assetto Corsa Competizione's telemetry, and since 2026-10-28 Assetto Corsa's and Guild Wars 2's link, come through the shared memory each game publishes for other apps, opened read-only and closed at each look; since 2026-10-29 ELDEN RING's and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN's window is captured for their boss banners, which desk.menu.does.screen says on its own line: a picture of the window, never the game's memory). Not "never opens a game's process": on Windows the app asks the system for a running program's path with limited query rights (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, World of Warcraft's included), which reads none of its memory.

desk.menu.does.nothing.text: Nothing else leaves this computer: no account, no tracking and no ads.
desk.menu.does.nothing.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer.

desk.menu.does.removes.text: Turning a game off removes its file. Uninstalling QuestPump leaves its own folder with your progress: delete that folder to remove it too.
desk.menu.does.removes.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer.

desk.menu.does.saves.text: The files {games} save on this computer: QuestPump only notices when one is saved or removed, never opens it and keeps none of it.
desk.menu.does.saves.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game heard by the files it saves is on (2026-10-28: Slay the Spire 2, whose run history folder gets a new file at each run's end; since 2026-10-29 World of Warships, whose replays folder holds tempArenaInfo.json while a battle runs and gets a new replay at its end, and Rainbow Six Siege X, whose MatchReplay folder gets a folder each match and a round file each round; later that day PUBG, whose Demos folder gets a folder each match and its PUBG.replayinfo at the end, and Halo: The Master Chief Collection, Brawlhalla, rFactor 2, Le Mans Ultimate, osu!, Stardew Valley and Warcraft III, each of which saves a carnage report, a replay, a results file or a save at an end): QuestPump reads only the folders' listings for whether a file is there and the newest file's or folder's time, never a file, a file's name or the Steam id in a folder's path. {games} lists their names. "Runs" until 2026-10-29, when the games that save replays joined.

desk.menu.does.screen.text: The middle of the window {games} show on this computer, about four times a second while they run, to see when a boss falls: QuestPump keeps no picture and no word of it.
desk.menu.does.screen.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game heard by its boss banners is on (2026-10-29: ELDEN RING and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN, Windows alone): {games} lists their names. The band across the middle of the game's own window (38 % to 62 % of its height) is captured through Windows.Graphics.Capture at most four times a second while the game runs, tested for the gold banner a boss's death shows and read by Windows' own OCR for its words; every frame and every word stays in memory for that test alone, never saved, logged or sent (docs/computer-games.md §6.2).

desk.menu.does.sends.note: Caps label on What QuestPump does on this computer.

desk.menu.does.shared.text: The live data {games} publish on this computer for other apps, for when a race or a match is over.
desk.menu.does.shared.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a game heard by its documented shared memory is on (slice 48: iRacing, Assetto Corsa Competizione; 2026-10-28: Assetto Corsa, and Guild Wars 2's MumbleLink, read for its PvP matches alone, never the character's identity; 2026-10-29: Automobilista 2, its game, session and race states alone): {games} lists their names.

desk.menu.does.steam.text: Which programs run from the Steam folders of {games}, to know when each one closes, while Notice games I play is off.
desk.menu.does.steam.note: On What QuestPump does on a Mac, while Notice games I play is off and a Steam game is turned on (slice 48's second fix round, docs/computer-games.md §6.1): {games} lists those games' names. With noticing off QuestPump still reads Steam's manifests on the startup volume and tells each turned-on Steam game by the programs that run from its folder, and reads nothing else for the detector (games/detect.rs steam_records). Windows shows desk.menu.does.steam.windows.

desk.menu.does.steam.windows.text: Steam's own list of the games it runs, for {games}, to know when each one closes, while Notice games I play is off.
desk.menu.does.steam.windows.note: The same on Windows (slice 48's second fix round): with noticing off QuestPump still reads Steam's game-process log and its manifests to tell each turned-on Steam game, never Windows' list of games nor the other launchers' records (games/detect.rs steam_records). {games} lists those games' names.

desk.menu.does.title.note: The title of the page the Menu's row What QuestPump does on this computer opens: kept short for the page's title bar.

desk.menu.does.udp.text: The telemetry {games} send to this computer only, for when a race is over.
desk.menu.does.udp.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer, while a racing game heard by its UDP telemetry is on (slice 48: F1 25, Forza Motorsport): {games} lists their names.

desk.menu.does.updates.text: A look for updates and the move animations, from GitHub.
desk.menu.does.updates.note: On What QuestPump does on this computer: the updater and the figures' films come from the app's release page on GitHub.

desk.menu.does.usage.text: Counts of each day, to questpump.com, while Usage statistics is on: which features you used and how many pumps you did, without your name or any id.
desk.menu.does.usage.note: In What it sends: the anonymous counts (contract/telemetry-api.yaml), this computer's and the game's, one batch a game day with no id; Usage statistics is the Menu's switch (menu.usage).

desk.menu.does.watches.note: Caps label on What QuestPump does on this computer.

desk.menu.email.computer.note: The {device} of "Open your progress on this {device}" and "Sign out on this {device}?" in the desktop app.

desk.menu.heart.computer.text: QuestPump on this computer does three more things. It measures every move of a pump from your heart rate before the pump's first move. With a watch, it judges moves where your hands hold you up, like push-ups, on the {after} seconds after the set, since the watch reads poorly during them. And it learns how your heart rate moves while you just play, so after a while it may ask for less or more rise, to fit your heart.
