desk.menu.heart.computer.note: Under How it decides on the computer: the after-set window and the calibration per source. {after} is the seconds after the set (30; questpump-core verdict::AFTER_SET_S), never typed here.

desk.menu.heart.reads.line.text: Only your heart rate. It comes from your watch while you run a play session on it, or from a heart-rate strap you turn on under Devices.
desk.menu.heart.reads.line.note: On How the heart-rate check works on the computer, under What it reads. Devices is the Menu's page with the strap's switch.

desk.menu.heart.stays.line.text: Your heart rate stays on your own devices: this computer, the game on it, your phone and your watch. It moves only between them, sealed on the way. Pluxia GmbH never gets it, and the backup file and feedback you send leave it out.
desk.menu.heart.stays.line.note: Under Where it stays on the computer, as the privacy policy says it.

desk.menu.link.check.no.note: The other answer to desk.menu.link.check.title: the answer is thrown away and a new code shows.

desk.menu.link.check.title.text: Does your phone show this number?
desk.menu.link.check.title.note: Over a six-digit number on Link a device on the computer (and in a browser), where the code's place was, once a phone answered the request code and no email sign-in tells which account to join: the phone that let it in shows the same number (menu.linkdevice.check), and anyone else who saw the code and answered first would not, so the computer joins only on Yes, join (slice 60's link request, since 2026-11-01).

desk.menu.link.check.yes.note: The answer to desk.menu.link.check.title: the computer joins the progress of the phone that answered.

desk.menu.link.other.text: That phone has other progress. Scan this with a phone that has this email's progress.
desk.menu.link.other.note: Under the request code on the computer (and in a browser) after an email sign-in asked for the account's key: a phone answered with another account than the one this email holds, so the computer refused it and shows a new code (slice 60's link request, the security review of 2026-10-31).

desk.menu.link.request.text: Scan this with QuestPump on your phone

desk.menu.phones.address.note: Under the code: {name} is the computer's name, {host} its address on the home network.

desk.menu.phones.address.ble.text: {name} · {host}: your phone pairs by Bluetooth now, and on Wi-Fi once it can reach this PC (above)
desk.menu.phones.address.ble.note: Under the code on Windows while the firewall card shows and the Bluetooth link serves (ble on): the code shows beside the card, since a phone that cannot reach the PC on Wi-Fi pairs by Bluetooth (2026-10-17).

desk.menu.phones.address.firewall.text: {name} · {host}: pair once your phone can reach this PC (above)
desk.menu.phones.address.firewall.note: Under the firewall card on Windows while the Bluetooth link does not serve: the code shows once the rule lets the phone in (desk.menu.phones.address.ble while it serves).

desk.menu.phones.address.lan.text: {name}: the phone cannot reach QuestPump yet ({error}); it tries again each minute
desk.menu.phones.address.lan.note: When QuestPump could not open its network port. {error} is the system's reason, in English.

desk.menu.phones.address.lan.host.text: {name} · {host}: the phone cannot reach QuestPump yet ({error}); it tries again each minute
desk.menu.phones.address.lan.host.note: The same, with the computer's address.

desk.menu.phones.address.none.text: {name} · no home network found: connect to Wi-Fi or Ethernet
desk.menu.phones.address.none.note: Instead of the code when the computer is on no home network. {name} is the computer's name.

desk.menu.phones.address.unread.text: {name} · pairing waits until QuestPump starts again
desk.menu.phones.address.unread.note: Instead of the code when QuestPump could not open its saved keys at this start (the Mac's Keychain kept locked, or a build not signed as QuestPump's release while the release's keys are there): a code of this run would end at the next start, so none shows, no phone is answered, and the paired phone links again after the next start. {name} is the computer's name.

desk.menu.phones.another.note: A button once a phone is paired: it shows the code again.

desk.menu.phones.ble.ask.text: Waiting for Bluetooth. If macOS asks, allow it.

desk.menu.phones.ble.failed.text: The Bluetooth link could not start. Turn it off and on again to try once more.
desk.menu.phones.ble.failed.note: The Bluetooth row's line when the link never started (2026-10-17: the system's own error stays in helper.log, never on the page).

desk.menu.phones.ble.lost.text: The Bluetooth link stopped. Turn it off and on again to start it once more.
desk.menu.phones.ble.lost.note: The Bluetooth row's line when the link ran and then stopped on an error (2026-10-17; desk.menu.phones.ble.failed when it never started). The system's own error stays in helper.log.

desk.menu.phones.ble.none.text: This computer has no Bluetooth, so your phone follows the game on Wi-Fi alone.

desk.menu.phones.ble.noperipheral.text: The Bluetooth in this PC can't link phones, so your phone follows the game on Wi-Fi alone.

desk.menu.phones.ble.off.text: Bluetooth is off: turn it on so your phone can link by Bluetooth.

desk.menu.phones.ble.refused.text: Bluetooth is not allowed for QuestPump. Allow it in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Bluetooth, so your phone can link by Bluetooth.

desk.menu.phones.ble.refused.windows.text: Bluetooth is not allowed for QuestPump. Allow it in your privacy settings, so your phone can link by Bluetooth.

desk.menu.phones.ble.title.note: The Phones page's switch for linking phones by Bluetooth (slice 43).

desk.menu.phones.code.text: The pairing code for your phone
desk.menu.phones.code.note: The pairing code's QR (QrWell) named for VoiceOver and NVDA.

desk.menu.phones.firewall.allow.note: The card's button: Windows asks for an administrator once.

desk.menu.phones.firewall.another.text: Windows made the rule, and another one still blocks QuestPump. In Windows Defender Firewall, Advanced settings, Inbound Rules, delete the rules for questpump-helper.exe, then press the button again.
desk.menu.phones.firewall.another.note: Under the card's button when an older rule still blocks QuestPump. questpump-helper.exe is the program's file name, as Windows lists it.

desk.menu.phones.firewall.blocked.text: Windows Firewall blocks every incoming connection on this network, even from allowed apps, so your phone cannot reach QuestPump. Open Windows Security, then Firewall & network protection, choose the network marked active, and turn off "Blocks all incoming connections". QuestPump looks again each minute.
desk.menu.phones.firewall.blocked.note: The card's text when the firewall blocks every connection. The quoted words are Windows Security's own.

desk.menu.phones.firewall.failed.text: That did not work ({error}). In Windows Defender Firewall, Advanced settings, Inbound Rules, delete the rules for questpump-helper.exe, then press the button again.
desk.menu.phones.firewall.failed.note: Under the card's button when the step failed. {error} is Windows' own reason, in English.

desk.menu.phones.firewall.rule.text: Windows Firewall keeps your phone and watch out until you allow QuestPump on your own network. The rule lets in only devices on your network, and Windows asks for an administrator once.

desk.menu.phones.firewall.title.text: Let your phone reach this PC
desk.menu.phones.firewall.title.note: A card's heading on Windows while Windows Firewall keeps the phone out.

desk.menu.phones.next.check.text: Now press Check again in the game's setup window.
desk.menu.phones.next.check.note: While the strip says the game's setup window shows its Check again (step check_again, 2026-10-13). Shown on the Phones page, under This computer's state and on the welcome's Game row. Check again is the game's setup button: keep it as the game names it.

desk.menu.phones.next.either.text: Now press Check again in the game, or type /reload there.
desk.menu.phones.next.either.note: After a phone paired, or after QuestPump first wrote into the folder of a game that was already running, while the game's strip has not told what it shows yet (an addon older than 2026-10-13, or no square read since the pairing): either way the game reads it. Check again is the game's setup button.

desk.menu.phones.next.grant.text: Next: allow screen reading on This computer, so QuestPump can see the game.
desk.menu.phones.next.grant.note: While the Screen Recording permission is missing and a phone is paired (step grant). This computer is the Menu's page. Nothing in the game is needed after it (2026-10-13).

desk.menu.phones.next.reload.text: Now type /reload in the game once, so it loads your saved progress.
desk.menu.phones.next.reload.note: While the strip says the running game loaded without QuestPump on the computer and showed at a /reload that it does not read its own save back: one /reload brings its saved progress back (step reload, 2026-10-13). /reload is the game's chat command.

desk.menu.phones.pair.note: The pairing section's heading before a phone is paired, and the button on the first start on the computer (its On this computer card's Phone row and its last page) that opens the pairing code in a window with that heading while none is; also the button of Pump home's pair card and of Pro's page without a phone, which open the same window.

desk.menu.phones.paired.title.note: The pairing section's heading once a phone is paired.

desk.menu.phones.phone.note: The welcome's Phone row's label: the paired phone and its watch.

desk.menu.phones.quiet.text: Your phone has not connected for two weeks. To pair it again, scan this code with it.
desk.menu.phones.quiet.note: On the Phones page while the paired phone has not reached QuestPump on this computer for 14 days (its app may be gone, or unpaired out of reach): the pairing code shows again under it.

desk.menu.phones.renew.note: A button: makes a new code, which ends every pairing. It asks for a second press first.

desk.menu.phones.renew.armed.text: Press again to end every pairing
desk.menu.phones.renew.armed.note: The button's words for five seconds after the first press.

desk.menu.phones.title.note: A row in the Menu and the title of its page: the pairing code for the QuestPump app on a phone, and the phone paired.

desk.menu.phones.unnamed.note: The computer's name when the system gives none: on the Phones page and as the name the paired phones show for it.

desk.menu.phones.unread.text: Your phone's pairing could not be read, so it ended: scan this code again with your phone.
desk.menu.phones.unread.note: On the Phones page after QuestPump's settings file did not read at its start: a new pairing code ended the pairing, until the phone scans the code again.

desk.menu.pro.adds.note: The section label over what Pro adds in QuestPump on the computer.

desk.menu.pro.comes.text: It comes with QuestPump Pro in the app on your phone.
desk.menu.pro.comes.note: Pro's page on the computer while Pro is off and no Get Pro shows (contract/store.json's web block not live, or its prices still null): where Pro comes from, over Pair your phone. The computer shows no price.

desk.menu.pro.get.note: The primary on Pro's page on the computer while Pro is off and contract/store.json's web block is live and holds a price (slice 64): it opens questpump.com's Pro page in the browser, where a purchase comes to the account that links the email it is paid with. The computer shows no price.

desk.menu.pro.manage.note: A button on Pro's page on the computer while the account's Pro was bought on questpump.com (slice 64): it opens Paddle's customer portal in the browser, where the player changes or cancels the subscription.

desk.menu.pro.on.text: Pro is on through your phone, so its extras show here too.
desk.menu.pro.on.note: Pro's page on the computer while a paired phone's Pro subscription holds, or the account's Pro from the App Store or Google Play (slice 64).

desk.menu.pro.refused.text: Pro on your phone could not be confirmed here.
desk.menu.pro.refused.note: The Menu's Pro row line and Pro's page while the paired phone's last Pro proof could not be checked on this computer (a build without Google Play's licensing key, or a test purchase), never while the subscription has simply ended.

desk.menu.pro.sync.on.note: The primary of the window Get Pro opens while Sync is off: it turns Sync on, then opens questpump.com's Pro page.

desk.menu.pro.sync.title.text: Turn on sync to get Pro?
desk.menu.pro.sync.title.note: The window Get Pro opens on the computer while Sync is off: Pro goes with the account, which sync keeps (slice 64).

desk.menu.pro.weeks.text: Your weeks in the Saga: the days you trained in each week, and your moves.
desk.menu.pro.weeks.note: What Pro adds on the computer, the Log's Pro weeks (each game week's days in the moves' steps, the moves per week); the computer shows no Health minutes, so pro.has.weeks's minutes are left out.

desk.menu.section.pumps.note: The caps label over the Menu's card of the player's own pumps: Sound and voice, Your setup and Backup.

desk.menu.setup.body.reset.text: Your Body switches, experience and moves on this computer could not be read, so they start empty. A paired phone sends them again when its app opens; check them below.
desk.menu.setup.body.reset.note: On Your setup on the computer, over the Body switches, while the file that keeps them did not read at this start and no device has filled them since.

desk.menu.sound.note: A row in the Menu: the pump's sounds, the voice and the speakers or headset they play on.

desk.menu.sync.unread.text: Sync waits until QuestPump starts again.
desk.menu.sync.unread.note: The Sync card's line, its switch greyed, when QuestPump could not open its saved keys at this start (as desk.menu.phones.address.unread): nothing syncs in that run, since an account joined then would be lost at the next start, which reads the keys again. As menu.sync.demo on the phones.

desk.offers.open.text: Open the pump after each match
desk.offers.open.note: A switch of the Games tab's After a match card: each offer opens the pump at Ready, at a match's end as at a game's close, and the match card shows only while it is off (2026-10-29, Rapha: "this pop up is not needed at all"; "Open the pump when the game closes", at the close alone, until then); on at first since 2026-10-27 (Rapha: "make it default to start for everyone"; off at first until then) (slice 56; the Offers page's until then).

desk.offers.pause.game.note: A choice of Pause offers (its window on the Games tab, the tray's submenu, the menu of a pump's Pause): until the game running now closes. {game} is its name (Dota 2, a picked program's).

desk.offers.pause.game.none.note: The choice of Pause offers that names the game running now (its window on the Games tab, the tray's submenu), dimmed while no game QuestPump watches runs.

desk.offers.paused.game.note: The pause's state (Pause offers' value and its window's line on the Games tab, the Now card's words while paused, the tray's submenu): until that game closes. {game} is its name.

desk.offers.paused.none.note: The pause's state while offers come (Pause offers' value and its window's line on the Games tab, the tray's submenu).

desk.place.desk.note: A choice where the player pumps on the computer (the first start, and the window before the first own pump on a computer that never asked it): pumps with no floor moves and no room to move (the game's Office preset).

desk.place.floor.note: A choice where the player pumps on the computer (the first start, and the window before the first own pump): floor moves and room to move too.

desk.place.go.note: The gold button of the first start's place step: the first Quick pump starts at once. After a restart before that pump, the step shows it again.

desk.place.title.note: The heading of the first start's step that sets the floor moves, room to move and quiet mode on this computer, and of the window that asks it once before the first own pump on a computer that never did.

desk.plist.bluetooth.text: QuestPump links your phone by Bluetooth, so it gets each pump with its screen locked, and reads your heart-rate strap and walking pad.
desk.plist.bluetooth.note: The Mac's question before the desktop app first uses Bluetooth: on the Phones page while its Bluetooth link is on (slice 43), or once the player turns on a heart-rate strap or a walking pad (helper/src-tauri/Info.plist).

desk.plist.screen.text: QuestPump reads the small row of coloured squares the QuestPump addon shows in the corner of World of Warcraft.
desk.plist.screen.note: The Mac's Screen Recording usage string (helper/src-tauri/Info.plist): the desktop app reads the row of coloured squares the addon paints in the game window. World of Warcraft is the game's name: keep it as it is.

desk.pump.done.locked.text: Not counted: you said you felt unwell before it began, so pumps are paused.
desk.pump.done.locked.note: Under a catch-up's moves on the computer when a felt-unwell stop dated before its start reached QuestPump while it ran (from a phone, a watch or the game's save): a pump that began while pumps rest pays nothing, and the moves stay unfinished.

desk.pump.done.paid.text: Done. The game counts these moves the next time it loads.
desk.pump.done.paid.note: Under a catch-up's moves on the computer: the unfinished moves it paid reach World of Warcraft at its next login or /reload.

desk.pump.done.reset.text: Not counted: your progress was reset after this pump began.
desk.pump.done.reset.note: Under a catch-up's moves on the computer when the game's progress was reset (/qp reset all) while it ran: the moves it owed belong to the progress that was reset, so nothing is paid.

desk.pump.done.unpaid.text: Not counted here: these moves were already done on another device.
desk.pump.done.unpaid.note: Under a catch-up's moves on the computer when the game or another device paid them while it ran.

desk.pump.focus.note: The veil over a pump whose window lost the focus mid-pump (the game came to the front): the keys would reach the game, so a click gives the window the focus back.

desk.pump.fullscreen.off.note: Button at the top of Big view while the window fills the screen: back to the window, remembered.

desk.pump.fullscreen.on.note: Button at the top of Big view (the countdown, a running move): fills the screen with the window, remembered for the next pump.

desk.pump.tray.on.note: The tray menu's line while a pump runs on this computer, its window hidden or behind the game: no control, it says why QuestPump holds the computer awake.

desk.shell.tabs.note: Read by VoiceOver and NVDA as the name of the five tabs, Pump, Hero, Book, Log and Games (slice 56), at the window's foot or in its left rail.

desk.slider.value.note: A Slider's level beside its track, 0 to 100 in steps of 5. A screen reader reads it as the slider's value.

desk.sound.ask.note: The first pump's question on the computer, over the outputs: where the sounds and the voice play, so a headset left on the desk does not swallow them.

desk.sound.callouts.note: A switch under the voice in pumps: one recorded line after a move's name on its Ready view (on by default).

desk.sound.gone.text: {name} is not connected, so the sound plays on this computer.
desk.sound.gone.note: The picked output is unplugged or switched off: QuestPump falls back until it is back. {name} is the output's system name.

desk.sound.looking.note: While QuestPump lists the computer's outputs.

desk.sound.offers.note: A switch (off by default): the voice says one line when the match-over card shows.

desk.sound.output.note: The section label over the outputs the sound and the voice can play on.

desk.sound.reader.text: VoiceOver is on, so while this window is in front the voice's lines go to VoiceOver instead.
desk.sound.reader.note: Shown while VoiceOver runs: while QuestPump's window has the focus a pump's lines are said by VoiceOver through the page, never by QuestPump's voice over it; with the window behind another, hidden or minimized, QuestPump's voice says them.

desk.sound.reader.windows.text: A screen reader is on, so while this window is in front the voice's lines go to it instead.
desk.sound.reader.windows.note: Shown while Windows says a screen reader runs (Narrator, NVDA, JAWS): while QuestPump's window has the focus a pump's lines are said by the screen reader, never by QuestPump's voice over it; with the window behind another, hidden or minimized, QuestPump's voice says them.

desk.sound.system.note: The output row that follows the computer's own choice (macOS Sound settings, Windows' default device).

desk.sound.system.now.note: Under This computer's sound: the output the computer uses now, by its system name.

desk.sound.test.note: A row that plays the go's bell and a line of the voice on the picked output; picking an output plays it too.

desk.sound.title.note: The Menu's row and the page's title: QuestPump's sounds, its voice and the output they play on.

desk.sound.voice.note: A switch: the voice that reads a pump's lines (on by default).

desk.sound.volume.note: The section label over the three volume sliders (Master, Sounds, Voice), as a game's audio settings have them.

desk.sound.volume.master.note: A volume slider under Volume: how loud everything the app plays is, the sounds and the voice alike (a game's master volume).

desk.sound.volume.voice.note: A volume slider under Volume: how loud the voice is (a pump's lines, the rep count, Match over.); the Sounds slider beside it reuses menu.sounds.

desk.tray.open.note: The tray menu's item that opens QuestPump's window.

desk.tray.phone.none.note: The phone's line before any phone is paired: the Phones row's line in the Menu and the welcome's Phone row (the tray's item says desk.tray.phone.pair then); the tray's Rust words it.

desk.tray.phone.pair.note: The tray menu's second line while no phone is paired: a click opens QuestPump's window on the Menu's Phones page, with the pairing code. The ellipsis says it opens a window that asks for more.

desk.tray.phone.paired.note: {phone} is the paired phone's name. The tray menu's second line, the Phones row's line in the Menu, the Phones page's line under its heading and the welcome's Phone row: a phone is paired, and no device takes the countdowns now.

desk.tray.phone.paired.linked.text: Paired: {phone} · your phone gets the countdowns now
desk.tray.phone.paired.linked.note: {phone} is the paired phone's name. The tray menu's second line, the Phones row's line in the Menu, the Phones page's line under its heading and the welcome's Phone row: the phone holds the link and gets each pump's countdown.

desk.tray.phone.watch.note: {phone} is the paired phone's name. The tray menu's second line, the Phones row's line in the Menu, the Phones page's line under its heading and the welcome's Phone row: the phone and its watch are paired, and none takes the countdowns now.

desk.tray.phone.watch.linked.text: Paired: {phone}, with its watch · your watch gets the countdowns now
desk.tray.phone.watch.linked.note: {phone} is the paired phone's name. The tray menu's second line, the Phones row's line in the Menu, the Phones page's line under its heading and the welcome's Phone row: the watch holds the link.

desk.tray.phone.watch.phone.text: Paired: {phone}, with its watch · your phone gets the countdowns now
desk.tray.phone.watch.phone.note: {phone} is the paired phone's name. The tray menu's second line, the Phones row's line in the Menu, the Phones page's line under its heading and the welcome's Phone row: the phone holds the link.

desk.tray.quit.note: The tray menu's item that quits QuestPump on this computer (it saves first).

desk.tray.state.found.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line and the first line of This computer; Pump home's status chip shows only what needs fixing since 2026-10-27) once QuestPump found World of Warcraft with QuestPump on this computer and keeps the progress for it: the game is closed, or runs while nothing asks QuestPump to read it.

desk.tray.state.lacks.text: QuestPump is not in the game yet
desk.tray.state.lacks.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line, Pump home's status chip, the first line of This computer) while a World of Warcraft runs whose AddOns folder holds no QuestPump.

desk.tray.state.none.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line, the first line of This computer, and the Game row's line on the welcome's On this computer card) while QuestPump knows no World of Warcraft here and watches no other game (else desk.tray.state.watching): a fact, never a fault (pumps on this computer work without the game).

desk.tray.state.out.text: The game is out of view
desk.tray.state.out.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line, Pump home's status chip, the first line of This computer) while World of Warcraft with QuestPump runs, its squares were read in this run and have been out of view for a few seconds: a loading screen, a movie, the interface hidden with Alt+Z, the game minimised or on another Space. A passing fact, never a fault; before the squares first read in this run, desk.tray.state.waiting.

desk.tray.state.reading.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line and the first line of This computer; Pump home's status chip shows only what needs fixing since 2026-10-27) while QuestPump reads the game's squares on the screen, and for a few seconds after they leave the view, so a corner covered for a moment never changes it.

desk.tray.state.step.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line, Pump home's status chip, the first line of This computer) when This computer has a step to do: the screen reading's permission a device needs, the game folder's rights, the move to Applications, or a screen reading that stopped. On Pump home a click opens This computer.

desk.tray.state.waiting.text: Waiting to see QuestPump in the game
desk.tray.state.waiting.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line, Pump home's status chip, the first line of This computer) while World of Warcraft with QuestPump runs and its squares are not read yet in this run of it (the game still loading, the login screen or a realm queue, the squares out of view before they first read; once read, desk.tray.state.out). Only ever said of a game that runs.

desk.tray.state.watching.note: This computer's state (the tray menu's first line, the first line of This computer, the Games tab's Now card; Pump home's chip until 2026-10-27) while QuestPump knows no World of Warcraft here and watches one other game for its matches' end: {game} is its name as the Games tab shows it (Counter-Strike 2, a picked program's name).

desk.tray.state.watching.games.note: This computer's state (the tray, This computer, the Games tab's Now card; Pump home's chip until 2026-10-27) while QuestPump knows no World of Warcraft here and watches several other games for their matches' end (two or more: the one form is never shown).

desk.tray.streak.done.note: The tray menu's streak line once today has a pump (2026-10-09): {days} is the streak's day count. Before that the line is the streak reminder's words (reminders.notify.streak.body and its forms), while felt unwell rests the pumps pump.home.streak.resting's. Shown only, never a control.

desk.tray.tooltip.note: The tray icon's tooltip. QuestPump is the program's name; {state} is this computer's state as the tray menu's first line says it (Reading the game, Game found · progress kept, …).

desk.welcome.computer.note: The label over the welcome's card of what QuestPump found on the computer: the game and the phone, each with its line.

desk.welcome.computer.choose.note: The Game row's action on the welcome's On this computer card while QuestPump found no World of Warcraft on this computer (the row's line is the tray's No game found yet): opens the system's folder picker, as Change… on This computer does.

desk.welcome.found.note: The heading of the note that drops in at the top once, when QuestPump on the computer found the player's progress at its first open and skipped the first start (never "Welcome back", the reward for coming back after days away).

desk.welcome.found.both.text: From the game and your phone.
desk.welcome.found.both.note: That note's line when the progress came from the game and from a phone.

desk.welcome.found.game.note: That note's line when the progress came from the game.

desk.welcome.found.here.text: From your pumps on this computer.
desk.welcome.found.here.note: That note's line when the progress is only the pumps done on this computer.

desk.welcome.found.pair.text: Pair your phone with the card on Pump home.
desk.welcome.found.pair.note: The found note's last line while no phone is paired: Pump home's card opens the pairing code.

desk.welcome.found.phone.note: That note's line when the progress came from a phone or its watch.

desk.welcome.hero.title.note: The heading over the body map after the first pump on the computer, and the map's name for a screen reader.

desk.window.menu.about.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the app menu's item that shows the version and the maker.

desk.window.menu.app.note: The macOS menu bar's first menu, the app's own: macOS shows the app's name there. Never translated.

desk.window.menu.close.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Window menu's item (Cmd-W); during a pump it asks first.

desk.window.menu.copy.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's item.

desk.window.menu.cut.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's item.

desk.window.menu.edit.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's title.

desk.window.menu.fullscreen.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the View menu's item that fills the screen with the window (macOS names it Exit Full Screen itself while it is).

desk.window.menu.hide.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the app menu's item that hides the window (Cmd-H).

desk.window.menu.hideothers.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the app menu's item that hides every other app (Option-Cmd-H).

desk.window.menu.minimize.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Window menu's item (Cmd-M).

desk.window.menu.paste.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's item.

desk.window.menu.quit.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the app menu's item that quits QuestPump on this computer (Cmd-Q); during a pump it asks first.

desk.window.menu.redo.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's item.

desk.window.menu.selectall.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's item.

desk.window.menu.showall.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the app menu's item that shows every hidden app.

desk.window.menu.undo.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Edit menu's item.

desk.window.menu.view.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the View menu's title.

desk.window.menu.window.note: macOS menu bar, while QuestPump's window is open: the Window menu's title.

desk.window.save.title.note: The title of the system's save dialog when the player saves a share card as a picture.

desk.window.save.video.title.note: The title of the system's save dialog when the player saves a day's reel as a video file (slice 45: the Share window's Save video).

desk.zoom.in.note: macOS View menu (Cmd-+): makes everything in the window larger, one step of This computer's Size.

desk.zoom.out.note: macOS View menu (Cmd--): makes everything in the window smaller, one step of This computer's Size.

desk.zoom.reset.note: macOS View menu (Cmd-0): back to the window's default size, 100 in This computer's Size.

expedition.bar.left.note: At the ExpeditionBar's trailing edge after the clock mark: {time} is the minutes and seconds left of the length chosen (12:40). Gone once none is left.

expedition.bar.round.note: The ExpeditionBar's caps during a round: {round} is the round in play, {count} the rounds planned (the engine's estimate, which may change as each round is decided).

expedition.bar.spoken.note: The ExpeditionBar read after its stage (Round 3 of 5, 12 minutes left), in whole minutes.

expedition.done.early.note: The calm Result's title of an expedition ended part way (End the expedition, End the pump here): the rounds done, the warm-up counted as one.

expedition.done.line.note: The line under Expedition complete: the minutes it took (whole minutes) and the place's name.

expedition.done.spoken.note: The Result's one announcement to VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's screen reader.

expedition.done.title.note: The Fanfare's words on an expedition's Result.

expedition.named.note: A timed pump named by its length (slice 51; Rapha, 2026-10-21): the title of its share card (20-min pump). The min is short for minutes and takes no plural.

expedition.next.cooldown.note: Caps over the cool-down's moves on the breather before it.

expedition.next.round.note: Caps over the next round's moves on the breather: {round} is its number (the warm-up is not counted).

expedition.place.hint.note: The hint of the place line under the Pump screen's button and of the place rows (Start a pump, Your setup): it opens the places window, where the player picks where they train.

expedition.rest.note: Caps over the breather's ring between two rounds of an expedition (30 s).

expedition.rest.spoken.note: The breather read by VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's screen reader as it opens.

expedition.round.start.note: The breather's secondary: opens the next round's first move at once instead of waiting for the ring.

expedition.saga.cooldown.note: The Saga's title of an expedition's cool-down round.

expedition.saga.round.note: The Saga's title of an expedition's round: {round} is its number, the warm-up not counted.

expedition.saga.warmup.note: The Saga's title of an expedition's warm-up round, a pump of its own.

expedition.stage.cooldown.note: An expedition's last round (a stretch, then a flow): the bar's caps and the round's title.

expedition.stage.round.note: The title of an expedition's round on its pump screens: {round} is its number, the warm-up not counted.

expedition.stage.warmup.note: An expedition's first round (a mobility move, then steady cardio): the bar's caps and the round's title.

expedition.stop.note: The breather's quiet button and a row of a round's More (after End the pump here): ends the timed pump at once and shows the Result of the rounds done.

expedition.title.note: A timed pump's name (slice 51; the expedition in the code; Rapha, 2026-10-21: one Quick pump with a length, no word of its own): the caps source over each of its rounds' pump screens (as Picked for you over a Quick pump), where its minutes are not shown. Never "session" (the game's session).

feedback.box.label.note: The text box's name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: what the box is, never the page's title or the Send button's words.

feedback.counter.note: Under the text box: the characters typed of the most it takes (120/500).

feedback.counter.label.note: The counter under the text box as VoiceOver and TalkBack read it (the screen shows 120/500): the characters typed of the most the box takes.

feedback.from.android.note: The first line of what goes, with every message, ticked or not: where it comes from and the app's version ({version} as 1.4.0). Never "Sent from": nothing has gone yet.

feedback.from.iphone.note: The first line of what goes, with every message, ticked or not: where it comes from and the app's version ({version} as 1.4.0). Never "Sent from": nothing has gone yet.

feedback.numbers.banked.note: Pumps the player put off with the game's Bank all button, whose moves wait as unfinished.

feedback.numbers.days.note: Whole days since the oldest entry this phone holds of the player's QuestPump history, the game's or its own; 0 on the first day.

feedback.numbers.finished.note: Pumps with a move done. A pump is the set of moves a finished quest asks for.

feedback.numbers.maxsets.text: Max sets on one ladder on a usual play day: {value}
feedback.numbers.maxsets.note: The middle value (the median) of how many max sets the player did on one ladder in one day they played. {value} is 0, a whole number such as 3 or a half such as 2.5, as the phone writes numbers, never 3.0 or 0.0. A ladder is a family of moves from easy to hard; a max set is a set done to the most reps the player can.

feedback.numbers.move.note: {move} is a move's name (Split squat). {easier}: how often the player took it as the easier version of a harder move; {stopped}: how often they ended it before its time.

feedback.numbers.moves.text: Easier picks and early stops, by move:
feedback.numbers.moves.note: Heads the list of moves the player took as the easier version of a harder one, or stopped before their time.

feedback.numbers.none.note: In place of the list of moves when no move has an easier pick or an early stop.

feedback.numbers.note.text: Only the counts below go with your words, and no name. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
feedback.numbers.note.note: Under Add my numbers while it is on: the counts listed below go with the player's text. Send is the button below it: keep its name as the button reads.

feedback.numbers.note.off.text: Only your words and the version go, and no name. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
feedback.numbers.note.off.note: Under Add my numbers while it is off: only the player's text and the app's version go. Send is the button below it: keep its name as the button reads.

feedback.numbers.tick.note: Checkbox, on at first: adds the counts listed under it to the message.

feedback.numbers.unfinished.note: The moves the player still has to do, at the moment the page opened. Unfinished is the game's word for them.

feedback.numbers.unreadable.text: Your numbers could not be read right now. Turn off Add my numbers to send just your words.
feedback.numbers.unreadable.note: In place of the counts when the phone could not read the player's history: Send stays off while the tick is on. Add my numbers is the tick above: keep its name as the tick reads.

feedback.numbers.window.note: Heads the counts under it. {days} is always 14; each day starts at 4 a.m., as in the game.

feedback.placeholder.text: Tell us what you like, what is wrong or what you miss.
feedback.placeholder.note: Placeholder of the text box: the player's own words to the people who make QuestPump.

feedback.queued.text: Not sent yet. It goes out by itself the next time you open QuestPump.
feedback.queued.note: The phone was offline or the server was busy: the message waits on this phone and is sent again later.

feedback.refused.text: Not sent: the message was turned away. You can write to {address} instead.
feedback.refused.note: The server refused the message, and it is not sent again. {address} is the support mail address, contact@questpump.com, shown as a mail link.

feedback.reply.text: We read every message, but we cannot write back: it has no name or address. If you want an answer, write to {address}.
feedback.reply.note: On the page, always: a message carries no name and no address, so nobody can answer it. {address} is the support mail address, contact@questpump.com, shown as a mail link.

feedback.send.note: Button: sends the message. Off while the text box is empty.

feedback.sending.note: Shown while the message goes out.

feedback.sent.note: The message reached the people who make QuestPump.

feedback.waiting.text: {count} messages wait to go. They go by themselves when you are online.

plural.one: {count} message waits to go. It goes by itself when you are online.
plural.other: {count} messages wait to go. They go by themselves when you are online.

feedback.waiting.note: Under Send while messages the phone could not send yet wait on it and no other line shows there: they go by themselves once the phone is online with QuestPump open.

games.after.note: The caps label over the Games tab's cards of the offers after a match (slice 56): Moves per match, Open the pump after each match, Pause offers, Send a test offer.

games.aim.text: Rest your arms while it runs
games.aim.note: A switch row in the window of a game marked aim in contract/links.json (a shooter: Counter-Strike 2) on the Games tab, shown while that game is on, on by default (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §5).

games.found.dismiss.note: A row in a found game's window on the Games tab (slice 56): its tile goes, for good; the Hidden row brings it back.

games.grant.note: A row under a game whose folder Windows keeps closed: Windows asks for an administrator once.

games.hidden.note: A row of the Games tab's last card while a found game was put away with Not a game, its value how many (slice 56); and the title of the window it opens, which lists them to show again.

games.hidden.restore.note: A hidden game's row action in the Hidden window on the Games tab (slice 56): its tile comes back.

games.more.note: A row of the Games tab's last card (slice 56), while one is listed, and the title of the window it opens: the named games of this system QuestPump does not find on this computer, each with its switch, for an install it does not find.

games.more.intro.text: Turn a game on and QuestPump offers you a pump after each match or when you close it.
games.more.intro.note: The line at the top of the More games window on the Games tab, over its list (Rapha, 2026-10-27: "you think from this menu that these games are available and compatible, you dont expect that these games give you pumps"): what a switch there does. True of every row: a game that tells QuestPump each match's end offers after each match, one heard only by its program closing (Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Rocket League and Hearthstone before Ask after each match) offers when it closes. A switch only says whether QuestPump watches for that game; it never moves the game into Your games, which it joins once it is found on this computer.

games.new.note: What a screen reader hears after the Games tab's name while the tab's dot shows (slice 56): a game found since the player last opened the tab (until 2026-10-28 also, until they first did, a Riot game neither on nor off).

games.none.note: The Games tab's empty state's heading while QuestPump found no game on this computer and the player added none (slice 56), over Add a game.

games.notice.note: A switch of the Games tab's last card, on by default (slice 56; slice 48's, docs/computer-games.md §6.1): off, QuestPump notices no new game running; the games found already stay.

games.now.playing.note: The Games tab's Now card's heading while a game QuestPump watches runs (slice 56), beside the game's icon. {game} is its name (links.name.<key>, a found or picked program's).

games.offer.close.text: Offer a pump when you close {game}
games.offer.close.note: The switch at the top of a game's window on the Games tab, for a game QuestPump hears only by its program closing (a found or added program; Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Rocket League or Hearthstone before Ask after each match): on, its close offers a pump; off, it offers none. It says when, so the window needs no other row for it (Rapha, 2026-10-26: "make it super precise and clear what things do"; Offer a pump with an Asks after row until then). The game's line while a step is owed shows under it. {game} is its name (links.name.<key>, a found or picked program's).

games.offer.match.text: Offer a pump after each match
games.offer.match.note: The switch at the top of a game's window on the Games tab, for a game that tells QuestPump each match's end (League of Legends by its game process, which a match is; a fed game's feed or log; a file game after Ask after each match): on, each match's end offers a pump; off, it offers none. It says when, so the window needs no other row for it (Rapha, 2026-10-26; Offer a pump with an Asks after row until then). The game's line while a step is owed shows under it.

games.pace.note: The section label over the Segmented. Moves per match (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §3): the twin of the game's Moves per quest (Locales/enUS.lua settings.pace*), on the desktop app's Games tab and Your setup and the phones' Your setup; it sizes every pump after a game's end, on every device (the body's match_pace).

games.pace.balanced.note: A Segmented choice, the default, the game's settings.pace.balanced. Moves per match (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §3): the twin of the game's Moves per quest (Locales/enUS.lua settings.pace*), on the desktop app's Games tab and Your setup and the phones' Your setup; it sizes every pump after a game's end, on every device (the body's match_pace).

games.pace.extreme.note: A Segmented choice, the game's settings.pace.extreme. Moves per match (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §3): the twin of the game's Moves per quest (Locales/enUS.lua settings.pace*), on the desktop app's Games tab and Your setup and the phones' Your setup; it sizes every pump after a game's end, on every device (the body's match_pace).

games.pace.light.note: A Segmented choice, the game's settings.pace.light. Moves per match (slice 48, docs/computer-games.md §3): the twin of the game's Moves per quest (Locales/enUS.lua settings.pace*), on the desktop app's Games tab and Your setup and the phones' Your setup; it sizes every pump after a game's end, on every device (the body's match_pace).

games.pause.note: A row of the Games tab's After a match card on the computer, its value the pause's state, the title of its window, the tray menu's submenu, and the title of the first group in the menu of a pump's Pause on the phones and the computer (whose choices also end the pump): no game offer for a while (slice 56; the phones' since 2026-11-05, their linked games' and their own games' offers).

games.pause.four.note: A choice of Pause offers: a row of its window on the Games tab, an item of the tray's submenu and of the menu of a pump's Pause on the phones and the computer.

games.pause.hour.note: A choice of Pause offers: a row of its window on the Games tab, an item of the tray's submenu and of the menu of a pump's Pause on the phones and the computer.

games.pause.night.note: A choice of Pause offers (its window on the Games tab, the tray's submenu, the menu of a pump's Pause on the phones and the computer): until the next game day begins. {time} is that clock time in the device's own format, 04:00 on most nights.

games.pause.resumed.note: A choice of Pause offers (its window on the Games tab, the tray's submenu, the menu of a pump's Pause on the phones and the computer): until the player resumes them (the computer's Games tab or tray, the phones' Linked games or Games on this phone).

games.paused.resumed.note: The pause's state (Pause offers' value and its window's line on the Games tab, the Now card's words while paused, the tray's submenu; on the phones the line of the card over Resume offers on Linked games and Games on this phone): until the player resumes the offers.

games.paused.until.note: The pause's state (Pause offers' value and its window's line on the Games tab, the Now card's words while paused, the tray's submenu; on the phones the line of the card over Resume offers on Linked games and Games on this phone): {time} is the clock time it ends, in the device's own format.

games.pick.note: The last tile of the Games tab's grid, the empty state's button and the title of the window it opens (slice 56; a row of the Games page, Any game: pick its program, until then): the games QuestPump knows whose program has a window now, each with Turn on, then the programs with a window now, one of which the player picks to watch (its close offers a pump), and More games at its foot.

games.pick.more.text: Choose which games give you pumps
games.pick.more.note: The line under More games at the foot of the Add a game window (2026-10-26): what the More games window it opens is for, the games QuestPump knows by name for this system, each with the switch that says whether it offers a pump (Rapha, 2026-10-27: "it just says more games and not enable quest pump or sth"; Games QuestPump knows by name until then).

games.pick.none.text: No program has a window open now.
games.pick.none.note: The Add a game window's line while no program has a window open (slice 56).

games.port.note: A row in the window of a game whose feed comes to a port on this computer, while it is on (slice 48: Legends of Runeterra's API, F1 25's and Forza Motorsport's telemetry), its value the port; and the title of the window it opens to change it.

games.port.invalid.note: Under the Port window's field while what it holds is no whole number from 1024 to 65535 (slice 48): Done keeps nothing then. The numbers are the lowest and highest port the field takes, written as they are.

games.port.taken.note: Under the Port window's field while the port typed is the one another racing or loopback game takes (slice 48): Done keeps nothing then, as the desktop app refuses it. {game} is that game's name (links.name.<key>).

games.program.remove.note: A row in the window of a program the player added on the Games tab: it is watched no more and its tile goes.

games.pump.note: The start of a game's standing pump (slice 57: every match its own pump): the tray's item, Pump home's foot, the Games tab's Now card while the offer stands and nothing holds it, and the phones' Pump tab offer; {game} the offer's own name, one on every surface (a named game's as contract/links.json's computer list writes it, a found or added program's own name). It names the game the pump follows, never the match's length, a result or a debt (the care rule).

games.resume.note: Ends the pause of the game offers now: the Games tab's Now card's button and a row of the Pause offers window while a pause stands, the tray's item, and on the phones the button of the card on Linked games and Games on this phone while a pause stands.

games.setup.note: The primary of a game's window on the Games tab (slice 56) for the four games heard through a file QuestPump puts in their folder (Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Rocket League, Hearthstone), while the game is on and the player has not asked for it yet: it puts the file there, and the game then asks after each match instead of its close.

games.status.api.text: {game} does not answer on this computer. In its settings, turn on Third Party Endpoints at the port below, then start it again
games.status.api.note: A game asked on the loopback whose own settings can turn its API off and that runs without answering (slice 48: Legends of Runeterra, whose settings name the switch Third Party Endpoints with its port; Riot: "can be disabled and the port may be adjusted in the settings menu"). The port below is the Port row under it. StarCraft II, whose client API no setting is known to change, shows games.status.restart instead. {game} is the game's name.

games.status.asking.note: A game's line while the one-time administrator step's prompt is up.

games.status.failed.text: QuestPump could not write {game}'s setup file. Turn it off and on to try again.
games.status.failed.note: A turned-on game's line when its setup file could not go in for a reason other than the folder's permissions (Copy diagnostics and the log say which). {game} is its name.

games.status.inioff.text: Your TAStatsAPI.ini turns Rocket League's stats off. Set PacketSendRate=1 in it, then start the game again.
games.status.inioff.note: Rocket League's line when the player's own TAStatsAPI.ini (which the desktop app reads and never writes over) turns the game's Stats API off. The file and key names are written as they are typed.

games.status.launch.text: Add -gamestateintegration to Dota 2's launch options in Steam, then start it again
games.status.launch.note: Dota 2's line when it ran two minutes without a word: it posts its state only with this launch option, which the player adds in Steam (the game's Properties, Launch options). The option is a code, written as it is typed.

games.status.launch.condebug.text: Add -condebug to {game}'s launch options in Steam, then start it again
games.status.launch.condebug.note: Deadlock's and Team Fortress 2's line when the game ran two minutes without a word in its console log (2026-10-29): Valve's games write that log only with this launch option, which the player adds in Steam (the game's Properties, Launch options), as Dota 2's games.status.launch asks for its own; QuestPump never edits Steam's settings. The option is a code, written as it is typed. {game} is the game's name (links.name.deadlock, links.name.teamfortress).

games.status.nojournal.text: {game} wrote no journal since it started. Start it again
games.status.nojournal.note: Elite Dangerous' line when it ran two minutes (SILENT_MS) since its start and no journal of it came in this run (slice 48): its Journal file in Saved Games is written at each start. {game} is the game's name (links.name.elite).

games.status.noshared.text: {game} shared no race data since it started. Start it again
games.status.noshared.note: iRacing's and Assetto Corsa Competizione's line when the game ran two minutes (SILENT_MS) since its start and the data it publishes for other apps (its documented shared memory) could not be read in this run (slice 48). {game} is the game's name (links.name.<key>).

games.status.noshared.ams2.text: In {game}'s Options, then System, set Shared Memory to Project CARS 2, then start it again
games.status.noshared.ams2.note: Automobilista 2's line when it ran two minutes (SILENT_MS) since its start and its race data could not be read (2026-10-29): the game publishes its documented shared memory only once the player sets Options, System, Shared Memory to "Project CARS 2" (the format QuestPump reads); QuestPump never changes the game's settings. {game} is the game's name (links.name.automobilista).

games.status.permission.text: Allow QuestPump to write to {game}'s folder. Windows asks once.
games.status.permission.note: A turned-on game's line on Windows when its folder (under Program Files) refuses the setup file: the button beside it runs the one-time administrator step, as the game folder's does. {game} is its name.

games.status.porttaken.text: Another program, such as SimHub, uses port {port}. Keep {game} on that program's port, have it forward to another port and set that one in Port below. Or set a free port in Port below and the same one in the game's settings
games.status.porttaken.note: A racing game heard by the telemetry it sends (slice 48: F1 25, Forza Motorsport) whose port on 127.0.0.1 another program holds while the game runs (a telemetry tool such as SimHub, which can forward what it receives to another port): forwarding keeps both programs hearing the game, so it comes first; the Port row under it changes the port QuestPump listens on. Once the game closes, the line goes back to the game's first one. {port} is a port number, written as it is; {game} is the game's name (links.name.<key>).

games.status.restart.note: A turned-on game's line when it ran as its setup file went in, or ran two minutes without a word: it reads the file at its start only. {game} is its name (links.name.<key>). Since slice 48 also StarCraft II, whose client API on the loopback did not answer while it ran: no setting of its own is known to turn that API off, so starting it again is the advice (games.status.api is Legends of Runeterra's).

games.status.udp.text: In {game}'s Telemetry Settings, turn UDP Telemetry on and UDP Broadcast Mode off, set UDP IP Address to 127.0.0.1, UDP Port to {port} and UDP Format to 2026, 2025 or 2024
games.status.udp.note: F1 25's line while it is turned on and not heard yet (slice 48): the player sets these in the game's own Settings, Telemetry Settings, in its words (EA's F1 25 menu as F1Laps' and Track Titan's setup pages name it, read 2026-10-20). {game} is the game's name (links.name.formulaone); {port} is a port number (its default 20777, or the one set in the Port row under it), written as it is. UDP Format 2026 is the 2026 Season Pack's, read as 2025's and 2024's are (feeds.rs formula); 2023 numbers its sessions another way and is not read. Forza Motorsport shows games.status.udp.forza instead.

games.status.udp.forza.text: In {game}'s Gameplay & HUD settings, under UDP Race Telemetry, turn Data Out on, with its IP address 127.0.0.1 and its port {port}
games.status.udp.forza.note: Forza Motorsport's line while it is turned on and not heard yet (slice 48), in its menu's words (Settings, Gameplay & HUD, UDP Race Telemetry: Data Out, Data Out IP Address, the port; Turn 10's Data Out page and Simucube's setup page, read 2026-10-20); either packet format (Sled or Car Dash) is read. {game} is the game's name (links.name.forza); {port} is a port number (5555, QuestPump's own default, or the one set in the Port row under it), written as it is.

games.status.udpformat.text: Set UDP Format to 2026, 2025 or 2024 in {game}'s Telemetry Settings
games.status.udpformat.note: F1 25's line when its telemetry reaches the port in a UDP Format QuestPump does not read (slice 48: 2023 or older, whose session numbers differ): the player picks one of these in the game's Telemetry Settings. {game} is the game's name (links.name.formulaone).

games.test.note: A row of the Games tab's After a match card: shows the card now, as a match's end will.

games.test.held.text: Not now: no offer comes during a pump or a match, while the game with QuestPump runs, or while you rest after feeling unwell.
games.test.held.note: Under Send a test offer on the Games tab, in place of its line, while the offers are held; the row is disabled then.

games.tile.off.note: The one word under a game's name on its dimmed tile on the Games tab while the player turned it off (slice 56): its end offers no pump. Keep it to a short word.

games.tile.on.note: The value of a game QuestPump knows in the Add a game window while its program (League of Legends' client, the Riot Client) has a window and the game is off: the row turns it on (2026-10-26). Until 2026-10-28 also the small button on a Riot game's tile while it was neither on nor off, and the button of its question on the Games tab and on the card. Keep it short.

games.tile.playing.note: The one word under a game's name on its tile on the Games tab while the game runs (slice 56), and under a recent game's name on Pump home (2026-10-27). Keep it to a short word.

games.yours.note: The caps label over the Games tab's grid of game tiles (slice 56): the games found or installed on this computer and the programs the player added.

health.connect.android.note: Button: asks for access to Health Connect.

health.connect.ios.note: Button: asks for access to Apple Health, to save the pumps as workouts and read back the minutes played (Android's health.connect.android: Save to Health Connect).

health.connecting.ios.note: In place of Save to Apple Health (health.connect.ios) while Health's own sheet is on its way (it takes seconds to show).

health.minutes.week.note: In the Health card at the Log's foot, beside a number: the minutes of QuestPump's own workouts in Health in this game week.

health.none.ios.text: No QuestPump workouts in Apple Health yet.

health.notsaving.ios.text: To save your pumps there: the Health app, your profile, Apps, QuestPump, Workouts.
health.notsaving.ios.note: The steps in the Health app that let QuestPump save workouts: on the Log's Health card, and on Pump home's follow card once Apple Health was asked and still may not save them (2026-10-14). Apps and Workouts are the Health app's own words: use its words in the language.

health.plist.share.text: QuestPump reads back its own workouts, your Apple Watch's play sessions and the pumps this device saved, to show the minutes you played each week. With the sitting reminder on, it also reads your steps and stand hours.
health.plist.share.note: The system's question before the app reads Apple Health. Says "this device", not "phone": an Info.plist string takes no placeholder, and the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

health.plist.update.text: QuestPump saves each pump this device times as a workout in Apple Health, with its start and end.
health.plist.update.note: The iPhone's question before it saves workouts to Apple Health (Info.plist); the system shows it with Allow and Don't Allow. Says "this device", not "phone": an Info.plist string takes no placeholder, and the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

health.rationale.privacy.note: Link: opens the privacy policy on questpump.com.

health.rationale.reads.text: It reads back the exercises QuestPump saved, to show your minutes per week in the Saga. With the sitting reminder on, it reads your steps from every app for the last hour, even while QuestPump is closed, to notice an hour of sitting.
health.rationale.reads.note: Log is the name of the app's log screen. The sitting reminder is the switch on the Reminders page.

health.rationale.stays.text: QuestPump never sends what it saves or reads there off your phone.

health.rationale.title.note: Page title. Keep both names as they are.

health.rationale.writes.text: QuestPump saves each play session your watch records to Health Connect. It saves the exercise with one segment per pump, and its heart rate and steps. Each pump this phone times is saved as an exercise too, with only its start and end.

health.record.pump.note: The title of an exercise QuestPump writes to Health Connect for a pump this phone timed; {title} is the pump's title, such as "Kill quest · one move".

health.record.session.note: The title of an exercise QuestPump writes to Health Connect for a play session the watch recorded; other apps show it.

health.saved.android.note: Under the Health Connect heading: QuestPump's pumps and play sessions are written to Health Connect.

health.saving.ios.note: Under the Apple Health heading at the Log's foot: the pumps this phone times are saved as workouts.

health.title.android.note: Section header: Google's Health Connect by its name, never translated.

health.title.ios.note: Section header: Apple's Health app by its name. Keep Apple's name for it in the language.

health.unavailable.android.text: Health Connect is not on this phone. Your pumps stay in QuestPump.

health.update.android.text: Health Connect needs an update before QuestPump can save your pumps there.

health.update.button.android.note: Button: opens Health Connect's page in Google Play.

kit.back.note: Name of the round back button on a page's top bar, read by VoiceOver and TalkBack: leaves the page for the one before it.

kit.button.busy.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack while a button waits for its task to finish.

kit.days.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the day pips under a next step: {have} game days counted of the {need} it takes.  Plural on the day count (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check: "0 of 1 days" after a step down); {have} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers.

kit.eachside.note: Under a move's goal on its Ready view, in the caps word's place: do it on the left and on the right.

kit.familiarity.count.note: How well the player knows a move with its place on the scale (the game's tip.move.fam): {word} is New, Tried, Familiar or Learned, {step} its place from 0, {total} the top place, 3 (Tried (1 of 3)). The move's page and the Book's tooltip for a move done without a record.

kit.familiarity.days.note: Familiar with the days to the next word: {word} is Familiar, {days} the game days the move was done of the {need} that make it Learned, {step} of {total} its place on the scale.

kit.familiarity.familiar.note: How well the player knows a move: done on several days. On a move's page and its tooltip, in words, never a colour.

kit.familiarity.learned.note: How well the player knows a move: done on many days. On a move's page and its tooltip, in words, never a colour.

kit.familiarity.new.note: How well the player knows a move: never done. On a move's page and its tooltip, in words, never a colour.

kit.familiarity.tried.note: How well the player knows a move: done once. On a move's page and its tooltip, in words, never a colour.

kit.fanfare.moves.note: A catch-up pump's banner in place of Quest complete, which only a quest turned in earns (3 moves done).

kit.fanfare.paragon.note: The Result's banner past level 60 when the pump raised the Paragon rank (it takes the level's place), a late rank's toast line and the XP bar's caption past level 60 (Paragon 3). Paragon is a rank's name: keep it as the game's own word.

kit.fanfare.paragon.spoken.note: What a screen reader says for the Paragon banner (You reached Paragon 3).

kit.fanfare.pump.note: The fanfare's title after an app pump that no quest started (a Quick pump, a pump after a match or a stream), where Quest complete would say a quest was turned in.

kit.fanfare.quest.note: The fanfare's title after a pump, as the game says when a quest is turned in.

kit.fanfare.spoken.note: What a screen reader says for the level-up banner, whose words turn from Quest complete to the level (kit.level, QP 13): You reached QP 13. QP is the app's level, not a word to translate.

kit.fanfare.streak.note: A streak milestone (7, 30, 100, 365 or 1,000 days) on the Result's banner, or as its first row when a level took the banner, and since slice 45 how the streak card reads in the Share window; a milestone of whole years from 730 days takes kit.fanfare.streak.years.

kit.fanfare.streak.spoken.note: VoiceOver and TalkBack's announcement of a streak milestone.

kit.fanfare.streak.years.note: A streak milestone of whole years from two (730, 1,095, 1,460 or 1,825 days; 2026-10-09) on the Result's banner, or as its first row when a level took the banner, and since slice 45 how the streak card of such a streak reads in the Share window: {years} is the years, 2 or more.

kit.fanfare.streak.years.spoken.note: VoiceOver and TalkBack's announcement of a streak milestone of whole years (kit.fanfare.streak.years).

kit.figure.pause.action.note: TalkBack's action on a move's playing figure, which shows a round pause mark at its corner: it stops the loop where it is.

kit.figure.pause.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint on a move's playing figure, which shows a round pause mark at its corner: tapping it stops the loop where it is.

kit.figure.play.action.note: TalkBack's action on a move's paused figure, which shows a round play mark at its corner: it plays the loop again.

kit.figure.play.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint on a move's paused figure, which shows a round play mark at its corner: tapping it plays the loop again.

kit.goal.note: Small label under a move's goal, the least the pump asks (16+), and over the goal on a ladder's page. One word.

kit.goal.set.note: Small label under a move's goal on its Ready view, in place of Goal, when the move's ladder already had sets this game day: the set of that ladder this one is today (set 2 today), whose goal is the repeat share of the player's form. The iPhone follows on a Mac.

kit.goal.value.note: A move's goal: the least the pump asks, with a plus for more (16+). Keep the plus after the number.

kit.legend.label.note: Read by VoiceOver, TalkBack and screen readers as the Legendary moment opens: the step's quality word, then the move (Legendary: One-arm push-up).

kit.level.note: The player's level, in the game's own words (QP 13): under the XP bar, the words the Result's banner turns to at a new level, and a late level toast's line under Level up. QP is QuestPump's level: never translated.

kit.maxset.note: A move's goal when the player has no record on it yet: one set of as many as they can. Two short words.

kit.more.note: Name of the round button with three dots, read by VoiceOver and TalkBack: opens a pump's other choices.

kit.move.how.note: Heading over a move's numbered steps (the game's How, contract/moves.json how): on a pump's Ready view, in a move's window and on a step's card (a move's page says How to, ladders.journal.how).

kit.move.tips.note: Heading under How over a move's tips (the game's Tips, contract/moves.json tips, with the move's own advice last).

kit.objective.spoken.time.note: What a screen reader says for a timed move's length or a clock's time left or held, which the screen shows as "30 s" or "0:30"; also a timed move's seconds on a pump's page in the Log.

kit.objective.state.done.note: Read after an objective line's label when the move is done; on a step's card, after the row of another ladder's step the climb waits for, once that step is done (its check mark).

kit.objective.state.missed.note: Read after an objective line's label when the pump ended without the move; on a step's card, after the row of another ladder's step the climb waits for, while that step is not done yet (its dash).

kit.pill.record.note: A reward on a pump's Ready view: the move can set the player's first record.

kit.pill.xp.note: A reward on a pump's Ready view: the experience points the move up next pays. XP is short for experience points. Also how VoiceOver and TalkBack read the XP at a Log row's right (75 XP).

kit.pips.label.note: What a screen reader says for a ladder's pips: the step the player has reached of the ladder's fourteen.

kit.quality.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for a move's button (Push-up, Uncommon 5). {quality} is the quality word (Starter, Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary), {rung} the move's rung on its ladder.

kit.quality.untrained.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the button of a move the player has not placed on its ladder yet.

kit.record.load.note: A set done with a weight, as a record or a last set shows it: {kg} the kilograms (12.5), {reps} the reps. Keep the multiplication sign.

kit.record.load.each.note: A set done with a weight in each hand: {kg} the kilograms of each, {reps} the reps.

kit.record.none.note: Under Record on a move or a ladder before the player's first set on it: no record yet.

kit.record.yours.note: The player's best on a move as the move keeps it, a count (15) or a hold's time as a clock (0:26): on the count step, and the Book's tooltip line for a move with a record.

kit.rep.note: The unit under the count the player types when it is 1: one repetition. The number stands over it.

kit.reps.note: The unit under the count the player types when it is not 1: repetitions. The number stands over it.

kit.reward.best.note: A result row after a clean counted set under the best (slice 42): the form's best stands.

kit.reward.best.new.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line (slice 42): a clean count over the form's best, a record (its shine, stat point and sound).

kit.reward.check.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line in the unlock line's place (slice 42): a stretch check passed, {move} the move it opened (Pistol, hands on the desk), shown only where the move is open after the set (slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17: a move still held by another wait never says it is open). A climb's check says kit.reward.check.climb, never a move of the step.

kit.reward.check.climb.text: Check passed: {ladder} can climb to step {n}
kit.reward.check.climb.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line in the unlock line's place, for a climb's stretch check passed (slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17; the game's ui.result.checkClimb): {ladder} the ladder whose climb the check holds (Squat, never the pose's own family), {n} the step that climb goes to (7). A move's check is kit.reward.check.

kit.reward.check.placed.note: A result row under kit.reward.check where the pass lifted the stretch ladder (a placement, rung cause check; slice 42): {ladder} that ladder (Ankle), {n} its new step (4), with the unlocks it reached after it.

kit.reward.cleanday.note: A result row (slice 42): the clean day a counted set saved Yes, to the end brought, {have} of the {need} the climb to step {n} takes; none when today's day was in already.

kit.reward.earned.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack after an earned reward's words (+1 Strength, earned).

kit.reward.enough.note: A result row: a first max set reached the top of its step, which is enough to move to the next step (the game's words). {value} is a count or a hold's time.

kit.reward.first.note: A result row: a move's first max set, its first record. {value} is a count (12) or a hold's time (0:26).

kit.reward.fullmove.note: A result row (slice 52): the full move this session brought (a Yes, asked or by Keep going, on a steady move dosed at the player's own timed step that ran the full 45 s while the step's dose stood at the ledger's top, ledger_m's 1500), {have} of the {need} the climb to step {n} takes (Full move 1 of 2 toward step 4).

kit.reward.haulday.note: A result row after a Long Haul answered Yes (slice 55): the game days with a Yes at this length, {have} of the {need} that open the next length, {next} (long_haul_days, 2: Long Haul 1:30: day 1 of 2 toward 2:00.); none at the longest.

kit.reward.mastered.note: The result row once a step is mastered, and the watch summary's line in the unlock line's place (slice 42): {ladder} the ladder (Squat), {n} the step (6). No app toasts it (the game toasts its own).

kit.reward.next.note: Under a first record's row: the least the next fresh set asks, written as a goal (13+, or a hold's 0:28+).

kit.reward.notallout.text: Not all out: saved, no clean day
kit.reward.notallout.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line, after Not all out (slice 53), as kit.reward.slipped.

kit.reward.opened.note: A result row: the pump opened the next step of a ladder whose colour (orange or gold) a later set earns (Opened: Archer push-up); kit.reward.unlock once earned.

kit.reward.placed.text: Your step: {value}. Your record of {record} stands.
kit.reward.placed.note: A result row: a max set after a break (a placement) at or under the move's record, which stays (the game's words). {value} and {record} are counts (15, 22) or a hold's times (0:26).

kit.reward.record.note: A result row: the move's new best. {value} is a count (18) or a hold's time (0:26).

kit.reward.rekindled.note: A result row: a step earned again after a rung down (Won back: Archer push-up), shown quieter than a first unlock.

kit.reward.return.back.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line (slice 53's return): the first cardio move after 14 game days without one ended any other way, so the step went one down, {n} the step now (Back to step 5.); each clean or full-move day climbs one back to the step held before.

kit.reward.return.holds.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line (slice 53's return): the first cardio move after 14 game days without one, a window saved Yes, to the end or a steady move with a Yes, kept the step, {n} (Still on step 6.).

kit.reward.slipped.text: Form slipped: saved, no clean day
kit.reward.slipped.note: A result row, and the watch summary's line, after Form slipped (slice 42).

kit.reward.stat.note: A stat point earned (+1 Strength): a result row for each stat the pump raised; on the phones' Ready view of a game pump, the pill for the stat a record would raise on a loaded move with a weighted record, whose condition the phone cannot know (the game relays no planned weight; every other Ready pill is kit.reward.stat.beat).

kit.reward.stat.beat.note: On a pump's Ready view, the pill for the stat the move's record would raise, with its condition as the game's chip says it ('+1 Strength' over 'if you beat 12'): {record} is the count past which the set is a record, a count, a hold's time as a clock (0:40) or, on a loaded move, the reps at the planned weight that match the weighted record. A pill of its own, never summed with a certain stat gain.

kit.reward.step.note: The line under an unlock: the ladder and its step on the one scale of fourteen (Push · step 7), beside the quality word.

kit.reward.tag.first.note: The Result's tag on a move's row whose first max set set its first record (2026-10-29), in gold with the record glyph; the next goal or kit.reward.enough under it. The iPhone shows it once its Result has the same rows (owed).

kit.reward.tag.record.note: The Result's tag on a move's row whose count passed its record (2026-10-29), in gold with the record glyph, kit.reward.was beside it; a counted set's new best clean count takes it too. The iPhone shows it once its Result has the same rows (owed).

kit.reward.title.note: A result row: the pump earned a title (New title: the Tested).

kit.reward.topday.text: Day {have} of {need} at the top, toward step {n}
kit.reward.topday.note: Under a move's Result row (2026-10-29) where the move stands for its strength ladder's step: the game days at the top of its range so far, {have} of the {need} the climb to step {n} takes (the sheet's nx, what the ladder's ring counts), beside as many pips; none once the days are in or no climb is open. The iPhone shows it once its Result has the same rows (owed).

kit.reward.unlock.note: A result row: the pump unlocked the next step of a ladder (Unlocked: Archer push-up); its line under it names the ladder and the step with the quality word.

kit.reward.vault.note: A result row: the pump reached one of the weekly vault's goals, which pays XP; the goal is the line under it.

kit.reward.vault.embers.note: Under Weekly goal reached: the embers tier reached this week (slice 55, in place of cardio minutes: 3, 9 or 15 embers).

kit.reward.vault.moves.note: Under Weekly goal reached: the goal of moves done this week (40 moves).

kit.reward.vault.records.note: Under Weekly goal reached: the goal of records beaten or stars earned this week (3 records or stars).

kit.reward.was.note: Beside kit.reward.tag.record on a move's Result row (2026-10-29): the record the count passed, a count (35), a hold's time (0:26) or a loaded record with its weight (10 kg × 20). Lower case: it follows the tag. The iPhone shows it once its Result has the same rows (owed).

kit.reward.won.note: A result row: a set earned an orange (Legendary) or gold (Artifact) step its climb had opened (Earned: One-arm push-up), the step's colour and its moment; its line under it names the ladder and the step with the quality word.

kit.second.note: The unit under a hold's count when it is 1. The number stands over it.

kit.seconds.note: The unit under a hold's count when it is not 1. The number stands over it.

kit.set.note: Caps word under an owed move a catch-up pays without asking its count (a timed move, or a list from a helper before 2026-10-12), and the goal such a move of reps shows in the timer ring and the Live Activity: one set; since 2026-10-12 a catch-up doses its rep moves and holds and asks their count, which shows their goal or Max set instead.

kit.share.note: Name of the share button, read by VoiceOver and TalkBack: shares a card or a record.

kit.stars.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for a step's stars: {stars} earned of {total} (3).

kit.stepper.less.note: Name of the minus button beside the count, read by VoiceOver and TalkBack.

kit.stepper.more.note: Name of the plus button beside the count, read by VoiceOver and TalkBack.

kit.steps.banked.note: Small, in the Legendary orange, centred above a match pump's step bars of the unfinished moves riding after its own (slice 61; Rapha, 2026-11-02): those bars are moves the player banked before. One word.
