kit.steps.move.note: Beside a pump's step bars, and what a screen reader says for them: which of the pump's moves is on now.

kit.steps.rider.note: Beside a pump's step bars, and what a screen reader says for them, on an unfinished move riding a match's pump that carries unfinished moves after its own (slice 61), the game's line beside its move (Panel.lua ui.panel.riders, ui.panel.riderOf): which of the unfinished moves is on now, then which of the whole pump's moves.

kit.steps.riders.note: Beside a pump's step bars, and what a screen reader says for them, on a move of the pump's own in a match's pump that carries unfinished moves after its own (slice 61), the game's line beside its move (Panel.lua ui.panel.riders, ui.panel.riderOf): which of the whole pump's moves is on now and how many unfinished moves ride in it.

kit.sweep.go.note: In the ring at the end of the countdown: start the move now. One short word.

kit.sweep.goal.note: Under a hold's clock: the hold's goal as minutes and seconds (goal 0:15); the ring fills toward it.

kit.sweep.goal.reps.note: Under the count of a set of reps the voice counts aloud, which rises with the figure's reps: the set's goal, the least the pump asks (goal 16+); the ring fills toward it.

kit.sweep.goal.spoken.note: What a screen reader says for the goal under a hold's clock, which the screen shows as "goal 0:15".

kit.sweep.record.note: Under a hold's clock: the player's best hold in seconds; s is short for seconds.

kit.sweep.record.spoken.note: What a screen reader says for the record under a hold's clock, which the screen shows as "record 42 s".

kit.tile.favourite.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for a move the player marked as favourite. {label} is what the tile reads otherwise (Knee push-up, Uncommon 5).

kit.tile.off.note: A small mark on a move's tile in Book: the player switched the move off for pumps (Include in pumps off). Keep it to a short word.

kit.tile.off.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for a move the player switched off for pumps. {label} is what the tile reads otherwise (Knee push-up, Uncommon 5).

kit.toast.embers.note: A toast's heading once a game day, as the day's third ember lights (slice 55, embers_day): three cardio moves done in full today; its line kit.toast.embers.line.

kit.toast.embers.line.note: Under Cardio done today (slice 55): the embers lit this week so far, the day's three among them (7 this week).

kit.toast.imported.note: The heading of the note that drops in at the top when a sheet imported during a pump shows once the pump has ended.

kit.toast.imported.line.note: The imported sheet's note: Hero (the tab) shows the sheet.

kit.toast.level.note: The heading of the note that drops in at the top at a new QP level.

kit.toast.moved.note: A toast's heading, once an install, as the game's first sheet takes Hero over from the phone's own (2026-10-09): {name} is the character's name as Hero shows it.

kit.toast.moved.game.text: Your progress now lives in the game
kit.toast.moved.game.note: kit.toast.moved for a character the sheet names no name for.

kit.toast.moved.line.note: Under the moved toast's heading: the character's level (QP is QuestPump's level, never translated) and its streak; with no streak the line is kit.level alone.

kit.toast.paragon.note: A toast's heading when the game's sheet shows a Paragon rank the pump raised after its Result had closed; its line is the rank (Paragon 3).

kit.toast.record.note: The heading of the note that drops in at the top after a record, and the chip under a count that passes the record.

kit.toast.record.line.note: The record note's line: the move, the new record and the count the next pump asks for (Push-up 23 · next 24).

kit.toast.rekindled.note: The same toast for a step earned again after a rung down.

kit.toast.title.note: The heading of the note that drops in at the top when the character earns a title.

kit.toast.unlock.note: A toast's heading when a step the last game pump unlocked reaches the phone after its Result closed; its line is the move with its quality word.

kit.toast.won.note: A toast's heading when an orange or gold step a set of the last game pump earned reaches the phone or the computer after its Result closed; its line is the move with its quality word.

kit.vault.complete.note: Beside the weekly vault's title once all its goals are reached this week, the embers' third tier among them (slice 55), and when they start again (Complete · resets Mon 04:00).

kit.vault.embers.note: A weekly vault goal (slice 55, in place of Cardio minutes): the embers lit this week, in three tiers, 3, 9 and 15 (vault_embers), each a weekly goal paying XP; its row shows the next tier's need (4/9) with three tier pips.

kit.vault.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack and screen readers for a weekly vault goal: its name, then done so far of the goal (Moves done, 32 of 40).

kit.vault.moves.note: A weekly vault goal: the moves done this week, every source's (40 moves; as the game's HUD names it).

kit.vault.reached.note: Read by screen readers after a weekly vault goal reached this week.

kit.vault.records.note: A weekly vault goal: the records beaten and the stars earned this week.

kit.vault.reset.note: Beside the weekly vault's label: when its goals start again, the week's turn as the locale writes a short weekday and time (Resets Mon 04:00).

kit.vault.value.note: A weekly vault goal's progress: done so far over the goal (32/40); the embers' over their next tier (4/9, slice 55).

kit.vault.week.bear.note: The weekly vault card's caps title in Bear week (slice 54, in place of Weekly vault): one omen a week for every player, Hare, Fist, Frog, Bear and Oak in turn by the vault's week. An omen's name, a game word.

kit.vault.week.fist.note: The weekly vault card's caps title in Fist week (slice 54, in place of Weekly vault): one omen a week for every player, Hare, Fist, Frog, Bear and Oak in turn by the vault's week. An omen's name, a game word.

kit.vault.week.frog.note: The weekly vault card's caps title in Frog week (slice 54, in place of Weekly vault): one omen a week for every player, Hare, Fist, Frog, Bear and Oak in turn by the vault's week. An omen's name, a game word.

kit.vault.week.hare.note: The weekly vault card's caps title in Hare week (slice 54, in place of Weekly vault): one omen a week for every player, Hare, Fist, Frog, Bear and Oak in turn by the vault's week. An omen's name, a game word.

kit.vault.week.oak.note: The weekly vault card's caps title in Oak week (slice 54, in place of Weekly vault): one omen a week for every player, Hare, Fist, Frog, Bear and Oak in turn by the vault's week. An omen's name, a game word.

kit.weekdots.rested.note: Read after the days pumped in the streak's week marks (2026-10-09): {days} names the weekdays a rest token kept the streak through (or keeps it through while today is open), as one list (Tuesday and Wednesday). Never worded as a miss or a loss.

kit.weekdots.resting.note: Read after the days pumped and the rest tokens' days in the streak's week marks (2026-10-09): {days} names the weekdays the player rested after feeling unwell, which the streak skips, as one list.

kit.window.covered.text: Another app is covering the screen. Close it and try again.
kit.window.covered.note: Android: the error line in a trust window's failure slot (Pair, Let in, Join, the check number's Done, Delete account, Sign out, Remove email, Remove {device}, the account question's Add or Join) after a tap on its confirming button came through another app's window drawn over QuestPump, which the button refuses (tapjacking). Its close and Not now still work.

kit.xp.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the XP bar (QP 12, 340 of 1,077 XP). QP is QuestPump's level: never translated.

kit.xp.label.paragon.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the XP bar past level 60 (Paragon 3, 1,200 of 10,000 XP).

kit.xp.label.paragon.rested.note: The same with rested XP (Paragon 3, 1,200 of 10,000 XP, 400 rested); "rested" describes the XP.

kit.xp.label.rested.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the XP bar with rested XP (QP 12, 340 of 1,077 XP, 120 rested). QP is QuestPump's level: never translated. "rested" describes the XP and takes no plural form.

kit.xp.progress.note: Under the XP bar: the XP gathered in this level over the XP the level needs (775 / 1,077).

ladders.card.behind.computer.text: On this computer your {ladder} is at step {n}; your game is ahead.
ladders.card.behind.computer.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: the Book shows the game's sheet, which stands higher on this ladder than this computer's own pumps. {ladder} is the ladder's name (Push-up), {n} that step on the one 1-14 scale (3); the Start trains that step.

ladders.card.behind.phone.text: On this phone your {ladder} is at step {n}; your game is ahead.
ladders.card.behind.phone.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: the Book shows the game's sheet, which stands higher on this ladder than this phone's own pumps. {ladder} is the ladder's name (Push-up), {n} that step on the one 1-14 scale (3); the Start trains that step. Android's; the iPhone's is ladders.card.behind.phone.ios (2026-10-15).

ladders.card.behind.phone.ios.text: On this {device} your {ladder} is at step {n}; your game is ahead.
ladders.card.behind.phone.ios.note: The iPhone's twin of ladders.card.behind.phone. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

ladders.card.best.note: Under a counted cardio step's measure on its card (slice 42): the shown form's best clean count.

ladders.card.check.note: Caps label over a step card's check rows (slice 42): a pose of the Flexibility tree answered at its goal pose once, which a move or the climb waits for.

ladders.card.check.done.note: A check row done (slice 42): {date} the game day the check was passed, day and short month (16 Oct).

ladders.card.check.done.step.note: A check row done with no answer that did it, by a stretch ladder's own climb (slice 42): {ladder} the stretch ladder of the choice that is done, the shown one where it is (Ankle), {n} its step now.

ladders.card.check.line.text: Hold this pose once at Good or better to unlock {move}.
ladders.card.check.line.note: Under an undone check row, and beside the Do the check Start of a card or a move's window or page (slice 42): {move} the move the check opens (Pistol, hands on the desk).

ladders.card.check.line.perfect.text: One Perfect hold at its goal pose opens {move}.

ladders.card.check.line.step.text: One hold at its goal pose opens the climb to step {n}.
ladders.card.check.line.step.note: ladders.card.check.line where the check gates the climb (the rung's need, slice 42): {n} the next step on the one 1-14 scale (7).

ladders.card.check.line.step.perfect.text: One Perfect hold at its goal pose opens the climb to step {n}.

ladders.card.check.need.note: A check row (slice 42): {move} the pose (Deep squat at the desk, heels flat), answered Good or Perfect once. On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.card.check.need.perfect.note: A check row where only Perfect passes (ns.MarkNeeds, slice 42): {move} the pose (Wrist lean). On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.card.clean.text: {count} clean days of {seconds} s all out
ladders.card.clean.note: A counted cardio step's measure and limit on its card (slice 42): {count} the clean days its climb takes (3, 4, 5 or 6: Constants.lua cardio_clean_days), {seconds} the window (library constants countS, 30).

ladders.card.day.text: Today already counts toward the next step.
ladders.card.day.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: the climb's day at the top already counted this session; the next set counts toward it again in a later session.

ladders.card.day.next.text: Your next set counts toward the climb from {time}.
ladders.card.day.next.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: no set counts toward the climb again before the next game day (a pose held today, a timed cardio step's moves done today): {time} is that day's start, a time of day (04:00).

ladders.card.earn.text: One fresh set of {earn} earns this step's colour.
ladders.card.earn.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: on an orange (Legendary) or gold (Artifact) step this set can earn now, the count of a fresh set that earns its colour, its range's floor (3 fresh earns it., a hold's 0:20 fresh earns it.). {earn} is a count of reps or a hold's time.

ladders.card.earn.fresh.text: Fresh again at {time}. Then one set of {earn} earns its colour.
ladders.card.earn.fresh.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: on an orange or gold step to earn whose set is not fresh yet: from {time}, a time of day (08:00), a set of {earn} earns it (Fresh again at 08:00: then 3 earns it.). {earn} is a count of reps or a hold's time.

ladders.card.earn.from.text: From {time}, a Perfect hold earns it.
ladders.card.earn.from.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: on a pose's orange step whose pose was held today: from {time}, the next game day's start (04:00), a Perfect hold earns it.

ladders.card.earn.mark.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: on a pose's orange step: the pose held its whole time and answered Perfect to How close to the goal pose? earns its colour.

ladders.card.foot.note: Caps label of the pinned foot of a step's card, a move's window and a move's page on a step ahead or a kept step: over one row of the player's own step's tile beside the climb's Start, so the step's figure above never stands over another move's button.

ladders.card.foot.own.note: Caps label of the To get here block on the player's own step's card (the step now or the ladder's top), on both phones and the computer, where its Start trains another move than the step's (its proof, an easier move stepped down to, a place start): over one row of that move's tile beside the Start, in the card's pinned foot. On a step ahead or a kept step, and in a move's window or page, the same row reads ladders.card.foot (To get here). The game's card says the same in its own key (tree.card.trainWith).

ladders.card.footer.note: The share card's last line: the character's name and the ladder (Tester · Push).

ladders.card.forecast.note: Pro's date on a step's card (slice 52): when the step's climb may come at the player's own pace, half to twice the Stamina Ledger's middle, {span} a length of ladders.path.span.* (4–16 days, 2–6 weeks); beside a timed cardio step's Full moves (the next step), a hold ladder's top days (its window's top) and, once its path is in, a counted step's clean days. With Pro only, nothing while the player's rise (on a counted step its clean days per play day) is not known yet, never on a counted set's Ready view. A guess in game days, never a promise.

ladders.card.fresh.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: the move was trained lately, so its goal is lighter now: from {time}, a time of day (08:00), a fresh set asks for a record again (docs/safety.md hazard 1's fresh line).

ladders.card.full.note: A row's label on a timed cardio step's card (slice 52), its value ladders.card.full.value: the full moves toward the next step. A full move is a session with a Yes on a steady move dosed at the player's own timed step while the step's dose stood at the ledger's top (M 1500) that ran the full 45 s, by its dose or Keep going's (a 30-s Start from the card counts none until Keep going runs it to 45 s); two climb the step.

ladders.card.full.value.note: The Full moves row's value (slice 52): {have} of the {need} full moves the climb takes (cardio_full_days, 2: 1 of 2). Since 2026-10-29 also the count at the end of the climb's line under To step up on Android and the computer, beside its DayPips: {have} of the {need} days.

ladders.card.gear.note: A line in the quiet part of a step's card, as the game's ladder tooltip says it: one more piece of equipment, {gear} as Your setup names it (Pull-up bar), would open {count} more moves on this ladder, the hardest of them of the quality {quality} (Epic).

ladders.card.group.main.note: Caps label of a step's card (StepCard, on the phones and the computer, slice 42): the first of its three groups, the step's anchor or the move standing in for it under the player's setup. Since 2026-10-29 on Android only where the move stands in for the anchor or waits for a step or a check, the climb's line under To step up.

ladders.card.group.master.note: Caps label of a step card's mastery (StepCard, 2026-10-29; slice 42's Mastered, a reward, never a gate) over its progress row, ladders.card.master.count with its pips, on a step the player has before it is mastered; once mastered the card says ladders.step.mastered alone.

ladders.card.group.same.note: Caps label of a step's card (slice 42): the third group, the step's other moves (variety, other muscles, gear versions), never required for the next step, which its name says (Same level until 2026-10-22, with a line under it).

ladders.card.group.same.more.note: The For variety group folded where the card's face has no room (slice 42): {count} is the moves in it; a tap unfolds it. Since 2026-10-29 on Android and the computer the folded row stands without the group's caps label over it, which it names already; the label comes back as the group unfolds.

ladders.card.group.then.note: Caps label of a step's card (slice 42): the second group, the moves the climb to the next step waits for after the main move, in order (the rung's path: ns.Stages), each a stage row. Since 2026-10-29 on Android and the computer only over a step above the player's own path: on the player's step its stages stand under To step up (ladders.card.group.up).

ladders.card.group.up.note: Caps label of a step's card on the player's own step (StepCard, 2026-10-29): what opens the next step as one checklist, the climb's line with its days (its pips and ladders.card.full.value's count), the path's stages, each step of another ladder and each stretch check the climb waits for. It took the place of ladders.card.group.then on the player's step, and of the climb's line under ladders.card.group.main.

ladders.card.haul.note: A button beside Start on the cardio step's card (slice 55): one steady move of the step's steady form, the card's own pick, for {time} (1:30, later 2:00, 2:30 and 3:00: long_haul_s) at a pace too fast for full sentences, run only from here, never in a quest's pump. Long Haul is the move's name, a game word.

ladders.card.hint.note: A move's soft need, never a gate (slice 42): {move} the pose that helps (Downward dog), a button to its move window; the move's own advice under it where the library gives one.

ladders.card.main.standin.text: {move} replaces {anchor} for your equipment and settings.
ladders.card.main.standin.note: Under the main move of a step's card when the setup leaves the step's anchor out (slice 42): {move} the move standing in for it (Pistol, hands on the desk), {anchor} the anchor (Bulgarian split squat).

ladders.card.master.count.note: The progress row under Master this step (StepCard, 2026-10-29), with its pips: {have} of the {need} moves the setup offers on the step at their top once (ns.MasteryLeft), the main move among them. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text, as ladders.step.mastery's. The iPhone's card still says ladders.step.mastery (owed).

ladders.card.more.note: The folded part of a step's card on the phone, a row that opens and folds it: the step's other moves, what it opens on other ladders, the ladder's top, the weight and equipment lines and Ladder page.

ladders.card.need.or.note: A need row of a step's card whose need is an any group (slice 42): its alternatives joined, each in ladders.tree.chip's words (Pull-up · step 8 · Strength, or One-arm towel row · step 8 · Strength); done when one is.

ladders.card.now.note: A row's label on the step card of a hold ladder (the wall sit, the core, the side, the L-sit) and of power (slice 52), beside the step's days at its top, its value ladders.card.now.value: what the Stamina Ledger reckons the player can do now.

ladders.card.now.value.note: The Now row's value (slice 52): the range the Stamina Ledger puts the player's hold in now, {low} to {high}, each a hold's time as the card shows a hold (2:44-3:45; the game's 164-225 s), or power's reps (12-16). Since 2026-10-29 also the value of a step card's Range cell (ladders.card.stat.range): the step's range, {low} to {high}.

ladders.card.opens.note: Caps label in the quiet part of a step's card over the steps of other ladders that this step opens, each a button (ladders.tree.chip's words) that selects that step.

ladders.card.pace.note: A row's label on a timed cardio step's card (slice 52, the Stamina Ledger), its value ladders.card.pace.value: the steady move a full quest gives the player now on that step.

ladders.card.pace.value.note: The Pace row's value (slice 52): {seconds} the seconds of the step's steady move a full quest gives the player now (the ledger's dose), {full} the full move's 45 s (38 of 45 s).

ladders.card.page.note: A row in the quiet part of a step's card (on a phone only on a card of another open ladder than the page it stands over, reached through a waits row or a This step opens row, or over Book's list): opens that ladder's own page (its Share, its Path, Pro's chart and Start this ladder over), the card closed first.

ladders.card.quality.note: The share card's line under the figure: the move's quality word and its step of fourteen (Uncommon · step 5).

ladders.card.range.note: The measure of a step's card (StepCard, on the phones and the computer) while the player has no record of the step's move: its range, {low} to {high} (Range 20-30; a hold's as clock times), on every step whose limit is a range. With a record the card shows ladders.measure.record instead. Since 2026-10-29 on the iPhone's card alone: Android's and the computer's show the stat strip's Range cell (ladders.card.stat.range) in its place.

ladders.card.reps.note: Under the record's number on the share card: repetitions.

ladders.card.stage.clean.note: A stage row of the cardio ladder's card (slice 42): {move} the form, or its alternatives joined by ladders.card.stage.or (Squat thrusts or sprawls), {have} of the {need} clean days of the step's own forms the stage takes (1 of 2). Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers.

ladders.card.stage.done.note: Read by VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's screen reader after a stage row that is done (slice 42): its move at its top on the stage's days, or skipped. Lower case: it follows the row's words.

ladders.card.stage.mark.note: A stage row of a step's card whose move is a pose (slice 42): {move} the pose (Wheel, hands on books), {days} the game days answered close enough to its goal pose (Perfect or Good) the stage takes (2). A strength or hold stage reads ladders.path.need.

ladders.card.stage.mark.perfect.note: ladders.card.stage.mark where only Perfect counts a day (ns.MarkNeeds, slice 42): {days} the game days answered Perfect the stage takes.

ladders.card.stage.open.note: Read by a screen reader after a stage row that is open and not done (slice 42): {have} of the {need} game days at its top. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers.

ladders.card.stage.opens.note: A stage row's line, and a move window's or page's, while the move is not open yet (ns.MoveOpen, slice 42): {move} the move whose top opens it (Bulgarian split squat), {goal} that top in its own unit with a loaded move's weight (25 a side, 12, 0:30, 20 with 15 kg or more: ladders.goal.load). The Start beside it runs that move at its own goal. On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.card.stage.opens.mark.note: ladders.card.stage.opens where the move that opens it is a pose answered Good or better once (slice 42): {move} that pose (Deep squat). On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.card.stage.opens.perfect.text: Opens after your first Perfect day of {move}
ladders.card.stage.opens.perfect.note: ladders.card.stage.opens where the pose that opens it must be answered Perfect once (slice 42): {move} that pose (Crow prep). On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.card.stage.or.note: A stage of two alternatives the setup offers (slice 42), their names joined (Pistol, hands on the desk or Ring-assisted pistol), both tiles shown.

ladders.card.stage.side.note: ladders.card.stage.opens' {goal} for an opening move done on each side (slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17; the game's tree.stage.side): {goal} its top in its own unit (25), so the line reads Opens after Bulgarian split squat at 25 a side. On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.card.stage.skip.off.note: A stage row the player's own list skips (Include in pumps off; slice 42), under its move's name; a row to that move's Include in pumps under it.

ladders.card.stage.skip.setup.note: A stage row the setup skips, every move of it shut (slice 42), under its move's name; a row to Your setup under it.

ladders.card.stage.skipped.note: Read by a screen reader after a stage row the setup or the player's own list skips (slice 42), before its skip line.

ladders.card.stage.waits.note: Read by a screen reader after a stage row still waiting for the move before it (slice 42), before its Opens after line.

ladders.card.stat.range.note: Caps name of a cell of a step card's stat strip (StepCard, 2026-10-29: the record, the range and the stars as labelled cells in place of one run-on line): the step's range for its move, its value ladders.card.now.value (10-40; a hold's as clock times), the top of which on two game days opens the next step. The iPhone's card still says ladders.card.range (owed).

ladders.card.stat.stars.note: Caps name of the stat strip's stars cell on the player's own step's card (StepCard, 2026-10-29), under its RungStars (read as kit.stars.label).

ladders.card.step.note: Button in a step's card on the computer while it shows another move of the step in its place (with that move's own Start): back to the step's own card.

ladders.card.tired.text: Records come back when you are fresh.
ladders.card.tired.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: after two sets on this ladder in one game day (the game's tip.muscle.fresh).

ladders.card.top.note: A line in the quiet part of a step's card: the ladder's last step, its limit. {move} is that step's move (One-arm push-up), {quality} its quality word (Artifact). Top step is the game's own word (ladders.bar.top).

ladders.card.topped.note: Read by a screen reader after a move in a step card's groups that reached its top once (MoveTile's topped mark, slice 42); nothing before its top. Lower case: it follows the move's name.

ladders.card.unlock.note: The unlock card's line: the move and its quality word (Archer push-up · Rare).

ladders.card.unlocked.note: The unlock card's heading, over the move's pose in its quality's edge.

ladders.card.up.clean.note: A counted cardio climb's row label under To step up on the player's own step (2026-10-29, Android and the computer), as Full moves is a timed one's: its count (ladders.card.full.value: 1 of 3) and DayPips at the row's end, in place of ladders.step.next.clean's sentence, which said the count twice beside them.

ladders.card.up.next.note: A strength climb's row under To step up on the player's own step (2026-10-29, Android and the computer): ladders.step.next's words with no "Next:" and no full stop, the group's label saying it already; its count (ladders.card.full.value) and DayPips at the row's end. {move} the move standing for the step, {goal} the top of its range with a plus (25+, 0:45+), {days} the game days at the top it takes.

ladders.card.via.pose.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window, the Tooltip's line and the tree's ladder line for a family whose opening waits for a pose's goal pose answered Good or better (slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17): {ladder} the family (Planche), {move} the pose. In place of ladders.card.via.step, whose step of the pose's own ladder every player already has.

ladders.card.via.pose.perfect.note: ladders.card.via.pose where only Perfect opens it: Planche opens at a Perfect Wrist lean.

ladders.card.via.record.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: on a ladder not open yet, whose Start climbs the ladder that opens it: {ladder} is the ladder that opens (Handstand), {move} the move whose record opens it (Push-up), {count} that record, a count of reps (15) or a hold's time (0:30). Also the Tooltip's line and the tree's ladder line for that ladder's column on a talent tree (the phones' and the computer's).

ladders.card.via.step.note: The line beside the Start of a step's card (StepCard) or a move's window: on a ladder not open yet that opens at another ladder's step: {ladder} is the ladder that opens (Power), {opener} the ladder whose step opens it (Cardio), {n} that step on the one 1-14 scale (5). Also the Tooltip's line and the tree's ladder line for that ladder's column on a talent tree (the phones' and the computer's). A ladder that waits for a pose's goal pose says ladders.card.via.pose (or .pose.perfect) instead (slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17).

ladders.card.weight.note: A line in the quiet part of a step's card on a move done with a weight, as the game's ladder tooltip says it: {best} the weighted record, {last} the last set, each a weight and its reps (kit.record.load: 10 kg × 20).

ladders.chart.counts.note: Chart legend: the dots, every count the player typed for the move.

ladders.chart.record.title.note: Chart title and its name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: the move's record over time with every count the player typed for it (Push-up: record and counts).

ladders.chart.rung.note: The chart's name for VoiceOver and TalkBack: Push: step over time.

ladders.chart.rung.label.note: A rung on the chart's axis: its number and its quality's word (3 Rare).

ladders.chart.rung.title.note: Chart title: the ladder's step by date.

ladders.chart.rung.word.note: A step with its quality, as the values list, a scrub and TalkBack read it: Step 3, Rare.

ladders.colours.note: Section label over Book's card of the qualities: how many ladders reach each colour. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.colours.count.note: A cell of Book's colour card: {have} ladders reached this quality, of {total} that can (5/21). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.colours.mastered.note: Under the qualities in the Book's colour card, from the first mastered step (slice 42): {count} steps where every move the setup offers reached its top (ns.MasteredCount); the game's Deeds row says the same. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.colours.spoken.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for a cell of Book's colour card (Uncommon, 5 of 21 ladders): {quality} is the quality's word, {have} the ladders that reached it, {total} the ladders that can. {have} comes formatted (one counted number a plural: Xcode infers the plural's argument only then). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.detail.pro.text: Your steps, records and counts over time come with QuestPump Pro.
ladders.detail.pro.note: A ladder's detail without Pro: its charts come with the subscription. A count is the number the player typed after a move. QuestPump Pro is a product name.

ladders.detail.restart.note: Row (destructive) at the foot of a ladder's page, on the strength and hold ladders (never cardio or a pose family, which keeps no record): it opens a confirmation before the ladder starts over (2026-10-08).

ladders.detail.restart.body.text: Its moves' records and its unlocked colours go, and you go back to its start. Your next set finds your step again. Your pumps, your XP and your other ladders stay. The game starts it over too the next time it loads.
ladders.detail.restart.body.note: Body of that confirmation: the ladder's records, rung and kept colours go and its next set places it again; pumps, XP and the other ladders stay; the game takes it when it next loads its save.

ladders.detail.restart.confirm.note: Button (destructive) in that confirmation: the ladder starts over.

ladders.detail.restart.title.note: Title of the confirmation before a ladder starts over: {ladder} is the ladder's name (L-sit).

ladders.favourites.none.note: Heading of Book's Moves when the Favourites filter is chosen, nothing is typed and no move is a favourite yet.

ladders.filter.all.note: A filter chip over Book's moves: every move.

ladders.filter.favourites.note: A filter chip over Book's moves: the moves the player marked as favourite.

ladders.filter.showall.note: The button under ladders.favourites.none and ladders.untrained.none: it chooses the All filter.

ladders.goal.load.note: A loaded move's top as its climb asks it (2026-10-12: a set with a lighter weight counts no day toward the next step), in place of the plain goal in ladders.step.next and ladders.path.need: {goal} the top as a goal with a plus (20+), {kg} the least weight in whole kg (15). The game says it alike (amount.climb). Also in a talent tree's Next line on the phones and the computer, and since 2026-10-19 (the double-check's fix review) in the {goal} of an opener's line (ladders.card.stage.opens, ladders.held.opens) on every surface, there with the plain top (20), as the game's Sheet.ClimbTop.

ladders.goal.load.each.text: {goal} with {kg} kg or more in each hand
ladders.goal.load.each.note: As ladders.goal.load, for a move done with a weight in each hand: {kg} is each hand's least weight in whole kg (5). The game says it alike (amount.climbEach). Also in a talent tree's Next line on the phones and the computer, and in an opener's line (ladders.card.stage.opens, ladders.held.opens) with the plain top.

ladders.held.check.text: Opens after your first Good hold of {move}.
ladders.held.check.note: What holds the path's next move where its own stretch check waits: {move} the check's pose (Deep squat at the desk, heels flat), held at its goal pose and answered Good or better once. The {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review), a whole sentence with its own full stop; the step card's row says the same without one (ladders.card.check.need), which stays a fragment there.

ladders.held.check.perfect.text: Opens after your first Perfect hold of {move}.
ladders.held.check.perfect.note: ladders.held.check where only Perfect passes the check (ns.MarkNeeds): {move} the pose (Wrist lean). The {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review), a whole sentence with its own full stop; the step card's row says the same without one (ladders.card.check.need.perfect), which stays a fragment there.

ladders.held.opens.note: What holds the path's next move where its stage waits for another move's top: {move} that move (Bulgarian split squat), {goal} its top in its own unit with a loaded move's weight (25 a side, 12, 0:30, 20 with 15 kg or more: ladders.goal.load). The {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review), a whole sentence with its own full stop; the step card's row says the same without one (ladders.card.stage.opens), which stays a fragment there.

ladders.held.opens.mark.text: Opens after your first Good day of {move}.
ladders.held.opens.mark.note: ladders.held.opens where the move that opens the stage is a pose answered Good or better once: {move} that pose (Deep squat). The {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review), a whole sentence with its own full stop; the step card's row says the same without one (ladders.card.stage.opens.mark), which stays a fragment there.

ladders.held.opens.perfect.text: Opens after your first Perfect day of {move}.
ladders.held.opens.perfect.note: ladders.held.opens where the pose that opens the stage must be answered Perfect once: {move} that pose (Crow prep). The {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review), a whole sentence with its own full stop; the step card's row says the same without one (ladders.card.stage.opens.perfect), which stays a fragment there.

ladders.hold.note: Caps label over a pose's hold time (0:30) where a ladder of poses shows it in the record's place.

ladders.hover.step.note: Line 2 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer (a phone's long press, the computer's pointer or keyboard focus): {quality} its quality word (Uncommon), {n} its step on the one 1-14 scale (5), {standing} where the player stands (ladders.standing.*: Uncommon · step 5 · your step). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.hover.tap.text: Tap for its card and Start
ladders.hover.tap.note: Line 4 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on a phone (a long press shows it), an instruction line: what a tap does while the step's card has a Start that can run. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.hover.tap.nostart.note: Line 4 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on a phone, an instruction line: what a tap does while the card's Start cannot run (refused, or pumps rest after feeling unwell). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.journal.also.list.note: The muscles the move works less: {muscles} is a list (Abs and Obliques), in the phone's list style.

ladders.journal.clear.note: Row (destructive) on a move's page under its record, shown only while the move has one: it opens a confirmation before the record goes (2026-10-08: a clear row, one move's record cleared on every device and in the game).

ladders.journal.clear.body.text: Your next set of it is a max set again. Your pumps, your XP and your ladder stay. The game clears it too the next time it loads.
ladders.journal.clear.body.note: Body of that confirmation: what goes (the record, so the next set is a max set to find the player's level again) and what stays; the game takes the clear when it next loads its save (the helper's mirror).

ladders.journal.clear.confirm.note: Button (destructive) in that confirmation: the move's record goes.

ladders.journal.clear.title.note: Title of the confirmation before one move's record is cleared: {move} is the move's name (Tuck L-sit).

ladders.journal.correct.note: Row on a move's page under its record, above Clear this record (slice 44): it opens the window that sets one saved set of the last 14 game days right, as if it had been typed right (a count, a hold's seconds, a set's weight, a pose's answer), on every device and in the game. Shown on a move whose sets can be corrected once it has a record or a recent set; disabled while a pump runs.

ladders.journal.how.note: Section label on a move's page over the steps of the move.

ladders.journal.last.note: A row on a move's page: the count or the time the player typed last time.

ladders.journal.stat.note: What a record on a counted move raises: {stat} is the stat's name (Strength).

ladders.journal.stat.learn.note: What a move with no count to beat (a stretch, a timed cardio move) raises as the player comes to know it: {stat} is the stat's name (Spirit).

ladders.journal.trains.note: Section label on a move's page over the muscles it works.

ladders.journal.you.note: Section label on a move's page over the player's own numbers for it.

ladders.mark.note: Caps label over a pose's goal pose (the code's mark): the sentence that says what the full pose looks like, which How close to the goal pose? asks about; on the ladder pages and over the sentence on the ask itself (2026-10-14, David: "the 'mark' (please rename for clarity)").

ladders.mark.days.note: Under a pose's mark: the game days toward the next step at this step (ns.PoseNeeds' have: a goal pose of the step answered How close to the goal pose? close enough, Perfect or Good, Perfect alone below a risky step; it reaches {total} only once the main pose's and the Perfect days are in too), of the days that open the next step (Days close enough: 2 of 3). Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.mark.days.perfect.note: Under a pose's goal pose where only Perfect counts a day toward the next step (a harder pose ahead, ns.MarkNeeds, the climb's ask): the game days toward the next step at this step (ns.PoseNeeds' have: a goal pose of the step answered How close to the goal pose? Perfect; it reaches {total} only once two of them are on the main pose), of the days that open it (Perfect days: 2 of 3). On the player's step's card on both phones, under its goal pose (which the card leaves out where the climb's line names it, E24), and under the goal pose in a ladder page's hero on both phones and the computer. The close-enough form is ladders.mark.days. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.measure.ahead.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a step ahead: {move} is the move of the step before it (Opens after Feet-elevated push-up). Since slice 42 also a waiting stage's line on a step's card, and a waiting move's in a move window and on a move's page, where the move that opens it has no top in a count (a cardio form's clean window; ladders.card.stage.opens names a strength or hold top), on the phones and in the computer's card. On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet.

ladders.measure.clean.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip and its spoken key line: the player's counted cardio step (slice 42), {have} of {need} clean days. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text.

ladders.measure.counteddays.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a strength or hold step whose record reached its window's top: {have} of the {need} game days at the top (a counted cardio step's from purple until slice 42, which counts clean days since, ladders.measure.clean).  Plural on the day count (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check: "0 of 1 days" after a step down); {have} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers.

ladders.measure.first.text: Your first max set finds your step
ladders.measure.first.note: The measure of a step's card (StepCard) and line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer: a strength, hold or counted cardio step with no record and no day yet, in place of the record (on a phone's card under the step's range, ladders.card.range, or a counted step's forms at their tops), never 0 %.

ladders.measure.full.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip and its spoken key line: the player's timed cardio step (steps 1-4; slice 52's full moves in place of slice 42's ready days), {have} of {need} full moves. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text.

ladders.measure.held.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the player's step while its climb is shut below the top (the next step waits for another ladder's, the setup shuts it, or the move is left out): its record on its range (ladders.measure.record, or its spoken form) then what holds the climb ({holds}: Waits for a record of 8 on Pull-up.), as the game's tree.key.held; with no record the hold alone.

ladders.measure.kept.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a kept step (reached before a step down) right above the player's step: {move} at its top {goal} on {days} game days brings it back (Comes back at Push-up 30+ on 1 day).

ladders.measure.kept.after.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a kept step higher up: {move} is the move of the step before it.

ladders.measure.kept.clean.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip: a kept step right above the player's counted cardio step comes back at that step's clean days (slice 42; a cardio climb back takes the same days as the climb).

ladders.measure.kept.full.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip: a kept step right above the player's timed cardio step comes back at its full moves (slice 52).

ladders.measure.kept.mark.text: Comes back after any goal pose is close enough on {days} days

plural.one: Comes back after any goal pose is close enough on {days} day
plural.other: Comes back after any goal pose is close enough on {days} days

ladders.measure.kept.mark.note: A pose family's climb back: any goal pose of the step below close enough to its goal pose on {days} days (tree.key.backPose). A kept step right above the player's (a step reached before a step down), line 3 of its Tooltip on the phones and the computer, as the game's tree.key.back* (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check); the strength and counted-days forms are ladders.measure.kept. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.measure.kept.perfect.text: Comes back after any goal pose is Perfect on {count} days

plural.one: Comes back after any goal pose is Perfect on {count} day
plural.other: Comes back after any goal pose is Perfect on {count} days

ladders.measure.kept.perfect.note: A pose family's climb back where only Perfect counts: any goal pose of the step below Perfect on {count} days (tree.key.backPerfect). A kept step right above the player's (a step reached before a step down), line 3 of its Tooltip on the phones and the computer, as the game's tree.key.back* (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check); the strength and counted-days forms are ladders.measure.kept. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.measure.left.text: {left} more to the top, then {days} days there

plural.one: {left} more to the top, then {days} day there
plural.other: {left} more to the top, then {days} days there

ladders.measure.left.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: the player's step past half its range: {left} more to its top (3, a hold's 0:05), then {days} game days at the top (3 to go, then 2 days).

ladders.measure.next.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: the next step: {move} is the move standing for the player's step (Push-up), {goal} its top with a plus (30+), {days} the game days at that top (Opens at Push-up 30+ on 2 days); with a path ladders.measure.next.path, a counted cardio step ladders.measure.next.clean (slice 42).

ladders.measure.next.clean.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip: the next step above a counted cardio step (slice 42).

ladders.measure.next.full.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip: the next step above a timed cardio step (slice 52).

ladders.measure.next.mark.text: Opens after any goal pose is close enough on {days} days

plural.one: Opens after any goal pose is close enough on {days} day
plural.other: Opens after any goal pose is close enough on {days} days

ladders.measure.next.mark.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a pose family's next step: any goal pose of the step below answered close enough to its goal pose (Perfect or Good) on {days} game days (Opens after any goal pose is close enough on 3 days; the game's tree.key.nextPose). Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.measure.next.path.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip: the next step whose climb also waits for its path (slice 42, in place of a proof): {move} at {goal} on {days} game days (2, or 3 on a tendon-heavy move: a next step never takes 1, a climb back reading ladders.measure.kept), then {count} stages of the path. Plural on {count}; {days} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers.
ladders.measure.next.path.text: Opens at {move} {goal} on {days} days, plus {count} more moves at their top

plural.one: Opens at {move} {goal} on {days} days, plus {count} more move at its top
plural.other: Opens at {move} {goal} on {days} days, plus {count} more moves at their top

ladders.measure.next.perfect.text: Opens after any goal pose is Perfect on {count} days

plural.one: Opens after any goal pose is Perfect on {count} day
plural.other: Opens after any goal pose is Perfect on {count} days

ladders.measure.next.perfect.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a pose family's next step that counts only Perfect answers: any goal pose of the step below answered Perfect on {count} game days (Opens after any goal pose is Perfect on 3 days; the game's tree.key.nextPerfect). Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.measure.notplaced.text: Your first max set shows where you start
ladders.measure.notplaced.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a ladder not placed yet.

ladders.measure.perfect.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, the key line in the step's own measure: a pose step whose next step counts only Perfect answers to How close to the goal pose?: {have} of {need} game days toward it (0 of 3 Perfect days; ns.PoseNeeds' have, which reaches {need} only once two of them are on the main pose).  Plural on the day count (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check: "0 of 1 days" after a step down); {have} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.measure.placing.text: Your next set shows where you start again
ladders.measure.placing.note: The measure of a step's card (StepCard) and line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer: a strength ladder back from a break, whose next set finds the player's step again (the cardio ladder's says ladders.measure.placing.window or .steady since 2026-10-24).

ladders.measure.placing.steady.text: Your next steady move finds your step again
ladders.measure.placing.steady.note: The measure of a step's card (StepCard) and line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, in ladders.measure.placing's place on the cardio ladder back from a break below closing_rung (steps 1-4), whose step a steady move at it measures again (its pace ask's answer, or a stop; the tree entry's placingBy, DB.lua cardioMeasure). The game's tree.key.placingSteady and tree.card.placingSteady (2026-10-24, the double-check of slices 52-55).

ladders.measure.placing.window.text: Your next 30-s all-out set finds your step again
ladders.measure.placing.window.note: The measure of a step's card (StepCard) and line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer, in ladders.measure.placing's place on the cardio ladder back from a break whose step its all-out window measures again (from closing_rung, step 5, where every pump closes on one; the tree entry's placingBy, DB.lua cardioMeasure: a steady move there measures nothing). The game's tree.key.placingWindow and tree.card.placingWindow (2026-10-24, the double-check of slices 52-55).

ladders.measure.proof.note: Line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip, and a ladder page's next row, on the phones and the computer: the player's step with its days in while a stage of its path is left, the move the climb's turn runs (slice 42, the proof until then; ns.PathNext, the move ns.PathTurn runs, as the step's Start runs it, since the double-check's fix review, 2026-10-19, the first stage open and not done until then): {proof} that move (Pistol, hands on the desk), {goal} its top with a plus (8+); a pose stage's on the ladder page is ladders.measure.proof.mark (or .mark.perfect), a cardio stage's ladders.measure.proof.clean.

ladders.measure.proof.clean.note: ladders.measure.proof where the stage is a cardio form (slice 42): {proof} the form (Squat thrusts or sprawls), {have} of the {need} clean days it takes. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text.

ladders.measure.proof.held.note: ladders.measure.proof where the path's next stage names a move not open yet (2026-10-19, the program's double-check: the engine's ns.PathNext and its ports' `waits`): {proof} that move (Pistol, hands on the desk), {wait} is always a whole sentence with its own full stop, which the line adds none after and no code adds or strips (2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review; slices 49-50 translate it whole): a stage's opener (ladders.held.opens: Opens after Bulgarian split squat at 25 a side., and its .mark and .perfect forms), the move's own stretch check (ladders.held.check: Opens after your first Good hold of Deep squat., and ladders.held.check.perfect), or another ladder's record or step (ladders.step.waits: Waits for a record of 12 on Feet-up push-up., ladders.step.waits.step). The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua tree.key.pathHeld).

ladders.measure.proof.mark.note: Slice 42 (docs/ui.md, "The step's groups, the checks, Mastered and cardio's days"): the next row of a pose ladder's page (ladders.detail) while a pose stage of its path is left after the main move's days, as ladders.measure.proof is a strength stage's: {proof} the stage's pose, answered close enough on {days} game days.

ladders.measure.proof.mark.perfect.note: Slice 42: ladders.measure.proof.mark where the stage's pose must be answered Perfect (ns.MarkNeeds).

ladders.measure.record.note: The measure of a step's card (StepCard) and line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer: a strength, hold or counted cardio step's record on its range, {low} to {high} (Record 22 · Range 20-30; a hold's as clock times), the range named as ladders.card.range names it alone (2026-10-29: a bare 10-40 beside the record read as nothing). Each is a count or a hold's time. Since 2026-10-29 Android's and the computer's step card show it as the stat strip's Record and Range cells (ladders.record.label, ladders.card.stat.range); the Tooltip's line and the iPhone's card keep it.

ladders.move.ahead.text: Ahead of your step for now
ladders.move.ahead.note: Over the figure and How to of a step ahead or a move above the player's reach in a tree's views (a step's card opened from a talent tree, a move window opened from that card), where it sits below the player's step; ladders.move.locked's words where no tree shows. It never starts on its own; the climb's Start stands in To get here. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.move.better.text: Not in pumps: your setup offers {move} instead
ladders.move.better.note: A move the pumps leave out because the player's equipment does it better: {move} is the name of the move that comes instead, such as Goblet squat.

ladders.move.favourite.note: Switch in a move's window and on its page: on, the pumps give this move first among the moves they may give.

ladders.move.include.note: Switch in a move's window: on, the pumps may give the move; off, they leave it out. On Your moves, what the switch of each move the player left out does, as the screen reader's hint after the move's name (a line under the name until 2026-10-22).

ladders.move.locked.note: Over the figure and How to of a move above the player's reach where no tree shows (a move's window from Book's Moves, a move's page, a step's card opened from a ladder's page or the list: the next step, a step ahead and a family not open yet's steps whose own move its Start does not run): it opens as the player climbs, and never starts on its own; the climb's Start stands in To get here. In a tree's views ladders.move.ahead says it (2026-10-14: the figure in place of the locked tile).

ladders.move.open.note: A row in a move's window: it opens the move's own page.

ladders.move.path.note: A row in a move's window on a phone (Book's Moves, a step card's Other moves): it closes the window and opens the path of the ladder the move stands on, scrolled to its step (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"). None for a move no ladder holds. The iPhone's trees say Show in tree (ladders.move.tree) until its twin lands.

ladders.move.setup.gear.note: Under the Include in pumps switch (off and greyed) in a move's window and on its page, and on a ladder's shut step (with a chevron to Your setup), when the move needs equipment the player has not added. {gear} is the equipment's name as Your setup lists it (Kettlebell). Your setup is the name of the page in the Menu where the player adds it; the row under this line opens it. On Your moves, the same line in place of Include in pumps under a move the player switched back on while it still needs equipment the player has not added (no row to Your setup there).

ladders.move.setup.off.note: Under the Include in pumps switch (off and greyed) in a move's window and on its page, and on a ladder's shut step (with a chevron to Your setup), when a switch of Your setup that the move needs is off. {setting} is the switch's name as Your setup lists it (Room to move, Floor moves). Your setup is the name of the page in the Menu; the row under this line opens it. On Your moves, the same line in place of Include in pumps under a move the player switched back on while it still needs a switch of Your setup that is off (no row to Your setup there).

ladders.move.setup.on.note: Under the Include in pumps switch (off and greyed) in a move's window and on its page, and on a ladder's shut step (with a chevron to Your setup), when a switch of Your setup that rules the move out is on. {setting} is the switch's name as Your setup lists it (Quiet mode, No jumping, Avoid head-down positions). Your setup is the name of the page in the Menu; the row under this line opens it. On Your moves, the same line in place of Include in pumps under a move the player switched back on while it still is ruled out by a switch of Your setup that is on (no row to Your setup there).

ladders.move.tree.note: A row in a move's window on a phone (Book's Moves, a step card's Other moves, a ladder page's): it closes the window, shows Ladders as the move's talent tree, scrolls to the step the move stands on and selects it (a ladder that waits whole: its column). None for a move no ladder holds. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.moves.count.note: Said by VoiceOver and TalkBack about a second after the search's words or the chosen filter last changed: how many moves Book's Moves shows now (25 moves).

ladders.moves.off.note: A chip over Book's Moves: how many moves the player switched off for pumps (Include in pumps off). A tap shows only those moves; a second tap shows every move again.

ladders.moves.other.note: Section label over the moves that belong to no ladder, after the families.

ladders.next.note: SectionLabel over Pump home's embers row and the step-up closest to done of all the ladders (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"); the Book's own Up next went on 2026-11-04.

ladders.next.time.note: A hold's next goal, the least that beats the record, as a clock time with a plus for more (0:47+). Keep the plus after the time.

ladders.opens.note: In Book's list of ladders, the row of a family the player cannot train yet, in the place of its move's name, beside a lock: what opens it; on a Hero page's list of the ladders that train a muscle or raise a stat, the same family's line, in the place of its quality. {ladder} is another ladder's name as Book shows it (Cardio); {step} is a step on the one 1-14 scale every ladder shares (5). The family opens once that ladder reaches the step. A family that waits for a move's record says ladders.opens.record instead, and one that waits for a pose's goal pose ladders.opens.pose (or .pose.perfect; slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17).

ladders.opens.pose.note: A family not open yet whose opening waits for a pose's goal pose answered Good or better (an opens entry with a move and a mark; slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17, the game's tree.check.need): {move} the pose. In place of ladders.opens, whose step of the pose's own ladder every player already has.

ladders.opens.pose.perfect.note: ladders.opens.pose where only Perfect opens it (the game's tree.check.needPerfect): {move} the pose (the planche's Wrist lean, after its Push-up record of 10).

ladders.opens.record.note: In Book's list of ladders, the row of a family the player cannot train yet, in the place of its move's name, beside a lock: what opens it; on a Hero page's list of the ladders that train a muscle or raise a stat, the same family's line, in the place of its quality. {move} is a move's name as Book shows it (Push-up); {count} is the record that move needs, a count of reps (15 opens the handstand, 10 the planche) or a hold's time (0:30). The family opens once the player's record on that move reaches it (the game's own line: Opens at a Push-up record of 15).

ladders.path.note: SectionLabel over a ladder's Path under its Steps card (2026-10-09): the road from the step the player stands on to the ladder's orange (Legendary) and gold (Artifact) steps. Every player sees the goal and every step with what it takes (free since 2026-10-14, David's call with the talent trees, which show every step to every player); Pro adds the pace, and without Pro one row offers it once the ladder has one.

ladders.path.branch.note: A row under a step on a ladder's path (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"): a step of another ladder this step opens, {ladder} that ladder's name and {step} its step; it opens that ladder's path at the step, or the step's card where the ladder is not open yet.

ladders.path.goal.note: The Path's first row: how many steps lie between the step now and the step it leads to, {quality} that step's quality word (Legendary, else the ladder's top: Artifact, or Rare on the wall sit). The row's second line names that step's move.

ladders.path.need.note: Under a step of a strength ladder's Path: what reaching it takes; and since slice 42 a strength or hold stage's row in a step card's Then, for the next step. {move} is the move standing for the step under it (or the stage's move), {goal} the top of its range as a goal with a plus (25+, a hold's 0:45+), {days} the game days at that top (2, or 3 on a tendon-heavy move). One day where a climb back takes it (return_days, 2026-10-15: "on 1 days" read wrong).

ladders.path.need.clean.note: The Path's need of a counted cardio step (slice 42): its clean days.

ladders.path.need.full.note: The Path's need of a timed cardio step (steps 1-4, slice 52): its full moves (cardio_full_days, 2).

ladders.path.need.mark.text: Rate any goal pose of the step below Good or Perfect on {days} days. Main pose's goal: {mark}
ladders.path.need.mark.note: Under a step of a pose family's Path: what reaching it takes: any goal pose of the step under it held its whole time and answered close enough to its goal pose (How close to the goal pose?: Perfect or Good) on {days} game days (3), {mark} the goal pose of that step's main pose, which one of the days must be on; the pose of the step under it alone, its mark named, until 2026-10-19. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.path.need.mark.perfect.text: Any goal pose of the step below Perfect on {days} days. Main pose's goal: {mark}
ladders.path.need.mark.perfect.note: Under a step of a pose family's Path whose pose is a harder one (head-down, a balance, or flagged skill or strain; ns.MarkNeeds): any goal pose of the step under it held its whole time and answered Perfect (How close to the goal pose?) on {days} game days opens it (3), {mark} the goal pose of that step's main pose, which two of the days must be on; the pose of the step under it alone, its mark named, until 2026-10-19. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.path.pace.note: With Pro, the Path's row under its goal once two of the ladder's climbs carry a date: how long the steps to that goal may take at the player's own pace, {span} a length such as "3–5 months" (ladders.path.span.*). A guess, never a promise (the line under it said so until 2026-10-22).

ladders.path.pro.text: Your pace to {quality} comes with QuestPump Pro.
ladders.path.pro.note: The Path's last row without Pro, once the ladder has a pace to show (two of its climbs carry a date, a day or more between two of them, and no step on the way is shut by the setup), led by Pro's helm, opening Pro's offer on the phones and Pro's page on the computer: {quality} is the quality word of the step the Path leads to. Since 2026-10-14 every step and what it takes is free, and Pro adds the pace alone. QuestPump Pro is a product name.

ladders.path.span.days.note: The Path's pace as one number of days (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's).

ladders.path.span.days.range.note: The Path's pace as a range of days (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's): {low} is always under {high}.

ladders.path.span.months.note: The Path's pace as one number of months (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's).

ladders.path.span.months.range.note: The Path's pace as a range of months (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's): {low} is always under {high}.

ladders.path.span.weeks.note: The Path's pace as one number of weeks (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's).

ladders.path.span.weeks.range.note: The Path's pace as a range of weeks (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's): {low} is always under {high}.

ladders.path.span.years.note: The Path's pace as one number of years (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's).

ladders.path.span.years.range.note: The Path's pace as a range of years (ladders.path.pace's {span}, and since slice 52 ladders.card.forecast's): {low} is always under {high}.

ladders.path.stand.note: Under the next step of the Path on a strength or hold ladder with a record: where the player stands against the top the step asks for, {record} the record of the move standing for the step now (17, a hold's 0:41). Its day pips follow it.

ladders.path.top.text: Every step of this ladder is yours.
ladders.path.top.note: The Path's one row once the player stands on the ladder's top step: no step is left above it. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer on the ladder's top step.

ladders.record.note: A move's record, the best count the player typed (record 22), on a ladder's record chart where a finger rests on it: VoiceOver's and Vico's touch label alike.

ladders.record.label.note: Label and chart legend: the move's record, the best count the player typed. Since 2026-10-29 also the caps name of the Record cell of a step card's stat strip (Android, the computer).

ladders.record.seconds.note: A hold's record in seconds (record 45 s), on a ladder's record chart where a finger rests on it, on both phones. Both forms read the same in English.

ladders.refuse.include.note: The row under a Start the player's own list refuses, which opens that move's page at its Include in pumps switch: {move} the move left out, so it never reads as the switch of the move a window shows beside it.

ladders.refuse.off.text: You left {move} out of your pumps
ladders.refuse.off.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). The player's own Include in pumps switch keeps {move} out (Ring row); its row opens that switch. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.refuse.off.too.text: You left {move} out of your pumps too
ladders.refuse.off.too.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). Under a setup line (ladders.refuse.setup.*) when the player's own Include in pumps switch keeps {move} out as well (Ring row).

ladders.refuse.other.gear.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). {ladder} is the other ladder whose step blocks the climb (Push-up), {n} that step on the one 1-14 scale (6). {gear} is the equipment as Your setup lists it (Rings or straps). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.refuse.other.off.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). {ladder} is the other ladder whose step blocks the climb (Push-up), {n} that step on the one 1-14 scale (6). {setting} is a switch's name as Your setup lists it (Room to move), which the move needs on. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.refuse.other.on.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). {ladder} is the other ladder whose step blocks the climb (Push-up), {n} that step on the one 1-14 scale (6). {setting} is a switch's name as Your setup lists it (No jumping), which leaves the move out while on. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.refuse.pain.text: Paused: you marked pain for this step
ladders.refuse.pain.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). A pain flag shuts the move the setup leaves this step; the row opens Your setup, which holds the pain switches. Start stays for a move of the ladder that spares the flagged joint.

ladders.refuse.pain.move.text: Paused: you marked pain for this move
ladders.refuse.pain.move.note: A move's window and its page where its Start is refused because a pain flag shuts the move (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens Your setup (menu.setup), which holds the pain switches.

ladders.refuse.setup.gear.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). {n} is the step that blocks, on the one 1-14 scale (6), on the way to the step or the step itself. {gear} is the equipment as Your setup lists it (Rings or straps). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.refuse.setup.off.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). {n} is the step that blocks, on the one 1-14 scale (6), on the way to the step or the step itself. {setting} is a switch's name as Your setup lists it (Room to move), which the move needs on. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.refuse.setup.on.note: A step's card where its Start is refused (no Start shows): the line, then a row that opens the page to change it (Your setup, menu.setup; that move's Include in pumps, ladders.move.include). {n} is the step that blocks, on the one 1-14 scale (6), on the way to the step or the step itself. {setting} is a switch's name as Your setup lists it (No jumping), which leaves the move out while on. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.search.note: The search field over Book's moves: its label and its prompt; since 2026-11-04 also the spoken name of the Book's round search button beside the gear, which shows Moves.

ladders.search.clear.note: The search field's clear button over Book's moves, and the button under ladders.search.none: it empties the search's words; the chosen filter stays.

ladders.search.none.note: Heading when the words typed in the search, with the chosen filter, leave no move.

ladders.segment.ladders.note: The iPhone Book's switch, first segment: the move ladders (each family's climb from easy to hard), until its unlock tracks land; Android and the computer show no switch since 2026-11-04.

ladders.segment.moves.note: The spoken name of the filters' group over the desktop app's Moves (behind the Book's search button since 2026-11-04, when the Ladders | Moves switch whose second segment this was went). On the iPhone also the Book's switch, second segment: every move the game knows, as tiles, until its unlock tracks land.

ladders.share.note: Button: shares the move's record as an image card; also the share sheet's title on Android.
