ladders.share.text.note: The text that goes with the shared record card: Push-up: 22.

ladders.share.unlock.note: The text shared with the unlock card (Unlocked: Archer push-up · Rare).

ladders.standing.ahead.note: Where the player stands on a step, the last words of the Tooltip's line 2 (ladders.hover.step), the tree's ladder line (ladders.tree.ladder) and a step's spoken name (ladders.tree.spoken), lower case: a step above the next.

ladders.standing.kept.note: Where the player stands on a step, the last words of the Tooltip's line 2 (ladders.hover.step), the tree's ladder line (ladders.tree.ladder) and a step's spoken name (ladders.tree.spoken), lower case: a step reached before a step down, above the player's step now.

ladders.standing.next.note: Where the player stands on a step, the last words of the Tooltip's line 2 (ladders.hover.step), the tree's ladder line (ladders.tree.ladder) and a step's spoken name (ladders.tree.spoken), lower case: the step above the player's.

ladders.standing.notplaced.note: Where the player stands on a step, the last words of the Tooltip's line 2 (ladders.hover.step), the tree's ladder line (ladders.tree.ladder) and a step's spoken name (ladders.tree.spoken), lower case: a ladder whose first max set has not come yet.

ladders.standing.now.note: Where the player stands on a step, the last words of the Tooltip's line 2 (ladders.hover.step), the tree's ladder line (ladders.tree.ladder) and a step's spoken name (ladders.tree.spoken), lower case: the step the player stands on.

ladders.standing.yours.note: Where the player stands on a step, the last words of the Tooltip's line 2 (ladders.hover.step), the tree's ladder line (ladders.tree.ladder) and a step's spoken name (ladders.tree.spoken), lower case: a step the player has.

ladders.start.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). The player's own step, a step they have, or a move at or under their step, at its own goal (Start Push-up · 28+). {goal} is the goal the pump will ask, with a plus (28+, a hold's 0:41+, a counted set's count 24+).

ladders.start.allout.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start for an all-out window, counted or not, with no number since slice 42 (Start Fast feet · all out, Start Jumping jacks · all out; a counted set's count goal, Start Jumping jacks · 24+, until then).

ladders.start.back.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). On a step the player had before a step down (kept): the climb back to it from their step now (Climb back with Push-up · 28+). {goal} is the goal the pump will ask, with a plus (28+, a hold's 0:41+, a counted set's count 24+).

ladders.start.back.max.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start.back for a move with no goal yet. Max set (kit.maxset's words): no goal yet, as many as you can.

ladders.start.back.plain.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start.back for a timed cardio move or a pose, which show no number.

ladders.start.check.note: The button of a step card's check row and the Start of a card or a move's window or page whose move or climb waits on a stretch check (ns.StartFor's kind check, slice 42): it opens the pose's Ready view as the check, however low its stretch ladder stands. One key for both.

ladders.start.climb.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). On the next step or a step ahead: the climb from the player's own step on that ladder, never the step's own move early; {move} is the move standing for the player's step, or the proof the climb waits for (Climb with Push-up · 28+, Climb with Close push-up · 12+). {goal} is the goal the pump will ask, with a plus (28+, a hold's 0:41+, a counted set's count 24+).

ladders.start.climb.max.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start.climb for a move with no goal yet. Max set (kit.maxset's words): no goal yet, as many as you can.

ladders.start.climb.plain.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start.climb for a timed cardio move or a pose, which show no number (Climb with Jog).

ladders.start.earn.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). Only when this set can earn an orange (Legendary) or gold (Artifact) step now (Earn Archer pull-up · 4+): {goal} is the pump's goal with a plus, never the count that earns the step, which the line beside it says (ladders.card.earn).

ladders.start.earn.max.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start.earn for a move with no goal yet, the step's move before its first record. Max set (kit.maxset's words): no goal yet, as many as you can.

ladders.start.earn.plain.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start.earn for a pose, which shows no number (Earn Wheel pose): a Perfect hold earns the step (ladders.card.earn.mark).

ladders.start.held.pump.text: Another pump is on. Finish it first.
ladders.start.held.pump.note: Pinned beside the greyed Start of a step's card or a move's window while a pump is on screen on this phone (one pump at a time): the reason it does not start.

ladders.start.max.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start for a move with no goal yet (Start One-arm push-up · Max set). Max set (kit.maxset's words): no goal yet, as many as you can.

ladders.start.place.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. On a ladder not placed yet, or back from a break: the max set that finds the player's step on it. The move it runs stands beside it (the card's Train with or To get here tile, or the window's own move) and its Ready view names it and asks the max set, so the label names neither (2026-10-29: "Find my step · Desk push-up · Max set" wrapped on a Wall push-up card and read as a third move).

ladders.start.plain.note: The one Start of a step's card (StepCard), the card's only gold button, and of a move's window and its page (slice 36's ns.StartFor); it opens the pump's Ready view with its figure and stop line, never the countdown. {move} is the move's name (Push-up). ladders.start for a timed cardio move or a pose, which show no number (Start Jog, Start Tree pose).

ladders.step.card.action.note: TalkBack's action on a step or Path row of a ladder's page and on a ladder not open yet in Book's list ("Double-tap to open its card"): it opens the step's card, with its Start.

ladders.step.card.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint on a step or Path row of a ladder's page and on a ladder not open yet in Book's list: a tap opens the step's card, with its Start. Apple's hints start with a verb in the third person.

ladders.step.earned.note: Under a step the player reached: {date} is the game day it was first reached, day and short month (3 Oct). A step once reached stays the player's (the game's ladders.step.earned). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.empty.note: A step of the scale no move of this ladder stands on. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.step.kept.note: Under a step the player reached on a day the app does not know. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.mastered.note: A step card's line on a mastered step (ns.Mastered, slice 42): {date} the game day it was mastered, day and short month (16 Oct). A reward, never a gate.

ladders.step.mastery.note: A step card's line before Mastered, on a step the player has (never a step ahead; slice 42): {have} of the {need} moves the setup offers here at their top once (ns.MasteryLeft), the main move among them. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text, since Xcode's catalog cannot number a plural with two integers. Since 2026-10-29 on the iPhone's card alone: Android's and the computer's show Master this step with ladders.card.master.count and its pips.
ladders.step.mastery.text: Mastery: {have} of {need} moves at their top

plural.one: Mastery: {have} of {need} move at its top
plural.other: Mastery: {have} of {need} moves at their top

ladders.step.next.note: Under the next step of a strength ladder: what opens it. {move} is the move that stands for the step now, {goal} the top of its range as a goal with a plus (25+, or 0:45+ for a hold, the clock the phones show a hold in), {days} the game days at the top it takes (2, or 3 on a tendon-heavy move). Its DayPips under it count the days done (the game's ladders.step.next says them in words). One day where a climb back takes it (return_days, 2026-10-15: "on 1 days" read wrong). Also a talent tree's Next line on the phones and the computer, where this climb glows.

ladders.step.next.clean.note: The climb line of a counted cardio step (slice 42), and a talent tree's Next line where it glows: {have} of the {need} clean days. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text.

ladders.step.next.full.note: The climb line of a timed cardio step (steps 1-4, slice 52), and a talent tree's Next line where it glows: {have} of the {need} full moves. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text.

ladders.step.next.mark.text: Next: rate any goal pose of your step Good or Perfect on {days} days. Main pose's goal: {mark}
ladders.step.next.mark.note: Under the next step of a pose family (yoga, stretching): any goal pose of the player's step answered close enough (How close to the goal pose?: Perfect or Good) on {days} game days opens it (3); {mark} is the goal pose of the step's main pose (Front thigh level with the floor, back knee straight, hands off the knee.), the pose its days need one day on. What the days still lack is the line under it (ladders.step.short.main, ladders.step.short.perfect, the game's Tree.PoseShort). Also a talent tree's Next line on the phones and the computer, where this climb glows. The close-enough line named the main pose's goal alone, "aiming for" it, until 2026-10-19. Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.step.next.mark.perfect.text: Next: any goal pose of your step Perfect on {days} days. Main pose's goal: {mark}
ladders.step.next.mark.perfect.note: The climb line of a pose step where only Perfect counts a day (the next pose a harder one: head-down, a balance, or flagged skill or strain; ns.MarkNeeds, the climb's ask): any goal pose of the player's step answered Perfect (How close to the goal pose?) on {days} game days opens the next step (3, two of them on the main pose); {mark} is the goal pose of the step's main pose. On both phones and the computer under a ladder page's next step and in a step card's climb, and in a talent tree's Next line too. The close-enough form is ladders.step.next.mark; the game's own line adds the days counted so far (ladders.step.nextPerfect). Since slice 47 (2026-10-19) any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day, and the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days, six until then), at least one on its main pose (pose_anchor_days; two, pose_anchor_days_risky, where only Perfect counts) and one answered Perfect (pose_perfect_days).

ladders.step.next.prove.note: The climb line of a counted cardio step whose clean days and path are in (slice 53), and a talent tree's Next line where it glows: the climb waits for one all-out window of the next step's own form, {move} (Tuck burpee), saved Yes, to the end. The first window of the next session is that form.

ladders.step.notplaced.text: Not started yet: your first max set on this ladder shows which step you start on.
ladders.step.notplaced.note: On the next step's row (the step above the one the ladder starts on) before the ladder's first max set: that first set (as many as you can) places the player on a step.

ladders.step.now.note: A chip on the ladder's step the player stands on now. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.step.off.note: Under the next step when the player's own Include in pumps switch is all that keeps its move out (switched off, or a move the pumps give only once switched on): {move} is that move. The row's chevron opens the move's page, where the switch is.

ladders.step.pain.text: Waits while a pain flag is set on this ladder.
ladders.step.pain.note: Under the next step while a joint the ladder loads is flagged as hurting: no climb until the flag is cleared. Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.short.main.text: Of the days left, {days} must be on {move}.

plural.one: Of the days left, {days} must be on {move}.
plural.other: Of the days left, {days} must be on {move}.

ladders.step.short.main.note: Under a pose step's climb line (ladders.step.next.mark, .perfect) on its card and on its ladder page's next row, and under the Ready view's days line (pump.ready.mark.days, .perfect), where the family's days still lack days on the step's main pose: {days} the main-pose days still to come (ns.PoseNeeds' mainLeft, the summary nx's fifth number, Pump:toward's `main`), {move} the main pose's name (ns.PoseMain: the move of the step's chain the pumps bring for it, one the player stepped down from or that is not open giving way to the next, else the step's anchor; Pump:toward's `mainPose` and, since 2026-10-20, the Book climb's; the game's ladders.step.shortMain, Tree.PoseShort). Shown only while mainLeft is above 0. Slice 47 (2026-10-19): any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day; the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days), at least pose_anchor_days of them on its main pose (pose_anchor_days_risky where only Perfect counts) and pose_perfect_days answered Perfect where Good counts too (ns.PoseNeeds).

ladders.step.short.perfect.note: After ladders.step.short.main, or alone, in the same places: the Perfect days the family's days still lack where Good counts too (ns.PoseNeeds' perfectLeft, the summary nx's sixth number, Pump:toward's `perfect`; never where only Perfect counts, whose every day is Perfect); {days} those days (1). The game's ladders.step.shortPerfect. Slice 47 (2026-10-19): any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day; the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days), at least pose_anchor_days of them on its main pose (pose_anchor_days_risky where only Perfect counts) and pose_perfect_days answered Perfect where Good counts too (ns.PoseNeeds).

ladders.step.shut.text: This step needs equipment or settings that are off in Your setup.
ladders.step.shut.note: Under the next step when Your setup leaves its move out and the app cannot name what to change (a sheet from the game). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.spoken.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for one step's row: {step} is its number (1-14), {quality} its quality word, {line} the row's words (the move and its line). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.step.start.note: Under a step the player held from the first pump (the start's steps; the game's ladders.step.start). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.toearn.text: Unlocked. One fresh set of {move} {goal} earns its colour.
ladders.step.toearn.note: Under the step the player stands on when it is orange (Legendary) or gold (Artifact) and no set has earned it yet (2026-10-09): its climb opened it, and one fresh set of {move} at {goal} (its range's floor as a goal with a plus, 3+, or a hold's 0:20+) earns its colour (the game's ladders.step.toEarn). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.toearn.mark.text: Unlocked. One Perfect hold of its pose earns it.
ladders.step.toearn.mark.note: Under the step a stretching or yoga family stands on when it is orange and no hold has earned it yet: its pose held its whole time once and answered Perfect to How close to the goal pose? earns its colour (the game's ladders.step.toEarnMark). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer.

ladders.step.waits.text: Waits for a record of {count} on {move}.
ladders.step.waits.note: A climb that waits for a step of another ladder (2026-10-09: the flags wait for the pull-up and the push-up): {count} is the record that does it (1, or a hold's time) and {move} the move it is set on, the one the player's setup offers at that step (the engine's ns.NeedAt with the setup's filter; the phones' ported needAt). No article before the move, which may start with a vowel. On both phones and the computer: the line of a ladder page's step or Path row that waits, the meta line under a need row's chip on a step's card (ladders.tree.chip), and the line beside a Start that runs that other ladder's climb (via needs) on a card, a move's window or a move's page; and line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip. The game says the same in its own key, the count first. On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet. As written, its full stop its own, the {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review).

ladders.step.waits.step.text: Waits until you do {move} on your {ladder} ladder.
ladders.step.waits.step.note: Under the next step when its climb waits for a step of a stretching, yoga or cardio ladder, which has no record to reach (2026-10-10): {move} is the move of that step, {ladder} that ladder's name as Book shows it (Twist). Since 2026-10-12 a pose step is done by doing its pose there close enough to its mark once (or a step above it), a cardio step by the ladder reaching it. The game's top-out line says the same (topout.needStep: do Twisted chair on your Twist ladder). Also line 3 of a talent tree step's Tooltip on the phones and the computer. On the phones' Result (pump.done) since slice 42's fix round (2026-10-17, F1.3): the row of a passed stretch check whose move, family or climb another wait still holds says that wait in these words, under the move it opens. On the watch's summary card (watch.summary) since slice 42's last review (2026-10-18): the same wait, in the unlock line's place, where a check the wrist's pose passed opens nothing yet. As written, its full stop its own, the {wait} of a held line (ladders.tree.next.proof.held, ladders.measure.proof.held; 2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review).

ladders.steps.note: Section label over a ladder's fourteen steps, from the top colour down.

ladders.steps.above.note: The first row of a ladder's Steps card, folded by default: the steps above the next one (6 more steps up to Artifact); {quality} is the quality word of the ladder's top step. A tap opens them in place and a second folds them; VoiceOver and TalkBack read the row as a button with its expanded state. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.steps.below.note: The last row of a ladder's Steps card, folded by default: the steps under the step now (4 steps below). A tap opens them in place and a second folds them; VoiceOver and TalkBack read the row as a button with its expanded state. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.tip.action.note: TalkBack's action on a move's tooltip in the Book ("Double-tap to show the move"): it opens the move's window, as VoiceOver's pump.line.hint says.

ladders.tree.back.note: A floating button over a talent tree on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04) while the player's frontier (the glowing step, else their highest step in the tree) is scrolled out of view: scrolls back to it. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.tree.break.text: Back from a break: your first set on each ladder shows where you start again.
ladders.tree.break.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04) while no step glows: back after a break, each ladder's first set places the player again.

ladders.tree.chip.note: A button naming another ladder's step: on a one-tree board where a link leaves for another tree, its chip (on a phone at the board's edge, laid out over it; on the computer in the row under the tree's grid), and in a step's card the button to each step it opens (or waits for in another tree); in a phone's step card the row of each step it opens and of each step its climb waits for, in every tree (2026-10-15). {move} the step's move (Push-up), {n} its step on the one 1-14 scale (6), {tree} its tree (Strength).

ladders.tree.day.text: Today already counts on every ladder here. The next day counts from {time}.
ladders.tree.day.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04) while no step glows: every open climb's day already counted; {time} is when the first counts again, a time of day (08:00).

ladders.tree.find.note: The search field over the computer's trees, its label and its prompt: a match outlines its step and dims the rest.

ladders.tree.ladder.note: The tree's ladder line under its Next line on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), naming the selected step's ladder: {ladder} the ladder as the sheet names it (Push), {n} the step on the one 1-14 scale (5), {standing} where the player stands (ladders.standing.*: Push · step 5 · your step). Also the name of each ladder's column for a screen reader. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.tree.mastered.note: Added after the standing in line 2 of a talent tree step's Tooltip (Rare · step 6 · yours · mastered) and in its spoken name on a mastered step (slice 42). Lower case: it follows the standing.

ladders.tree.more.note: The one expander of a talent tree on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04): opens the thin rows (steps no ladder of the tree holds or nears yet) for the session. {count} is how many steps they hold (Show the 9 steps ahead). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.tree.next.earn.text: Next: one fresh set of {move} {earn}+ earns it.
ladders.tree.next.earn.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), by the step that glows: its step is an orange or gold step still to earn: one fresh set of {move} at {earn}, its range's floor (3, a hold's 0:20), earns its colour. Keep the plus after {earn}.

ladders.tree.next.earn.mark.text: Next: one Perfect hold of {move} earns it.
ladders.tree.next.earn.mark.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), by the step that glows: its step is a pose's orange step still to earn: one Perfect hold of {move} earns its colour.

ladders.tree.next.proof.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), by the step that glows: its climb waits only for a stage of its path (slice 42; its proof until then), {proof} that stage's move (Close push-up) at its top {goal} with a plus (12+); a cardio stage's is ladders.tree.next.proof.clean.

ladders.tree.next.proof.clean.note: A talent tree's Next line where the glowing cardio climb waits only for a stage of its path (slice 42): {proof} its form, {have} of the {need} clean days. Plural on {need}; {have} comes as text. The iPhone alone shows it since 2026-11-04 (its trees).

ladders.tree.next.proof.held.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04) where the path's next stage names a move not open yet (2026-10-19; ns.PathNext's `waits`): {proof} that move (Knee clap push-up), {wait} is always a whole sentence with its own full stop, which the line adds none after and no code adds or strips (2026-10-19, the double-check's fix review; slices 49-50 translate it whole): a stage's opener (ladders.held.opens: Opens after Bulgarian split squat at 25 a side., and its .mark and .perfect forms), the move's own stretch check (ladders.held.check: Opens after your first Good hold of Deep squat., and ladders.held.check.perfect), or another ladder's record or step (ladders.step.waits: Waits for a record of 12 on Feet-up push-up., ladders.step.waits.step). The game says the same (Locales/enUS.lua tree.next.pathHeld).

ladders.tree.next.proof.mark.text: Next: {proof}, close enough to its goal pose on {days} days.
ladders.tree.next.proof.mark.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), by the step that glows: its climb waits only for a pose stage of its path, {proof} (Low lunge), answered close enough on {days} game days (2), as the card's stage row says it (ladders.card.stage.mark).  Plural on the day count (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check).

plural.one: Next: {proof}, close enough to its goal pose on {days} day.
plural.other: Next: {proof}, close enough to its goal pose on {days} days.

ladders.tree.next.proof.perfect.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), by the step that glows: ladders.tree.next.proof.mark where the pose must be answered Perfect, as the card's stage row says it (ladders.card.stage.mark.perfect).  Plural on the day count (2026-10-16, slice 40's double-check).

ladders.tree.next.trial.text: Next: do one max set of {move} to find where you start.
ladders.tree.next.trial.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04), by the step that glows: the tree's ladder the Trial places next, whose first set finds the player's step there (Push-up).

ladders.tree.none.text: Nothing to climb here right now: each ladder is at its top or waiting.
ladders.tree.none.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04) while no step glows: every ladder of the tree is at its top, not open yet or shut.

ladders.tree.pain.text: Paused: you marked pain for every climb here.
ladders.tree.pain.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name on the iPhone (its trees; Android and the computer show none since 2026-11-04) while no step glows: a pain flag holds each open climb of the tree.

ladders.tree.rest.text: Rest today. Pumps come back at {time}.
ladders.tree.rest.note: The Next line under a talent tree's name while no step glows, and the reason beside a greyed Start (a step's card, a move's window, a move's page), on the phones and the computer: the player said they felt unwell, which rests every pump until {time}, the next game day's start (04:00). Pump home and the computer's home say pump.rest.line.

ladders.tree.rotor.note: The name of VoiceOver's rotor on a talent tree: it lists the glowing step first, then each next step (the step above the player's on a ladder) in the tree's order. The iPhone alone shows it since 2026-11-04 (its trees).

ladders.tree.select.text: Select it and show its links
ladders.tree.select.note: The long press's action on a step of a talent tree for a screen reader (VoiceOver's named action, TalkBack's long-press label): it selects the step, draws its links to the steps it opens and waits for, and shows its Tooltip. Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.tree.spoken.note: Read by a screen reader (VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's) for a step of a talent tree: {move} its move (Push-up), {quality} its quality word (Uncommon), {n} its step on the one 1-14 scale (5), {standing} where the player stands (ladders.standing.*), {line} its key line, the Tooltip's line 3 with its first letter lowered, in words where the Tooltip uses signs (record 27 of 30: ladders.tree.spoken.record).

ladders.tree.spoken.beads.note: Read by a screen reader after a ringed step's key line where its climb has a path (the beads, slice 42): {done} of the {count} stages done. Lower case: it follows the key line. Plural on {count}; {done} comes as text.
ladders.tree.spoken.beads.text: then {done} of {count} moves for the next step done

plural.one: then {done} of {count} move for the next step done
plural.other: then {done} of {count} moves for the next step done

ladders.tree.spoken.held.note: The key line of ladders.tree.spoken for the player's step while its climb is shut below the top (ladders.measure.held read aloud): {record} its record in words (ladders.tree.spoken.record: record 22 of 30), {holds} what holds the climb with its first letter in lower case (waits for a record of 8 on Pull-up.).

ladders.tree.spoken.record.note: The key line of ladders.tree.spoken for a step with a record on its range: {record} the record, {high} its range's top (record 27 of 30), each a count or a hold's time.

ladders.tree.spoken.waiting.note: Read by a screen reader (VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's) for the column of a ladder that waits whole on a talent tree, one button: {ladder} its name (Handstand), {note} its note (ladders.tree.waits.*) and {sentence} what keeps it waiting without the ladder's name (ladders.opens.record or ladders.opens for a family not open yet, the refusal's line for one the setup or the player's list shuts), each with its first letter lowered (Handstand, not open yet: opens at a Push-up record of 15).

ladders.tree.waits.closed.note: A ladder that waits whole: a family that opens at another ladder's record or step. On a talent tree (the phones' and the computer's) the short note under its name where names show and line 2 of its Tooltip (its sentence stands in the tree's ladder line, the Tooltip and the card); on a step's card, the phones' and the computer's, the note under the card's header.

ladders.tree.waits.off.note: A ladder that waits whole: the player's own Include in pumps switches leave the ladder no move. On a talent tree (the phones' and the computer's) the short note under its name where names show and line 2 of its Tooltip (its sentence stands in the tree's ladder line, the Tooltip and the card); on a step's card, the phones' and the computer's, the note under the card's header.

ladders.tree.waits.setup.note: A ladder that waits whole: Your setup leaves the ladder no move (the equipment or a switch). On a talent tree (the phones' and the computer's) the short note under its name where names show and line 2 of its Tooltip (its sentence stands in the tree's ladder line, the Tooltip and the card); on a step's card, the phones' and the computer's, the note under the card's header.

ladders.untrained.none.note: Heading of Book's Moves when the Not trained yet filter is chosen, nothing is typed and no move is left untrained.

ladders.view.list.note: The Tree | List switch of Book's Ladders: the ladders as rows, each opening its ladder's page. On the computer the switch's second segment; on a phone the value of the TopBar's round Tree | List button while the list shows, which VoiceOver and TalkBack read after its label (ladders.view.show.tree, what a tap does). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.view.show.list.note: The label of the round Tree | List button in Book's TopBar on a phone while the trees show: a tap shows the ladders as a list (its glyph the list's). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.view.show.tree.note: The label of the round Tree | List button in Book's TopBar on a phone while the list shows: a tap shows the ladders as talent trees (its glyph the tree's). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

ladders.view.tree.note: The Tree | List switch of Book's Ladders: the ladders as talent trees. On the computer the switch's first segment; on a phone the value of the TopBar's round Tree | List button while the trees show, which VoiceOver and TalkBack read after its label (ladders.view.show.list, what a tap does). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

links.channel.note: Android only: the notification channel of the game offers, in the system's settings (its own channel, so it pops up as the iPhone's banner does).

links.channel.about.text: A pump on offer when you finish a game on this phone, or a game or a stream on a linked site
links.channel.about.note: Android only: the offers' channel's description, which also holds the question after a game on this phone (docs/phone-games.md B7).

links.chesscom.name.note: The label of the text box for the player's name on Chess.com.

links.chesscom.none.text: Chess.com has no player by that name.
links.chesscom.none.note: Under the name box when Chess.com finds no such player.

links.chesscom.prompt.note: The placeholder in the Chess.com name box.

links.chesscom.reads.text: QuestPump reads the games Chess.com shows for your name from this phone, never through Pluxia. No sign-in is needed.
links.chesscom.reads.note: Chess.com's page: what the app reads. Chess.com shows every player's games openly, so the app needs only the name.

links.error.note: When the site did not answer. {link} is the site's name.

links.error.kept.text: This phone could not keep the link. Try again.
links.error.kept.note: The line under the fields when the site answered but this phone could not store the sign-in, the name or the key.

links.lichess.reads.text: QuestPump reads your finished games on Lichess from this phone, never through Pluxia. Your sign-in stays on this phone.
links.lichess.reads.note: Lichess's page: what the app reads and where it keeps the sign-in.

links.link.note: Button: links the site with the name (Chess.com) or the key and the profile (Steam) typed above it.

links.name.assettocorsa.note: The game's own name, as its publisher writes it: a game's name on its tile and in its window on the desktop app's Games tab (contract/links.json's computer list, slice 48: heard through its documented shared memory).

links.name.assettocorsaone.note: The game's own name, as its publisher writes it: a game's name on its tile and in its window on the desktop app's Games tab (contract/links.json's computer list, 2026-10-28: the first Assetto Corsa, heard through its shared memory like Assetto Corsa Competizione).

links.name.automobilista.note: The game's own name, as its publisher writes it: a game's name on its tile and in its window on the desktop app's Games tab (contract/links.json's computer list, 2026-10-29: heard through its documented shared memory, once its Shared Memory is set to Project CARS 2, as a race begins and ends).

links.notify.ask.text: Allow notifications so QuestPump can offer a pump after your games.
links.notify.ask.note: The card on Linked games, and on Games on this phone once its automations or usage access work, while the phone was never asked about notifications (Not now on the window before its question); Turn on offers under it asks.

links.notify.off.text: Notifications are off for QuestPump, so no offer can show.
links.notify.off.note: The card on Linked games, and on Games on this phone once its automations or usage access work, while the phone refused QuestPump's notifications or turned them off; Open Settings under it opens the phone's own settings.

links.priming.allow.note: The window's button, and the quiet button of the notifications card (Linked games, Games on this phone) while notifications were never asked for: then the phone asks about notifications. Not Allow: the phone's own question has that word.

links.priming.later.note: The window's quiet button: no question now. Linked games says when notifications are off.

links.priming.title.text: Offer a pump after your games?
links.priming.title.note: The heading of the window shown once after the first link, before the phone asks about notifications: its question, over Turn on offers and Not now (2026-10-22: no body).

links.signin.note: Button: opens the site's own sign-in. {link} is the site's name (Lichess, Twitch).

links.state.again.note: A link's value and its page's state on Lichess and Twitch once the site stopped taking its sign-in, and the Menu's Linked games value while it is the first such link: the player signs in again. Chess.com and Steam say Link again.

links.state.linked.note: A link's value and its page's state: the player's name on that site (Linked as Sam).

links.state.off.note: A link's value and its page's state when the player has not linked that site.

links.state.relink.note: A link's state on Chess.com and Steam once its name or key stopped working (no sign-in there): the player links it again with the name or a new key. Lichess and Twitch say Sign in again.

links.steam.badkey.text: Steam did not take that key.
links.steam.badkey.note: Under the key box when Steam refuses the key.

links.steam.getkey.note: A row that opens Steam's page where the player makes their own key.

links.steam.key.note: The label of the text box for the player's own key from Steam. Web API is Steam's name for it.

links.steam.key.prompt.note: The placeholder in the Steam key's field: what a Steam Web API key looks like.

links.steam.noprofile.text: Steam has no profile by that name.
links.steam.noprofile.note: Under the profile box when Steam finds no such profile.

links.steam.private.text: Your Steam profile is private, so QuestPump can't see your games. Make your game details public on Steam.
links.steam.private.note: On Steam's page once linked, while Steam says the profile is not public: no game shows, so no offer comes.

links.steam.profile.note: The label of the text box for the player's Steam profile.

links.steam.profile.prompt.note: The placeholder in the Steam profile box: the profile's web address, its number or its custom name.

links.steam.reads.text: QuestPump reads the game you play on Steam from this phone, never through Pluxia. Your key stays on this phone.
links.steam.reads.note: Steam's page: what the app reads with the player's own key, and where it keeps the key.

links.steam.revokekey.note: A row on Steam's linked page that opens Steam's key page: the app forgets the key at Unlink, only Steam can turn it off for good.

links.steam.saved.note: In place of the key once Steam is linked: the key is kept on this phone and never shown again.

links.twitch.code.note: Caps over the code the player types on Twitch's page to link this phone, naming that page (RFC 8628 §3.3: the verification address beside the code).

links.twitch.expired.text: The code ran out. Try again.
links.twitch.expired.note: The code was not confirmed on Twitch in time; signing in again shows a new one.

links.twitch.open.note: Button: opens Twitch's page where the player confirms the code.

links.twitch.reads.text: From this phone, QuestPump reads when your Twitch stream is live and when it stopped, never through Pluxia. Your sign-in stays on this phone.
links.twitch.reads.note: Twitch's page: what the app reads and where it keeps the sign-in.

links.twitch.waiting.note: While the app waits for the player to confirm the code on Twitch.

links.unlink.note: Button (destructive): this phone forgets the link.

links.unlink.message.text: QuestPump forgets this link and offers no more pumps from it.
links.unlink.message.note: The confirmation's line: the sign-in, the name or the key leaves this phone.

links.unlink.title.note: Title of the confirmation before the phone forgets a link. {link} is the site's name.

live.done.note: The Live Activity's last state after the pump's last move. The iPhone's alone: Android's Live Update goes with its pump.

live.following.note: The line between the pumps the phone follows without the computer's name, which pump.follow.game carries (the release security review of 2026-10-31): the iPhone's Live Activity title on the Lock Screen (the Dynamic Island says pump.follow.game), and the public version of Android's ongoing notification (VISIBILITY_PRIVATE), which a locked phone shows where the player hides sensitive content, while the game runs on the computer.

live.next.note: The pump's next move on the Lock Screen and in the notification.

live.session.note: iPhone only: the Live Activity's title while the watch's play session runs and no pump has started yet; each pump shows there once it starts.

live.waiting.note: The line while the phone follows the paired computer and no game runs there yet, without the computer's name, which pump.follow.waiting carries (the release security review of 2026-10-31): the iPhone's Live Activity title on the Lock Screen after Follow the game started it, before the game was heard, and the public version of Android's ongoing notification (VISIBILITY_PRIVATE), which a locked phone shows where the player hides sensitive content, in any state of the link but a running game.

log.banked.note: In a game pump's line in the Log, right after where it came from (18:32 · in the game · banked), and on its page: the player banked the pump in the game before a move of it was done, so its moves wait as unfinished.

log.calendar.legend.note: The lead of the weeks' legend, before its steps (Moves a day: None, 1–3, 4–9, 10+, ★ a record).

log.calendar.record.note: The weeks' legend, its last words after the star glyph: a record day (Moves a day: None, 1–3, 4–9, 10+, ★ a record). The charts' legends say charts.legend.star.

log.calendar.records.note: A day's or a game week's new records: a week in Pro's weeks and a chart's record star as VoiceOver and TalkBack read them, and a starred week in a values list.

log.empty.title.note: The Log's heading before the first pump.

log.entry.peak.note: A pump's highest heart rate in beats per minute: peak 142 bpm. In the Log, and on a game pump's result after the helper's heart-rate check.

log.entry.peak.rise.note: A pump's highest heart rate and how far it rose over the pump's start: peak 142 bpm (+38). In the Log, and on a game pump's result after the helper's heart-rate check.

log.entry.steps.note: The steps counted during a pump.

log.held.note: In a pump's line in the Log, after its time, length and reps: the seconds its holds were held together, as a clock as every hold's time is written (14:02 · 1 min · 0:45 held). Also what VoiceOver and TalkBack say for a hold on a pump's page, which shows the clock alone: {time} is then the seconds in words (26 seconds held).

log.minutes.notready.android.text: Health Connect is not ready on this phone.
log.minutes.notready.android.note: The minutes chart when Health Connect is missing or needs an update.

log.minutes.short.note: A length in minutes: a pump's in the Log and on its page (3 min), and minutes played in a week, on a tap of the chart (42 min).

log.minutes.waiting.android.text: Health Connect has not answered yet.
log.minutes.waiting.android.note: The minutes chart while Health Connect's answer is awaited.

log.moves.none.of.note: Fills {moves} in a game pump's title in the Log when no move of it was done: Balanced game pump · 0 of 3 moves. {count} is how many moves the pump asked for.

log.nomove.note: In a game pump's line in the Log, right after where it came from (18:32 · in the game · no move done), and on its page: the pump ended before its first move (paused, or left), and it was not banked.

log.phone.pending.text: Not synced to your computer yet
log.phone.pending.note: A pump of the phone or the watch that has not reached QuestPump on the player's computer yet.

log.pro.row.note: The Saga's row that opens Pro's offer, naming what Pro adds there (2026-10-22: in place of See Pro with pro.has.weeks under it).

log.proven.note: The chip (and its accessibility label) on a pump whose heart rate rose enough for the check, and the title of the page that explains it (How the heart-rate check works).

log.pump.app.note: A pump's title in the Log for one done in the app before the app kept what the player finished: {moves} is its move count in words (3 moves).

log.pump.game.big.note: A Log row's title: a game pump for a big quest (the pump's size, pump.size.big's word; Big until 2026-10-27). {moves} is the pump's moves in words, the pump card's own (pump.moves.none, .one, .two, .three or .many: two moves, 5 moves).

log.pump.game.normal.note: A Log row's title: a game pump for a normal quest (the pump's size, pump.size.normal's word; Normal until 2026-10-27). {moves} is the pump's moves in words, the pump card's own (pump.moves.none, .one, .two, .three or .many: two moves, 5 moves).

log.pump.game.small.note: A Log row's title: a game pump for a small quest (the pump's size, pump.size.small's word: Light, Balanced or Extreme, Small, Normal or Big until 2026-10-27). {moves} is the pump's moves in words, the pump card's own (pump.moves.none, .one, .two, .three or .many: two moves, 5 moves).

log.pump.levelup.note: A Log row's title: the pump a level-up asked for. {moves} is the pump's moves in words, the pump card's own (pump.moves.none, .one, .two, .three or .many: two moves, 5 moves).

log.pump.moves.note: Section label on a pump's page over its moves and what was done.

log.pump.record.note: A chip on a pump's page: a move of it beat its record.

log.record.note: In a pump's line in the Log, after its time and length (14:02 · 3 min · a new record), and under a move on the pump's page.

log.reps.note: In a pump's line in the Log, after its time and length: the reps typed for its moves together (14:02 · 3 min · 36 reps). Also what VoiceOver and TalkBack say for a move's count on a pump's page, which shows the number alone (22 reps), and for the count in the timer ring while the voice counts a set of reps (7 reps).

log.result.notallout.note: A counted set saved Not all out in the Saga's and a pump page's move (slice 53: no clean day, never a best): {value} its count as the line writes one (12) or Not counted (pump.count.none) where it has none. The game's Log says the same (Locales/enUS.lua log.result.notAllOut).

log.result.slipped.note: A counted set saved Form slipped in the Saga's and a pump page's move (2026-10-19, the program's double-check; slice 42: no clean day, never a best): {value} its count as the line writes one (12) or Not counted (pump.count.none) where it has none. The game's Log says the same (Locales/enUS.lua log.result.slipped).

log.source.catchup.note: In a pump's line in the Log, right after its time, and on its page: a catch-up pump, which paid the moves the game still owed.

log.source.computer.note: In a pump's line in the Log, right after its time (or after where it came from: catch-up · on a computer), and on its page: the pump ran in QuestPump on a computer, the desktop app. Says a computer, never this or your computer: a row never says which computer it was.

log.source.game.note: In a pump's line in the Log, right after its time (18:32 · in the game · 4 min), and on its page: the game asked for the pump and the player did it there.

log.source.link.note: In a pump's line in the Log, right after its time, in place of on the phone: {link} is the linked game or service whose finish offered the pump (Lichess, Chess.com, Twitch, Steam).

log.source.matches.note: After the game in a pump's source words: the matches the player answered (after Wild Rift · 3 matches).

log.source.phone.note: In a pump's line in the Log, right after its time, and on its page: the player did the pump with the phone app. Says the phone, never this phone: a pump from the player's other phone reads it too. On the iPhone it words only a pump known from its rows alone, which may have been done on an Android phone; the iPhone's own pumps name the device (log.source.phone.ios).

log.source.phone.ios.note: In a pump's line in the Saga, right after its time, and on its page: the player did the pump with the app. The iPhone's twin of log.source.phone: {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad (an iPad runs the iPhone app too). Says the iPhone, never this iPhone: a pump synced from the player's other iPhone or iPad reads it too. A pump known from its rows alone, which may be an Android phone's, reads log.source.phone instead.

log.source.played.note: In a pump's line in the Saga, right after its time, and on its page, ahead of the link: a pump after a game on this phone, {game} its name (after Wild Rift).

log.source.played.any.note: The same when no game's name is known.

log.source.watch.note: In a pump's line in the Log, right after its time (or after where it came from: in the game · on the watch), and on its page: the pump, or a move of it, ran on the watch.

log.today.note: A day's heading over its pumps in the Log, and the last backup's day in the Menu.

log.week.none.note: What Pump home's week marks on the computer are read as before the game week's first move.

log.weeks.app.note: Chart legend: the moves done in the app's pumps (on the phone, on the watch, on the computer, and the ones a linked game offered).

log.weeks.catchup.note: Chart legend: the moves done in pumps that paid unfinished moves from the phone, the watch or the computer.

log.weeks.days.note: Title of Pro's weeks' days: a row a game week, each day marked by its moves; VoiceOver's name of that block.

log.weeks.days.count.note: A game week in Pro's weeks as VoiceOver, TalkBack and the values list read it, before its moves and records: 4 days with a move, 31 moves, 1 record.

log.weeks.game.note: Chart legend: the moves done in the game's pumps.

log.weeks.minutes.note: Chart title: the minutes played in each game week (QuestPump's own sessions, read back from the phone's health store).

log.weeks.moves.note: Chart title: the moves done in each game week, a column a week stacked by where they were done (Game, Catch-up, App).

log.weeks.split.note: A week's moves done by where they were done, on a tap of the chart and in its values: Game 31 · Catch-up 4 · App 6. The words are the chart legend's (log.weeks.game, .catchup, .app); each count after its word, never a plural.

log.weeks.title.note: Section title over Pro's weeks: the player's game weeks (each week's days, the moves and the minutes per week).

log.xp.note: At the right of a pump's row in the Log: the experience points the pump paid (+75). VoiceOver and TalkBack read it as 75 XP.

log.yesterday.note: A day's heading over its pumps in the Log, and the last backup's day in the Menu.

menu.about.contact.note: Legal text (the product-safety contact). {address} is the support mail address, contact@questpump.com, shown as a mail link.

menu.about.header.note: Section header: who makes the app.

menu.about.imprint.note: Link: opens the legal notice naming the company (German: Impressum).

menu.about.row.note: A row in the Menu and the title of its page: the safety note, privacy, acknowledgements, the imprint and support.

menu.about.security.note: Link: opens the page on how to report a security problem.

menu.acknowledgements.assets.note: Section header over the sound packs the app uses.

menu.acknowledgements.fonts.note: Section header over the fonts the app uses.
