menu.acknowledgements.licence.ofl.note: The fonts' licence by its own name, which stays in English in every language.

menu.acknowledgements.row.note: Row beside About in the Menu: opens the page that credits the fonts and sounds the app uses.

menu.acknowledgements.text.note: Opens a licence's full text under its font or asset.

menu.acknowledgements.title.note: Title of the page that credits the fonts and sounds the app uses.

menu.backup.both.note: Joins the two counts of a restore: {moves} as "9 moves", {entries} as "12 log entries".

menu.backup.entries.note: How many rows of the pump log a restore brought.

menu.backup.filename.note: The backup file's name, before its .json ending. {day} is the date as 2026-10-03. Use no slash or colon.

menu.backup.header.note: Section header: the backup file of the player's pumps.

menu.backup.header.sync.note: Section header and the Menu's row on every phone and the desktop app since slice 60: the backup file and the sync of the player's progress (the account sync, contract/sync-api.yaml).

menu.backup.kept.note: Follows the restore line as its second sentence: the file's settings did not replace the phone's.

menu.backup.last.note: {date} is the day and time the last backup file was saved, formatted by the phone.

menu.backup.moves.note: How many moves the pumps a restore brought hold. A move is one exercise of a pump.

menu.backup.never.note: No backup file was saved yet.

menu.backup.never.short.note: The Backup and sync row's value in the Menu: no backup file saved and no sync yet.

menu.backup.newer.text: This backup is from a newer QuestPump. Update the app first.

menu.backup.notbackup.text: This is not a QuestPump backup.

menu.backup.nothing.text: Nothing new: everything in this backup is already here.
menu.backup.nothing.note: A restore that brought nothing the phone did not have.

menu.backup.notsaved.text: The backup file was not saved.

menu.backup.restore.note: Button: reads a backup file back in.

menu.backup.restored.note: {items} is what came in: a count of moves, a count of log entries, or both joined by menu.backup.both.

menu.backup.restoring.note: Shown while a backup file is being read in.

menu.backup.save.note: Button: writes the backup file where the player chooses.

menu.backup.settings.note: A restore that brought character sheets and settings but no pumps.

menu.backup.toolarge.text: This file is too large to be a QuestPump backup.

menu.backup.unread.text: Your history did not load this time. Close QuestPump and open it again.

menu.backup.unreadable.text: The file could not be read.

menu.callouts.note: A switch in the Menu: one recorded line at a move's Ready view in the phone's own pumps, such as a record attempt, a step one day away or a streak day (on by default; Sounds off silences it too).

menu.characters.note: Section label on the helper's page over the characters the helper's sheets hold, the shown one ticked.

menu.crash.note: A switch in the Menu's QuestPump group: on, a crash report goes by itself at the next start. On by default, except in the EU, the EEA, India and Canada, where it stays off until the player says yes.

menu.crash.note.text: While this is on, a report goes to us by itself after a crash. Never your pumps, your health data or your name.
menu.crash.note.note: Legal text (the privacy disclosure): translate exactly. The line under the crash report switch.

menu.demo.header.note: Section label over the demo helper's switch on Safety and about.

menu.demo.toggle.note: Switch: plays a pretend helper on this phone, for a look at the app without a computer.

menu.email.code.expired.text: That code ended. Send a new one.

menu.email.code.field.note: The accessibility label of the six code boxes.

menu.email.code.limit.text: Too many codes for now. Try again later.

menu.email.code.wrong.text: That code is not right. {count} tries left.

plural.one: That code is not right. {count} try left.
plural.other: That code is not right. {count} tries left.

menu.email.delete.body.text: This deletes your synced progress and your email from QuestPump's server. Each device keeps its own progress.

menu.email.delete.pro.text: Your Pro subscription keeps billing through Google Play after this. Cancel it there first.
menu.email.delete.pro.note: In Delete your account? while Google Play holds the player's Pro, over Manage your subscription (Google Play's account deletion rule): deleting the account does not cancel it.

menu.email.delete.pro.ios.text: Your Pro subscription keeps billing through Apple after this. Cancel it there first.
menu.email.delete.pro.ios.note: In Delete your account? while the App Store holds the player's Pro, over Manage your subscription (App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v)): deleting the account does not cancel it.

menu.email.device.android.note: The {device} of menu.email.needkey.title and menu.email.signout.title on Android, which calls itself a phone (menu.sync.this.android); the iPhone names its model.

menu.email.invalid.text: That is not an email address.

menu.email.needkey.title.note: After an email sign-in, before this device has the key: {device} is the device's kind.

menu.email.remove.note: The Email page's linked view, under Sign out: the address leaves the account (DELETE /api/sync/v1/email) and the account and its progress stay; one confirmation (menu.email.remove.title, its action menu.sync.remove).

menu.email.remove.title.note: The confirmation of Remove email: {address} is the linked address, or menu.email.linked's words on a device that did not type it. Its action is menu.sync.remove; the account and its progress stay.

menu.email.signout.body.text: Sync stops here. Your progress stays on it.

menu.email.signout.title.note: {device} is the device's kind: iPhone, iPad, phone or computer.

menu.email.taken.join.note: Signs in with the email another account holds: this device's progress joins that account's.

menu.email.taken.title.text: This email has its own progress

menu.feedback.row.note: A row in the Menu's QuestPump group, beside Safety and about, and the title of the page it opens: a message to the people who make QuestPump, with the player's counts if they tick them.

menu.free.body.note: Section label in Your setup over the switches No jumping, Avoid breath-hold strain and Avoid head-down positions.

menu.free.equipment.note: Section header: what the player has at hand to train with.

menu.free.experience.locked.note: Under the experience question once the ladders have rungs, from the phone's own pumps or, with a helper paired, the game's rows (slice 26): the answer no longer changes them.

menu.free.focus.note: A row in Your setup, its value the current focus (Balanced): it opens the focus window.

menu.free.gear.action.note: A screen reader's way to a gear chip's touch and hold in Your setup, which shows the chip's tooltip (the piece's name, what it is, and what it would open while it is not chosen): TalkBack's long-click label ("Double-tap and hold to show what it is") and VoiceOver's named action, as menu.demo.toggle does for its hold; a tap still chooses or clears the piece.

menu.free.gear.opens.text: Now it would open {count} moves, up to {quality}.

plural.one: Now it would open {count} move, up to {quality}.
plural.other: Now it would open {count} moves, up to {quality}.

menu.free.gear.opens.note: The last line of a gear chip's tooltip in Your setup while the piece is not chosen, under its name and what it is (contract/sheet.json gear_tips): what adding it would open now, as the game's equipment tooltip says it. The tooltip shows on hover or keyboard focus on the computer and on a touch and hold on the phones. {count} is how many more moves the pumps could bring, {quality} the best quality word among them (Starter, Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Artifact).

menu.free.gear.opens.plain.note: menu.free.gear.opens for a piece whose moves have no quality (none of them stands on a row of harder versions): the last line of the gear chip's tooltip, shown on hover or keyboard focus on the computer and on a touch and hold on the phones. {count} is how many more moves the pumps could bring.

menu.free.opens.note: A line under Your setup's equipment chips, two at most: what adding a piece would open (Pull-up bar: 7 more moves, up to Legendary). The first names the piece that opens the most; the second the piece that opens the most once the first is added, its count the moves it opens past the first. {gear} is the equipment's name, {count} how many more moves the pumps could bring, {quality} the best quality word among them (Starter, Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Artifact).

menu.free.opens.plain.note: menu.free.opens for a piece whose moves have no quality (none of them stands on a row of harder versions): {gear} is the equipment's name, {count} how many more moves the pumps could bring (on the second line, past the first line's piece).

menu.free.pain.note: Section header over the joint switches: a joint switched on leaves out every move that loads it (2026-10-22: no footer under them).

menu.free.pain.ingame.note: {joint} is a joint's name, such as Knee: its pain flag was set in the game.

menu.free.place.note: Section label in Your setup over the switches Floor moves, Room to move and Quiet mode.

menu.free.restart.note: Button (destructive): deletes the records and history of the pumps the app runs by itself, on this phone, on the phones it syncs with and in the desktop app (slice 28: a reset row the sync and, since 2026-10-09, the helper's copy carry).

menu.free.restart.confirm.note: Button (destructive) in the confirmation: the app's own pumps start over.

menu.free.restart.footer.text: The app's pumps and history go, on this phone, on the phones it syncs with and in QuestPump on your computer, but your pain flags and your focus stay. The game keeps what it already has.
menu.free.restart.footer.note: Under the button: the app's rows go except its pain flags (the body's state, which the game also rests on) and its focus (one focus for the player, slice 30), on every phone that syncs (slice 28: the reset row goes with the sync) and, through the helper's copy, on every paired phone and the desktop app, whose own fold starts at it (2026-10-09); the rows the phones sent the helper stay in the game (slice 26).

menu.free.restart.title.note: Title of the confirmation before the app's own pumps start over.

menu.game.note: Section label in the Menu over Helper, Your setup, Your moves and Linked games.

menu.haptics.note: A switch in the Menu: the phone's vibrations with the sounds. The watch keeps its own.

menu.heart.baseline.text: First it finds where your heart rate was: the middle reading of the {before} seconds before the move starts.
menu.heart.baseline.note: Under How it decides. {before} is the seconds of the baseline, the rule's own number (60), never typed here: the cores' VerdictRule.baseline (Swift) and VerdictRule.BASELINE (Kotlin), questpump-core verdict::BASELINE_S on the computer.

menu.heart.computer.text: QuestPump on your computer does three more things. It measures every move of a pump from your heart rate before the pump's first move. With a watch, it judges moves where your hands hold you up, like push-ups, on the {after} seconds after the set, since the watch reads poorly during them. And it learns how your heart rate moves while you just play, so after a while it may ask for less or more rise, to fit your heart.
menu.heart.computer.note: Under How it decides (the phones' words; the desktop app's are desk.menu.heart.computer): the after-set window and the calibration per source. {after} is the seconds after the set (30; VerdictRule.afterSet, AFTER_SET), never typed here.

menu.heart.decides.note: Caps label on How the heart-rate check works: the rule.

menu.heart.isnot.note: Caps label on How the heart-rate check works, over the line that the check is a game mark and the not-a-medical-device line.

menu.heart.isnot.line.text: The check is a game mark, not a test of your body. It never stops a pump, and it never changes your XP or a record.
menu.heart.isnot.line.note: Under What it is not, above the not-a-medical-device line.

menu.heart.reads.note: Caps label on How the heart-rate check works: the data the check uses.

menu.heart.reads.line.text: Only your heart rate. It comes from your watch while you run a play session on it, or from a heart-rate strap you turn on in QuestPump on your computer.
menu.heart.reads.line.note: On How the heart-rate check works, under What it reads (the phones' words; the desktop app's are desk.menu.heart.reads.line).

menu.heart.rise.text: Then it looks for a rise over that within {window} seconds of the move's start: {reps} beats a minute for reps or cardio, {hold} for a hold or a stretch.
menu.heart.rise.note: Under How it decides. The rule's own numbers, never typed here: {window} the seconds after the move's start (60: VerdictRule.window in Swift, VerdictRule.WINDOW in Kotlin, verdict::WINDOW_S on the computer), {reps} the rise a move of reps or a timed one needs (20: dynamicRise, DYNAMIC_RISE, DYNAMIC_BPM), {hold} the rise a hold or a flow needs (12: isoRise, ISO_RISE, ISO_BPM). A flow is a stretch in the game's words.

menu.heart.row.note: A row in Safety and about, and a quiet button on a pump's page in the Log that shows the heart-rate check or a peak heart rate: opens the page that explains the check (App Store guideline 1.4.1).

menu.heart.stays.note: Caps label on How the heart-rate check works: where the heart rate is kept and who receives it.

menu.heart.stays.android.text: If you allow it, your phone also saves each play session from your watch in Health Connect, with its heart rate.
menu.heart.stays.android.note: Under Where it stays, on Android: the watch's play sessions in Health Connect, which the phone writes.

menu.heart.stays.ios.text: If you allow it, your watch also saves each play session in Apple Health, with its heart rate.
menu.heart.stays.ios.note: Under Where it stays, on the iPhone: the watch's play sessions in Apple Health.

menu.heart.stays.line.text: Your heart rate stays on your own devices: your phone, your watch, and QuestPump and the game on your computer. It moves only between them, sealed on the way. Neither Pluxia GmbH nor the Pro coach ever gets it, and your backup, your sync and feedback you send leave it out.
menu.heart.stays.line.note: Under Where it stays (the phones' words; the desktop app's are desk.menu.heart.stays.line), as the privacy policy says it.

menu.heart.twice.text: Two readings in a row must reach it, so one odd reading never counts.
menu.heart.twice.note: Under How it decides: two samples in a row at or over the needed level.

menu.heart.without.note: Caps label on How the heart-rate check works: what happens with no heart-rate source.

menu.heart.without.line.text: Without one, no move gets the check, and that is fine: every pump counts the same. A move also gets no check when the rise does not show or the reading drops out. It still counts in full.
menu.heart.without.line.note: Under Without a watch or strap: no source, an unproven move, a stream that dropped out; none of them changes what the pump counts.

menu.helper.header.note: Section header: QuestPump on the player's computer, the app for macOS and Windows that the phone pairs with.

menu.helper.none.note: The status chip on the helper's page: no helper paired.

menu.helper.rescan.note: Button: scan the helper's pairing QR code again, to pair anew.

menu.helper.unpair.note: Button (destructive): this phone forgets the helper.

menu.import.button.note: Button: imports the sheet: the text pasted in Import a sheet, or the sheet another app shared or a link opened, shown in Import this sheet?

menu.import.header.note: Section header: what a player who plays without QuestPump on the computer needs. QuestPump is the app's name; QuestPump on your computer is the app for macOS and Windows that the phone pairs with.

menu.import.placeholder.note: Placeholder of the paste field for the text the game copies (Data, Export in QuestPump's settings).

menu.import.remove.note: Button (destructive): deletes the character sheet imported by hand.

menu.import.scan.note: Button: opens the camera for the QR code the game shows after /qp qr.

menu.import.title.note: Button and sheet title: bring the character sheet in from the game by text or code. A sheet is the character sheet.

menu.link.confirm.browser.note: menu.link.confirm.title's {device} for a request code in the https form, which questpump.com/play shows (slice 63).

menu.link.confirm.computer.note: menu.link.confirm.title's {device} for a request code in the questpump-link: form, which the desktop app's Link a device page shows (slice 60).

menu.link.confirm.title.note:
Before the phone answers another device's request code (only one scanned on Link a device: a request link opened from the camera, https://questpump.com/link#req..

, only opens the scanner there): letting it in gives that device this phone's progress, so a code someone planted asks first (docs/plan.md slice 63). {device} is menu.link.confirm.browser or menu.link.confirm.computer, by the code's form, since a code carries no device name.

menu.link.confirm.yes.note: The primary button of menu.link.confirm.title: the phone answers the request code and the other device opens this progress.

menu.linkdevice.check.text: Check this number on the other screen
menu.linkdevice.check.note: Title of the window with a six-digit number after Let in, once the server took the phone's answer to a computer's or a browser's request code: the device that showed the code shows the same number and asks whether the phone shows it (desk.menu.link.check.title) before it joins.

menu.linkdevice.expired.text: That code ended. Show a new one on the other device.

menu.linkdevice.noscanner.note: Android only: the state line after Scan a code (Link a device) or Scan from another device (the Email page) when Google's code scanner could not start (Play services lacks its module or has not downloaded it yet); Paste a link follows under it. The iPhone's own scanner page says the camera's state instead (setup.camera.*).

menu.linkdevice.reveal.note: Button in the place of a code that opens the progress. Phones: on Link a device when a link opened the page (questpump://linkdevice, a browser's request code), it shows this device's link code, which a link never shows by itself. Computer: Link a device's QR, Email's request code, the restore code and the one typed to restore; the press keeps the window out of screen captures, then shows the code.

menu.linkdevice.show.text: Scan this with QuestPump on your other device

menu.linkdevice.taken.text: Another device answered that code first.
menu.linkdevice.taken.note: On Link a device after Let in, when the server says the request code was answered already: the phone shows no number, so the device that showed the code can tell its answer came from someone else.

menu.linkdevice.wrong.text: That is not a QuestPump link code.

menu.links.note: The Menu's row on The game card and the title of its page: the game and streaming sites the player links, so that finishing a game or a stream there offers a pump.

menu.links.count.note: The Linked games row's value: how many sites are linked (2 linked). Both forms read the same in English.

menu.links.none.note: The Linked games row's value when no site is linked.

menu.moves.note: A row in the Menu's The game card, after Your setup, and the title of its page: the moves the player left out of pumps and the favourites, each with its switch.

menu.moves.count.note: Your moves' value in the Menu: how many moves the player left out of pumps or made a favourite (a move both counts once).

menu.moves.favourites.note: Section label on Your moves over the moves the player marked as favourites (they come first in the pumps), each with its switch.

menu.moves.favourites.none.note: Under Favourites when the player marked no move as a favourite.

menu.moves.group.text: Include the whole group in pumps
menu.moves.group.note: The screen reader's hint on a row of Your moves whose title is an exercise group's name (Kettlebell), left out of pumps with all its moves (a line under the title until 2026-10-22): what the row's switch does, as Include in pumps says for a move; on takes the whole group back in.

menu.moves.none.note: Your moves' value in the Menu when no move is left out and none is a favourite.

menu.moves.out.note: Section label on Your moves over the moves the player switched off for pumps, each with its switch: on takes it back into the pumps.

menu.moves.out.none.text: You have left no move out.
menu.moves.out.none.note: Under Left out of pumps when the player switched no move or group off. It speaks of the player's own choices only: moves the setup or a pain flag leaves out are not listed on this page.

menu.off.note: The coach's row on Pro's page: the coach is off; also the value of Your QuestPump's Pump first row while it is off.

menu.on.note: The coach's row on Pro's page: the coach is on; on the iPhone also the value of Your QuestPump's Games on this phone row once a game's open and close arrived, and of its Pump first row while it is on.

menu.phone.note: Section label in the Menu over the Sounds and Haptics switches, Backup and sync and Reminders. Android's; the iPhone's is menu.phone.ios.

menu.phone.ios.note: Section label in the Menu over the Sounds and Haptics switches, Backup and sync and Reminders. The iPhone's twin of menu.phone. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

menu.phonegames.note: The Your QuestPump card's row and the title of its page: a pump on offer when a game on this phone closes.

menu.phonegames.count.note: Android: the Games on this phone row's value once it works: how many games it watches.

menu.phonegames.setup.note: The Games on this phone row's value until it works (Android before it was turned on with usage access, the iPhone before a game's open and close arrived), and on Android Pump first's row while it is on without usage access or Display over other apps.

menu.privacy.note: Link: opens the privacy policy on questpump.com.

menu.pro.from.web.note: The state line on Pro's page while the account's Pro was bought on questpump.com (slice 64), on the phones and the computer. Plain words, never a link: the phones show no way to a purchase outside the app (App Store Review Guidelines 3.1.1 and 3.1.3(b); Google Play's payments policy).

menu.pumpfirst.note: The Your QuestPump card's row and the title of its page: apps the player picks wait each day for the first pump.

menu.pumpfirst.count.note: Android: the Pump first row's value while it is on: how many apps wait.

menu.questpump.note: Section label in the Menu over Safety and about and Send feedback: the app's name.

menu.quick.length.note: A Menu row (2026-11-03) with the five lengths in a Segmented under it: how long the Pump screen's Quick pump runs, kept on this device.

menu.reminders.note: The Menu's row and the page of the reminders the player sets, the streak reminder and the sitting cue.

menu.reminders.nonotify.note: The Reminders row's value while a reminder or the sitting cue is on and the phone does not let QuestPump show notifications.

menu.reminders.off.note: The Reminders row's value when no reminder is on.

menu.repcount.note: A switch: in the app's own pumps the voice says each rep's number as a running rep move's figure finishes that rep, in the game's own voice, so the player can follow along, the pump's ring shows the same count and the count after Done starts from it (on by default; Sounds off turns it off too, and on the computer the voice's switch; a move done one side at a time counts each side from 1 until the player presses Switch sides; none on a counted set or a game pump).

menu.restore.line.text: Anyone with this code can open your progress. Keep it somewhere safe.

menu.restore.wrong.text: A character is off. Check the code.

menu.safety.title.note: Row and page title: the game's safety text.

menu.scan.placeholder.note: Placeholder of the Paste a link field: the start of the helper's pairing link (a sheet text pasted there works too, but the Menu's Import a sheet is its place). Keep the link as it is.

menu.setup.note: A row in the Menu, the title of its page, and a row in a Book move's window when the setup leaves the move out: where the player trains, the body switches, the experience, the equipment and pain.

menu.setup.gear.note: Your setup's value in the Menu: how many pieces of equipment the player chose.

menu.setup.nogear.note: Your setup's value in the Menu: no equipment chosen.

menu.setup.pumpon.text: A pump is running. Pain flags apply now; other changes apply from your next pump.
menu.setup.pumpon.note: Your setup's card on the phones and the computer while a pump runs that a change waits for (a catch-up of banked moves, whose Settings opens the page over it): a pain flag set here rests the moves it loads at once, every other change waits for the next pump.

menu.sounds.note: A switch in the Menu: the app's sounds (on by default).

menu.sync.addcomputer.title.note: After pairing, on a phone that syncs: {computer} is the computer's name.

menu.sync.captured.text: The code is hidden while your screen is recorded or shared.
menu.sync.captured.note: In place of the restore code, its entry field or Link a device's QR while the iPhone's screen is recorded, mirrored, AirPlayed or shared (since the release security review of 2026-10-31): the code opens the player's progress. Android keeps those pages from every capture instead.

menu.sync.deleted.text: Your account was deleted. With sync on, this device starts a new one.

menu.sync.demo.text: Sync waits while the demo helper is on.
menu.sync.demo.note: The sync switch's line while the demo helper plays: nothing syncs in the demo, and the switch is greyed.

menu.sync.devices.note: Section label on Backup and sync over the account's devices (this one first, then the player's other phones, iPads and computers), each with its last sync; a device not named yet shows its kind's word (menu.sync.kind.*).

menu.sync.failed.text: Sync did not work. It will try again soon.
menu.sync.failed.note: The sync switch's line after an error the phone retries by itself.

menu.sync.footer.text: Your pumps, counts and times, the game's sheet, your setup and this device's name sync to your other devices through QuestPump's server, encrypted with a key only your devices hold. QuestPump's makers can't read them. Heart rate, pain notes and unwell stops are left out. Turning sync off keeps every pump here.
menu.sync.footer.note: Under the Sync card: what syncs (the pump rows, the game's newest sheet, the setup with the Body switches, the device's name), where and who can read it (legal: the privacy disclosure; translate exactly).

menu.sync.full.text: Sync is full. Your progress stays on this device.

menu.sync.header.note: Section label above the Sync card on the Backup and sync page (slice 28).

menu.sync.join.other.text: Join the progress on your other device?
menu.sync.join.other.note: After another device's link code, when that device syncs other progress than this phone: on Link a device after its scan (menu.linkdevice), after the Email page's Scan from another device, and (since 2026-11-01) where the player is, over the first start or any page, for one pasted or scanned through Paste a link, the pairing scanner or Import a sheet. Joining brings this phone's progress along. A link code carries no device name, so the question names none (menu.sync.join.title names the computer after pairing).

menu.sync.join.title.note: After pairing, when the computer syncs other progress than this phone and that progress wins (a linked email, then more devices): joining brings this phone's progress along. A scanned link code names no device and asks menu.sync.join.other.

menu.sync.kind.android.note: A device's row in the Sync card's Devices while that Android phone has sent no name yet. Every device of the account is listed, so each can be removed, named or not.

menu.sync.kind.desktop.note: A device's row in the Sync card's Devices while that computer has sent no name yet. Every device of the account is listed, so each can be removed, named or not.

menu.sync.kind.ios.note: A device's row in the Sync card's Devices while that iPhone has sent no name yet. Every device of the account is listed, so each can be removed, named or not.

menu.sync.kind.unknown.note: A device's row in the Sync card's Devices while it has sent no name yet and its kind is one this build does not know (a newer QuestPump's), so a new kind never breaks the list. Every device of the account is listed, so each can be removed, named or not.

menu.sync.kind.web.note: A device's row in the Sync card's Devices while that browser has sent no name yet (the kind web, which the sync server takes once QuestPump plays in a browser). Every device of the account is listed, so each can be removed, named or not.

menu.sync.last.note: The sync switch's line once a sync went through; {date} is the day and time, formatted by the phone, as menu.backup.last.

menu.sync.newer.text: Another device synced with a newer QuestPump. Update the app to read its pumps.
menu.sync.newer.note: The Sync card's line when another device sent a batch of a newer version than this app reads (contract/sync-api.yaml, `v`): the batch is kept unread until an update. "Another device": the player's phones, iPads and computers.

menu.sync.rekey.text: Open QuestPump on one of your other devices first, then link this device again from there.
menu.sync.rekey.note: A join (sync turned on, a restore code, a link, a sign-in, the account question's Join) that the sync server holds back after a device was removed, until one of the player's devices still in the account makes the account's new key, which it does as soon as it opens; and sync turned on again on a device whose key that new key replaced while it was out (sync then turns off with this line). Either way the code this device holds no longer joins, so it needs a new restore code or a link from a device still in the account (contract/sync-api.yaml, "The account's new key"). On the phones: the Sync card's line and the answer of the Email, restore code and Link a device pages; on the computer: the Sync card's line and the Email, Restore code and Link a device pages.

menu.sync.remove.title.note: The confirmation when the player taps another device in the sync's Devices list: {device} is that device's name.

menu.sync.removed.text: This device was removed. Link it again from another device or with your restore code.

menu.sync.syncing.note: The sync switch's line while a sync runs.

menu.sync.this.android.note: The Sync card's row for the phone in the player's hand, with its last sync.

menu.sync.this.ios.note: The Sync card's row for the phone in the player's hand, with its last sync. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

menu.sync.unanswered.text: QuestPump's server did not answer. Check your connection and try again.
menu.sync.unanswered.note: A step of the Email, restore code or Link a device pages (sending a code, entering one, a restore code, a link code or its answer, Sign out, Remove email, Delete account), or Pro's Get Pro or Manage Pro on the computer, that the sync server did not answer or whose answer did not open: no connection, a server error or App Check refusing the call. These steps never retry by themselves, so the line asks the player to; menu.sync.failed is the Sync card's own line, for the sync that does retry.

menu.sync.waiting.note: The sync switch's line while the phone is offline: it syncs once it is back.

menu.tips.header.note: Section header of the tip jar.

menu.tips.small.note: The smallest of three tips, a one-time payment that unlocks nothing.

menu.unpair.message.text: QuestPump forgets your computer. Scan its code again to pair.

menu.unpair.title.note: Title of the confirmation before the phone forgets the computer it pairs with.

menu.usage.note: A switch in the Menu's QuestPump group and the privacy window: on, QuestPump sends which features are used and daily counts without any id. On by default, except in the EU, the EEA, India and Canada, where it stays off until the player says yes.

menu.usage.note.text: While this is on, QuestPump sends which features you use and daily counts of your pumps and your best streak, without your name. Never your health data.
menu.usage.note.note: Legal text (the privacy disclosure): translate exactly. The line under the usage statistics switch.

menu.version.note: The app's version at the foot of Safety and about (1.0).

menu.yours.note: Section label over the card at the Menu's top: one Row per part of QuestPump (this phone, the watch, the computer, the game, the linked games), each with a check or its one next step (2026-10-09).

menu.yours.game.note: The Your QuestPump card's row for the addon: the game it is for, named as the site and the addon card name it (contract/copy/words.json, blizzard: except). Its step is Get the addon, questpump.com/addon. Also the game's name on Pump home's recent games on the computer (2026-10-27), where its quest pumps count as its pumps.

menu.yours.game.on.note: The game row's meta line once the paired computer says World of Warcraft has QuestPump, or a sheet of the addon's reached this phone.

menu.yours.on.note: The meta line of the Your QuestPump card's This phone row, and of Your watch while the watch app is on the paired watch.

menu.yours.watch.note: The Your QuestPump card's watch row.

menu.yours.watch.add.note: The watch row's step while the paired watch lacks QuestPump: the iPhone shows the steps in the Watch app, Android opens Play on the watch.

offers.computer.title.note: Heading of the one-time offer of the desktop app, at the first 7-day streak or level 5 while no computer is paired. QuestPump on your computer is QuestPump's own app for macOS and Windows.

offers.later.note: The quiet button of the milestone offers of QuestPump's other parts (2026-10-09), and of the Wear OS start page's phone card: puts the offer away for good; the Menu's Your QuestPump card keeps the part findable. Also the quiet button of the priming windows before Android's usage access, overlay and battery settings, of the Good game! sheet and of Pump home's offer card after a game (docs/phone-games.md).

offers.links.open.note: The offer's primary, which opens the Linked games page, and the Your QuestPump card's Linked games step while nothing is linked.

offers.links.title.note: Heading of the one-time offer of the linked games, after the third Start a pump with a kind a link offers (A match, A stream) while nothing is linked.

offers.pumpfirst.open.note: The offer's primary, which opens the Pump first page.

offers.pumpfirst.title.note: Heading of the one-time offer of Pump first, after the first finished pump on the phone while it is off: the offer's only words over Pick apps and Not now (2026-10-22: no line under it).

offers.watch.failed.text: Your watch didn't answer. Open the Play Store on it and look for QuestPump.
offers.watch.failed.note: Android: under Install on my watch when no watch opened the listing (out of reach, or it refused).

offers.watch.install.note: Android's primary: opens Play's listing of QuestPump on each paired Wear OS watch that lacks it.

offers.watch.sent.note: Android: under Install on my watch once a watch opened Play's listing; the window then closes.

offers.watch.step.find.note: The iPhone's step 2 of 3: the Watch app's section of apps whose watch app is not installed yet.

offers.watch.step.open.text: Open the Watch app on this iPhone
offers.watch.step.open.note: The iPhone's step 1 of 3 to install the watch app (Apple's Watch app, My Watch).

offers.watch.title.note: Heading of the one-time offer of the watch app, after the third app pump on a phone whose paired watch lacks QuestPump.

phonegames.about.text: QuestPump keeps only when a game opens and closes, and never tells us which game.
phonegames.about.note: The privacy line at the top of Games on this phone (the iPhone shows no priming window before the Shortcuts set-up).

phonegames.access.allow.note: Android: the state card's button, which opens the priming window See when you play, whose Open Settings turns the question after play on and opens Android's settings.

phonegames.access.off.text: Usage access is off, so no offer can show.
phonegames.access.off.note: Android: the state card's line before usage access was given, or after it was turned off.

phonegames.access.on.note: Android: the state card's heading while QuestPump may see which app is in front.

phonegames.add.note: Android: the quiet button that opens the picker of every launchable app.

phonegames.added.note: Android: the label over the apps the player added to the games.

phonegames.found.note: Android: the label over the launchable apps in Android's game category, each with a tick.

phonegames.intent.closed.note: The iPhone's App Intent in Shortcuts that the player's Is Closed automation runs for a game.

phonegames.intent.game.note: The name of both game intents' optional parameter in Shortcuts: the game's name, which the question then shows.

phonegames.intent.opened.note: The iPhone's App Intent in Shortcuts that the player's Is Opened automation runs for a game (its title, read as the key's literal).

phonegames.minute.note: The unit under Shortest session's minutes in its window's stepper when it is 1. The number stands over it.

phonegames.minutes.note: The unit under Shortest session's minutes in its window's stepper when it is not 1. The number stands over it.

phonegames.pick.note: Android: the heading of the picker window of every launchable app.

phonegames.played.note: The iPhone's control (Control Center, the Lock Screen, the Action button) and Android's Quick Settings tile: opens the Good game! sheet for any game.

phonegames.played.about.text: Say how many matches you played and get your pump.
phonegames.played.about.note: The I just played control's description in the control gallery.

phonegames.priming.body.text: To offer a pump after you play, QuestPump needs to see when your games open and close, also while it is closed. It keeps only your games' opens and closes and never tells us which games you play. Android asks next.
phonegames.priming.body.note: Android: the window's line, Play's prominent disclosure before the usage access settings (Games on this phone): what is read (when apps open and close, also in the background) and what is kept.

phonegames.priming.title.note: Android: the heading of the window before Android's usage access settings.

phonegames.priming.turnon.note: Android: the window's primary while usage access is already on (given for Pump first): it turns on the question after play without Android's settings.

phonegames.ready.text: Usage access is on for Pump first, but offers after you play are still off.
phonegames.ready.note: Android: the state card's line while usage access was given (from Pump first's page) but Games on this phone was never turned on, so no question comes after play.

phonegames.ready.allow.note: Android: the state card's button in that state, which opens the window See when you play; its Turn on starts the question after play.

phonegames.shortcut.open.note: The walks' button: opens Apple's Shortcuts app.

phonegames.shortcut.step1.text: Add an automation: App, pick your games, Is Opened, Run Immediately. Its action: Game opened.
phonegames.shortcut.step1.note: Step 1 of 3: the Shortcuts app's own words (App, Is Opened, Run Immediately) and the intent's title, as it shows them.

phonegames.shortcut.step2.text: Add a second one with Is Closed and the action Game closed.
phonegames.shortcut.step2.note: Step 2 of 3: the second automation, for the game's close.

phonegames.shortcut.step3.text: Open a game, then close it.
phonegames.shortcut.step3.note: Step 3 of 3: the test, whose state shows under it.

phonegames.shortest.note: The row and the heading of its Stepper window: the least minutes of play that offer a pump.

phonegames.test.note: The quiet button that posts the question for a 20-minute session of a game, outside the gap and the reminders a day.

phonegames.test.done.note: The walk's test state with its check once a game's open and close arrived.

phonegames.test.held.text: Not now: no offer can show right now.
phonegames.test.held.note: Under Send a test offer when quiet hours, the felt-unwell lock, a running pump or notifications hold it.

phonegames.test.wait.text: Waiting for a game to open and close
phonegames.test.wait.note: The walk's test state until a Game opened and a Game closed arrived.

phonegames.tile.text: Add I just played to Quick Settings
phonegames.tile.note: Android: the quiet button that asks the system to add the I just played tile.

phonegames.watching.note: Android: the state card's line while usage access is on; {count} is how many games are ticked.

places.add.note: Opens a new place's page (from a template, or empty). Gone once the list holds its most.

places.button.note: Read out only (TalkBack, the computer's screen reader and its tooltip) for Pump home's round place button, which shows the place in use's glyph and opens the places window: {place} is the place in use's name.

places.default.tag.note: A small tag at the end of the default place's row: the place in use whenever no time of the schedule applies (2026-11-03).

places.delete.note: The delete mark on a row of Edit places and the destructive primary of the place's confirm window.

places.delete.body.text: Its equipment and switches go with it. Your pumps and records stay.
places.delete.body.note: The confirm window's line under Delete {place}?: what goes and what stays.

places.delete.keep.note: The confirm window's quiet secondary under Delete: closes it and keeps the place.

places.delete.spoken.note: The delete mark's name for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's screen reader: {place} is the place's name.

places.delete.title.note: The heading of the confirm window before a place is deleted (the window's own, never a system alert): {place} is its name.

places.drag.hint.note: The drag handle's hint on each row of Edit places but Home (a touch and hold anywhere on the row drags it too).

places.edit.note: The places window's quiet button and the title of the page it opens: reorder, rename and delete places.

places.full.text: {count} places is the most. Delete one to add another.
places.full.note: In place of Add a place once the list holds places_max places (contract/places.json, 12).

plural.one: {count} place is the most. Delete one to add another.
plural.other: {count} places is the most. Delete one to add another.

places.gear.group.bars.note: An equipment group's name (2026-11-03, Rapha: "we have a lot more equipment shuold have an expand button"; contract/sheet.json gear_groups, the game's ns.GearGroups): the head of a group that opens and closes on a place's page and Your setup.

places.gear.group.cardio.note: An equipment group's name (2026-11-03, Rapha: "we have a lot more equipment shuold have an expand button"; contract/sheet.json gear_groups, the game's ns.GearGroups): the head of a group that opens and closes on a place's page and Your setup.

places.gear.group.core.note: An equipment group's name (2026-11-03, Rapha: "we have a lot more equipment shuold have an expand button"; contract/sheet.json gear_groups, the game's ns.GearGroups): the head of a group that opens and closes on a place's page and Your setup.

places.gear.group.count.note: At the end of an equipment group's head: how many of its pieces are ticked (3 of 5); none while none is.

places.gear.group.home.note: An equipment group's name (2026-11-03, Rapha: "we have a lot more equipment shuold have an expand button"; contract/sheet.json gear_groups, the game's ns.GearGroups): the head of a group that opens and closes on a place's page and Your setup.

places.gear.group.weights.note: An equipment group's name (2026-11-03, Rapha: "we have a lot more equipment shuold have an expand button"; contract/sheet.json gear_groups, the game's ns.GearGroups): the head of a group that opens and closes on a place's page and Your setup.

places.gear.more.note: After the first three pieces of a place's equipment in words (Dumbbells, Kettlebell, Jump rope + 9 more): how many more it has.

places.glyph.bars.note: The name of the place icon place_bars (contract/places.json glyphs) for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's tooltip.

places.glyph.bed.note: The name of the place icon place_bed (contract/places.json glyphs) for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's tooltip.

places.glyph.desk.note: The name of the place icon place_desk (contract/places.json glyphs) for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's tooltip.

places.glyph.dumbbell.note: The name of the place icon place_dumbbell (contract/places.json glyphs) for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's tooltip.

places.glyph.home.note: The name of the place icon place_home (contract/places.json glyphs) for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's tooltip.

places.glyph.peak.note: The name of the place icon place_peak (contract/places.json glyphs) for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's tooltip.

places.home.meta.note: Home's meta line on Edit places: Home is the game's one setup, the first place, never deleted or moved.

places.home.note.text: Home is your setup in the game. A change here reaches the game at your next login or reload, and one made in the game comes here.
places.home.note.note: On Home's page under its equipment: Home's equipment and switches travel between the game, the computer and the phones (the body's home field).

places.move.down.note: An action on each row of Edit places but Home: the place one step down.

places.move.up.note: An action on each row of Edit places but Home, for VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's keyboard (Alt and the up arrow): the place one step up, never above Home.

places.place.default.note: A switch on a place's page: on for the default place, the place in use whenever no time of the schedule applies; turning it on at another place moves the default there.

places.place.delete.note: The destructive quiet button under Save on a place's page (never Home's, never a new place's): asks its confirm first.

places.place.empty.note: The first choice under Start from, chosen at first (2026-11-03, Rapha: "new (which has minimal pre selected that should be widely available)"): a place with no equipment, floor moves and room to move on, quiet mode off.

places.place.from.note: Caps over a new place's row of templates and Empty: choosing one fills the equipment, the switches and the icon, never a name the player typed.

places.place.icon.note: Caps over a place's six icons to choose from.

places.place.name.note: The label of a place's name field (at most 24 characters).

places.place.name.empty.note: Under the name field while it is empty: Save waits for a name.

places.place.new.note: The title of a new place's page, before it is saved.

places.row.note: Caps label of Start a pump's place row and of Your setup's place section: the place in use (its equipment and its three switches decide which moves a pump can ask).

places.schedule.note: The places window's row and the title of the weekly schedule's pages (2026-11-03, Rapha: "Monday 18-20 you set it to gym"): which place is in use at which times of the week.

places.schedule.add.note: The schedule's quiet button: opens a new time's page.

places.schedule.times.note: The Schedule row's meta line while it holds more than one time.

places.setup.note.text: Your places sync between your phones and your computer. Each device picks its own place in use; Home is your setup in the game.
places.setup.note.note: Under Your setup's place section on a phone (slice 51): the places travel, the place in use stays the device's.

places.template.gym.note: A place template's words (contract/places.json 'gym': a gym's equipment, quiet mode off), shown while the player has not renamed the place.

places.template.home.note: A place template's words (contract/places.json 'home': the game's setup, the first place), shown while the player has not renamed the place.

places.template.hotel.note: A place template's words (contract/places.json 'hotel': no equipment, floor moves, room to move and quiet mode on), shown while the player has not renamed the place.

places.template.office.note: A place template's words (contract/places.json 'office': no equipment, no floor moves or room to move, quiet mode on), shown while the player has not renamed the place.

places.template.outdoors.note: A place template's words (contract/places.json 'outdoors': no equipment, floor moves and room to move on), shown while the player has not renamed the place.

places.template.park.note: A place template's words (contract/places.json 'park': a fixed bar and a pole outdoors), shown while the player has not renamed the place.

places.time.days.note: Caps over a time's seven weekday chips, Monday first.

places.time.delete.note: The destructive quiet button under Save on a kept time's page: deletes it at one tap.

places.time.meta.note: A time's meta line under its days: its span in the device's hour cycle, then its place's name (18:00–20:00 · Fitness centre).

places.time.place.note: Caps over the places to choose the time's place from.

places.time.to.note: Caps over the time's end; one before From runs past midnight.

places.title.note: The heading of the places window: where the player trains, each place with its own equipment and switches.

play.notready.text: QuestPump in your browser is not ready yet.
play.notready.note: The one heading questpump.com/play shows before the browser's QuestPump goes live (docs/plan.md slice 63): nothing works there yet, and nothing is saved.

privacy.accept.note: Button, the window's primary in an opt-in region (the EU, the EEA, India and Canada), where both switches start off, while the player has moved no switch in it: turns both on as the player's answers and closes the window. Learnclash's Accept all (2026-10-13). Never shown where they start on.

privacy.body.text: Choose what QuestPump may send. You can change it any time in the Menu.
privacy.body.note: Under the title of the privacy window.

privacy.done.note: Button, the window's one button outside an opt-in region, where both switches start on: keeps both as the player's answers, as they are set, and closes the window.

privacy.link.note: A link to questpump.com/privacy, what each switch sends and who gets it.

privacy.reject.note: Button, in an opt-in region the second button under the primary, a full button of the same size: turns both switches off as the player's answers and closes the window, so saying no takes one tap as saying yes does. Learnclash's Reject all (2026-10-13).

privacy.save.note: Button, the window's primary in an opt-in region once the player moved a switch in it (in Accept all's place): keeps both switches as set as the player's answers and closes the window. Learnclash's Save choices (2026-10-13).

privacy.title.note: Title of the window that asks, once, what QuestPump may send.

pro.active.note: The line under QuestPump Pro on the Menu's card and on Pro's page, with Pro.

pro.demo.note.text: This is a demo of QuestPump Pro with sample history.
pro.demo.note.note: Over every Pro screen while the demo helper is on, with Pro bought too; in the Share window, a line under the styles while the demo opens them without Pro. QuestPump Pro is the paid subscription's name.

pro.failed.text: Your purchase didn't go through. Try again, or check your payment method in the store.
pro.failed.note: Under the plans after a purchase that failed (never after a cancel).

pro.has.cards.text: More looks for your share cards.
pro.has.cards.note: What Pro adds, the share-card styles' line, after its glyph: the card's ground and edge, never the figure.

pro.has.charts.text: Charts of your stats, your muscles and your records over time.
pro.has.charts.note: What Pro adds, the charts' line, after its glyph.

pro.has.coach.text: Burnish, the coach: a short talk after the sets that matter, and the story of your week.
pro.has.coach.note: What Pro adds, the coach, after its glyph (the offer's moment shows it only to a player who did not decline the coach). Burnish is the coach's name.

pro.has.computer.text: Your weeks, charts and card styles in QuestPump on your computer too.
pro.has.computer.note: What Pro adds, the computer's line, after its glyph: Pro on a paired phone shows Pro's weeks, every chart and the share-card styles in QuestPump on the computer too. On Pro's page always; in an offer's moment only while this phone is paired with a computer. QuestPump is the product name.

pro.has.path.text: Your pace on every ladder: about how long its next goal may take you.
pro.has.path.note: What Pro adds, the Path's pace, after its glyph (2026-10-14; the Path's steps free since then): on each ladder's page, about how long the steps to the Path's goal (the first orange or gold step above the step now, else the ladder's top) may take at the player's own pace, a guess from the days between their own climbs.

pro.has.surfaces.text: Your week on the streak widget, and the next move in the pump's notification.
pro.has.surfaces.note: What Pro adds on the system's surfaces, after its glyph: the medium widget's week (the streak's count on every widget, complication and Tile is free since 2026-10-09) and the Live Update's next move's line (the moves' segments are free since 2026-10-14, as the iPhone's StepsBar).

pro.has.surfaces.ios.text: Your week on the streak widget, and the next move on the Lock Screen.
pro.has.surfaces.ios.note: What Pro adds on the system's surfaces, after its glyph: the medium widget's week (the streak's count on every widget and complication is free since 2026-10-09) and the Live Activity's next move's line (the Live Activity itself, its StepsBar, the move that runs and its clock are free since 2026-10-13, as Android's Live Update; these words since 2026-10-14).

pro.has.weeks.text: Your weeks: the days you played, your moves and your minutes.
pro.has.weeks.note: What Pro adds, the weeks' line, after its glyph (also the line under the Log's See Pro row until 2026-10-22).

pro.manage.note: A quiet button on Pro's page with Pro, and in Delete your account? while the store holds Pro: opens the store's page where the player changes or cancels the subscription.

pro.moment.moves.note: The peak's line over the lead in the Pro offer's moment that comes once the player's moves done on every device reach 60: {count} is the moves done so far.

pro.moment.notnow.note: Button: closes the Pro offer's moment; that moment does not come back by itself.

pro.moment.plans.note: Button: opens Pro's page with the plans and their prices.

pro.moment.streak.note: The peak's line over the lead in the Pro offer's moment that comes once the streak reaches 7 days: {days} is the streak's days now.

pro.moment.unlock.note: The peak's line over the lead in the Pro offer's moment that comes once a climb earns a Rare or higher step: {quality} is the colour's name as the ladders show it (Rare, Epic, Legendary, Artifact).

pro.none.text: Google Play does not offer Pro here right now.

pro.none.ios.text: The App Store does not offer Pro here right now.

pro.pending.text: Your purchase is waiting for its payment. Pro starts once it goes through.

pro.pending.ios.text: Your purchase waits for approval. Pro starts once it is approved.
pro.pending.ios.note: Under the plans when Ask to Buy holds a purchase.

pro.plan.after.note: The line right over Pro's Subscribe: the chosen plan's billed amount first, then what comes before it: {charge} as "$49.99 a year" (pro.plan.year), {start} as "1 month free" (pro.plan.free).

pro.plan.day.note: A price charged every day; {price} as the store shows it.

pro.plan.days.note: A length of time in a plan's terms.

pro.plan.every.note: A price charged every few days, weeks, months or years: {span} as "3 months".

pro.plan.free.note: A plan's free start. {span} is its length, such as "1 month".

pro.plan.month.note: A price charged every month; {price} as the store shows it.

pro.plan.week.note: A price charged every week; {price} as the store shows it.

pro.plan.weeks.note: A length of time in a plan's terms.

pro.plan.year.note: A price charged every year; {price} as the store shows it.

pro.plan.yearly.note: A plan's name on Pro's page: charged every year.

pro.plan.years.note: A length of time in a plan's terms.

pump.addon.open.note: The card's button: opens questpump.com/addon in the browser, where the addon for the computer downloads.

pump.addon.title.text: Add QuestPump to World of Warcraft
pump.addon.title.note: Heading of Pump home's card while the paired computer has World of Warcraft without QuestPump's addon. World of Warcraft is the game's name.

pump.channel.note: The name of the phone's notification channel for the countdown it runs, in the system's notification settings.

pump.channel.offer.note: The name of the Android phone's alerting notification channel, in the system's notification settings: a game pump offered while QuestPump is not in front pops up with its first move (2026-10-13).

pump.check.again.note: A result line after a stretch check not passed (slice 42): the pose is saved as practice with its XP.

pump.chip.action.note: TalkBack's action for the computer's status chip on Pump and Hero's source chip ("Double-tap to show your computer"): a tap opens the Menu's page for the computer (VoiceOver's hint is pump.chip.hint).

pump.chip.blind.note: Pump home's status chip while the paired computer answers but QuestPump there cannot see World of Warcraft (its screen permission is missing, or its reading stopped): no pump's countdown comes. QuestPump is the app's name. Since 2026-10-13 also the line of Android's ongoing notification while the phone follows the game (LinkLine, one owner with the chip).

pump.chip.here.note: The helper's status chip: connected, and each pump's countdown comes to this phone. {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.chip.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint for the computer's status chip on Pump and Hero's source chip: a tap shows the computer's page, its state and what fixes it (TalkBack's action is pump.chip.action).

pump.chip.newcode.note: The status chip when the helper has a new pairing code. {computer} is the computer's name. Since 2026-10-13 also the line of Android's ongoing notification while the phone follows the game (LinkLine, one owner with the chip).

pump.chip.reaching.note: The status chip while the phone tries to reach the helper, and since 2026-10-13 the line of Android's ongoing notification while its link tries. {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.chip.unreachable.note: The status chip when the helper does not answer. {computer} is the computer's name. Since 2026-10-13 also the line of Android's ongoing notification while the phone follows the game (LinkLine, one owner with the chip).

pump.chip.watch.note: The status chip while the watch's play session holds the link. {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.climb.again.note: A result line after the window that proves the next step did not pass (slice 53): saved other than Yes, to the end, or stopped; nothing changes, and the next session's first window tries again. The counted step's card says the same while the proving waits for that session (ns.Proving's waits), in the Next line's place, as the game's (Locales/enUS.lua ladders.step.climbWaits).

pump.count.cap.text: Up to {max}: 50% more than the {counted} counted
pump.count.cap.note: Under the count's dial while the count stands at its most (slice 66, Rapha, 2026-11-04: "dont allow it to do more than 50% more of what the app counted"): {max} is that most and {counted} what the app counted (the reps the figure ended by Done, the stopwatch's seconds), each in the move's unit, reps as a number (45, 30), seconds as m:ss (1:00, 0:40). Shown only while the count is at its most and what the app counted set it, never where a floor did; pump.count.cap.goal where a set of reps' goal did. The iPhone shows it once its count moves onto the dial (owed, slice 66).

pump.count.cap.goal.text: Up to {max}: 50% more than the {goal} to beat
pump.count.cap.goal.note: Under the count's dial while the count stands at its most and the number a set of reps has to beat set it (slice 66; David, 2026-11-04: "you fix and decide on the best"): the app counts at the figure's pace, far slower than a fast honest set, so a set of reps takes half again its goal (its record without one) where that passes what was counted. {max} is that most and {goal} that number, reps as a number (46, 31). Shown only while the count is at its most, never where a floor set it; pump.count.cap where what the app counted did. The iPhone shows it once its count moves onto the dial (owed, slice 66).

pump.count.clean.end.note: The first of a counted set's three answers (slice 53; Clean to the end from slice 42 until then), as equal as the others: all out with the form held to the end, so the set counts a clean day and its count can set a best; on the window that proves the next step it climbs.

pump.count.clean.label.note: The label of a counted set's optional count (slice 42): empty or 0 saves no count.

pump.count.form.note: The question after a counted set (slice 42; since slice 53 it asks the effort too): {move} the form (Squat thrusts). Its answers: Yes, to the end, Form slipped and Not all out.

pump.count.hold.note: The question after a hold: how long it was held. {move} is the move's name, such as Wall sit.

pump.count.hold.side.note: The question after a hold done on each side: the seconds of the weaker side. {move} is the move's name.

pump.count.kg.note: Label of the weight box beside the reps on a move done with a weight (a dumbbell, a kettlebell, a bag): the weight in kilograms, pre-filled with the weight planned for the set.

pump.count.kg.each.note: Label of the weight box on a move with a weight in each hand: the kilograms of one of them.

pump.count.none.note: A counted set's optional count left empty or at 0 (slice 42): the stepper's value and the result's word, and since 2026-10-19 the Saga's and a pump page's word for such a set (HistoryPump.Move's counted with no reps; the game's Log says ui.result.cleanNone).

pump.count.notallout.note: The third of a counted set's three answers (slice 53): the player did not go all out; as Form slipped, the set is saved with its XP, counts no clean day and sets no best.

pump.count.preview.load.note: What the count step will save on a move with a weight: {count} the reps, {kg} the weight in kilograms with at most one decimal (12.5).

pump.count.preview.load.each.note: What the count step will save on a move with a weight in each hand: {count} the reps, {kg} the kilograms of each (12.5).

pump.count.reps.note: The question after a move of reps. {move} is the move's name, such as Desk push-up.

pump.count.reps.side.text: {move}: how many on your weaker side?
pump.count.reps.side.note: The question after a move of reps done on each side: the count of the weaker side. {move} is the move's name.

pump.count.save.note: Button: keeps the count on the stepper.

pump.count.slipped.note: The second of a counted set's three answers (slice 42): the set is saved with its XP, counts no clean day and sets no best.

pump.countdown.first.note: Heading over the countdown of a move done on one side, then the other.

pump.countdown.switch.note: Heading over the countdown between a move's two sides.

pump.done.back.ladder.note: Button at the Result of a pump started from a step's card or a move's window, in place of Continue: back to where it started, the ladder's page whose step card started it.

pump.done.back.list.note: Button at the Result of a pump started from a step's card or a move's window, in place of Continue: back to where it started, Book's list of ladders, from a ladder not open yet.

pump.done.back.move.note: Button at the Result of a pump started from a step's card or a move's window, in place of Continue: back to where it started, the move's window or its page.

pump.done.back.tree.note: Button at the Result of a pump started from a step's card or a move's window, in place of Continue: back to where it started, the talent tree, the started step selected and in view (its card closed; a tap on it opens the card again). Since 2026-10-29 only the iPhone shows it, until its twin of the ladders and their paths lands (docs/ui.md, "The Book's ladders and paths"), which Android and the computer show.

pump.done.banked.text: Its moves come back in your next pump.
pump.done.banked.note: The line under Banked in the game: banked moves are owed and ride the next pump.

pump.done.banked.title.note: Title of the result when the player banked the pump in the game.

pump.done.continue.note: Button at a pump's end: back to the Pump screen.

pump.done.early.note: Title of the calm result of a pump the player left part way: no fanfare.

pump.done.ended.text: The pump ended before a move ran.
pump.done.ended.note: A game pump the game ended (banked, or a fight) before any move ran.

pump.done.experience.note: Caps label under the experience points the pump earned.

pump.done.gameasked.text: The game asked for its own pump, so this one ended here.
pump.done.gameasked.note: Calm card's line when the game offered its own pump while an app pump ran on the phone or the computer (one pump at a time, as on the watch): the moves done stay.

pump.done.gameruns.text: The game is running, so these moves come in its next pump.
pump.done.gameruns.note: A catch-up pump's end on the phone once QuestPump on the computer answered while World of Warcraft with QuestPump runs there, and a catch-up's end on the computer when that client started while it ran (which ends it at once): the game asks the unfinished moves itself, so this catch-up paid none of them and they stay unfinished.

pump.done.lapsed.text: Press Start in the game, and the pump comes back here.
pump.done.lapsed.note: Start is the game's own button on its pump window.

pump.done.lapsed.title.note: Title of the result when the game offered a pump and never started it.

pump.done.load.next.note: After a set with a weight: the weight {kg} and the reps {target} the next fresh set of this move will ask (heavier once the top came twice).

pump.done.load.next.each.note: After a set with a weight in each hand: the kilograms of each {kg} and the reps {target} the next fresh set will ask.

pump.done.lost.text: Can't reach {computer}. Finish the pump in the game.
pump.done.lost.note: {computer} is the name of the computer the helper runs on.

pump.done.lost.title.note: Title of the result when the phone stopped reaching QuestPump on the computer during a game pump.

pump.done.paused.note: The line under Paused in the game.

pump.done.paused.title.note: Title of the result when the player paused the character in the game, which ended this pump.

pump.done.reload.text: The game pauses its pumps too the next time it loads.
pump.done.reload.note: After a felt-unwell stop on the phone while paired: the game reads the lock when it loads again.

pump.done.rest.note: After a pump ended for feeling unwell.

pump.done.rest.until.text: Rest now. Pumps stay locked until {time}.
pump.done.rest.until.note: {time} is a time of day, such as 4:00 AM.

pump.done.sent.text: Sent to your computer. The game shows it the next time it loads.
pump.done.sent.note: A catch-up pump reached QuestPump on the computer.

pump.done.skipped.note: The line under Ended early when the game ended a game pump short of done without banking or pausing it: every move skipped, a reset or a restored backup, a stand-up dropped.

pump.done.typecounts.text: Type your counts in the game.
pump.done.typecounts.note: A game pump's end, until the game's sheet says what it paid, where a move of reps or a hold ran: its counts are typed in the game.

pump.done.waiting.text: Waiting for your computer: it goes as soon as the phone reaches it.
pump.done.waiting.note: A catch-up pump waits to be sent to QuestPump on the computer.

pump.figure.action.note: TalkBack's action on the still figure (animations off): a tap plays one repetition.

pump.figure.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint on the still figure (Reduce Motion on): a tap plays one repetition.

pump.figure.label.text: The move, shown by the armour figure
pump.figure.label.note: The accessibility label of the move's figure: an armour that plays one repetition of the move.

pump.figure.right.note: Under the still of a move done right (its key pose), beside a check mark; the still beside it shows the move done wrong. The still's spoken label is pump.figure.right.label.

pump.figure.right.label.note: Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the still of the move done well. {move} is the move's name (Forearm plank).

pump.figure.wrong.note: Under the still of a move done wrong (a common fault), beside a cross; the fault's words, such as Hips sag toward the floor, follow under it.

pump.figure.wrong.label.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the still of a move done wrong. {fault} is the fault's words from the move list, such as Hips sag toward the floor.

pump.follow.allow.health.note: The follow card's button and the helper page's while Apple Health was never asked: shows Health's own permission sheet (2026-10-14). Apple Health is Apple's app: keep its name.

pump.follow.ble.allow.note: Asks Android's Nearby devices permission again.

pump.follow.ble.denied.ios.text: QuestPump may not use Bluetooth on this {device}. Allow it in Settings to follow the game while it's locked.
pump.follow.ble.denied.ios.note: The iPhone's state ble_denied (2026-10-17): Settings turned off QuestPump's Bluetooth or its accessory's access, while this device's Bluetooth is on. Open Settings goes to QuestPump's page there. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad (AboutPage.device; 2026-10-19).

pump.follow.ble.nearby.text: Allow Nearby devices for QuestPump, so this phone can follow the game by Bluetooth.
pump.follow.ble.nearby.note: Nearby devices is Android's name for the permission: use the system's own words.

pump.follow.ble.off.text: Bluetooth is off on this phone. Turn it on so pumps reach it also away from your Wi-Fi.
pump.follow.ble.off.note: Android follows the game with the screen off on Wi-Fi already: the line names only what Bluetooth adds (2026-10-17).

pump.follow.ble.off.ios.text: Bluetooth is off on this {device}. Turn it on in Control Center to follow the game while it's locked.
pump.follow.ble.off.ios.note: {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad (AboutPage.device; 2026-10-19).

pump.follow.ble.start.note: The follow card's button: links {computer}, the computer's name, by Bluetooth (2026-10-22: no line over it).

pump.follow.ble.turnon.note: Opens Android's question to turn Bluetooth on.

pump.follow.control.about.text: Shows each pump from the game on your Lock Screen.
pump.follow.control.about.note: The Follow the game control's description in the control gallery (2026-10-14).

pump.follow.game.note: While the phone follows a running game in the background (the helper's game_asks, 2026-10-13): the line of Android's ongoing notification between pumps, its private content (its public version says live.following), and the iPhone's Live Activity between pumps, in the Dynamic Island alone (the Lock Screen's says live.following). {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.follow.needs.health.text: To follow the game on the Lock Screen, let QuestPump save workouts in Apple Health.
pump.follow.needs.health.note: Pump home's follow card on the iPhone while Apple Health may not save QuestPump's workouts: the play session that keeps following the game with the phone locked needs it (2026-10-14). Apple Health is Apple's app: keep its name.

pump.follow.needs.live.text: Live Activities are off for QuestPump. Turn them on to see each pump on your Lock Screen.
pump.follow.needs.live.note: Pump home's follow card on the iPhone while the player turned Live Activities off for QuestPump in Settings (2026-10-14); Open Settings goes there. Live Activities is Apple's name for the feature: use its words in the language.

pump.follow.needs.notify.text: Notifications are off for QuestPump, so pumps can't show with the screen off.
pump.follow.needs.notify.note: Pump home's follow card on Android while QuestPump's notifications are off, or its pump channel (Countdown on this phone) or its offer channel (Pumps from the game) is (2026-10-14); Open Settings opens that channel's page, or the app's notification settings.

pump.follow.needs.promote.text: Live Updates are off for QuestPump. Turn them on to see each pump at the top of your screen.
pump.follow.needs.promote.note: Pump home's follow card on Android 16 QPR2 (API 36.1) and later, where apps request promotion, while the player turned Live Updates off for QuestPump (2026-10-14); Open Settings opens that setting, or the app's notification settings where a phone lacks it. Live Updates is Android's name for the feature: use its words in the language.

pump.follow.open.text: Open QuestPump to follow the game.
pump.follow.open.note: What the Follow the game control says where it cannot start following without the app: the iPhone is not paired, Live Activities are off for QuestPump, Apple Health may not save workouts, or the session or its Live Activity cannot start in the background (2026-10-14).

pump.follow.start.note: The iPhone's button on Pump home and its control in Control Center, on the Lock Screen and on the Action button (2026-10-14): starts following the game on the paired computer, so each pump from it shows on the Lock Screen. A verb phrase.

pump.follow.stop.note: Ends the phone's following of the game: the action on Android's ongoing notification, until QuestPump is opened again, and the button on the iPhone's Live Activity, until QuestPump is opened again or Follow the game is tapped (2026-10-13; Follow the game since 2026-10-14). A verb.

pump.follow.waiting.note: While the phone follows the paired computer and no game runs there yet: the line of Android's ongoing notification (2026-10-13), its private content (its public version says live.waiting), and the iPhone's Live Activity after Follow the game started it before the game was heard (2026-10-14), in the Dynamic Island alone (the Lock Screen's says live.waiting). {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.guide.pause.note: The same button while it reads: stops the reading where it is.

pump.guide.read.note: Button by How on the computer's Ready view and at the foot of the countdown and a running move: reads the move's How and Tips aloud in the game's own voice, as the game's button does.

pump.guide.resume.note: The same button once paused: reads on from the line it paused in.

pump.held.text: {count} moves come with your next quest in the game

plural.one: {count} move comes with your next quest in the game
plural.other: {count} moves come with your next quest in the game

pump.held.note: {count} is how many owed moves the game puts into its next pump.

pump.helper.ble.ask.text: Open the Phones page of QuestPump on {computer} and allow Bluetooth there.
pump.helper.ble.ask.note: The computer has not answered QuestPump's Bluetooth question yet (ble ask).

pump.helper.ble.away.note: The Bluetooth link row's state: linked, the computer not in Bluetooth range now.

pump.helper.ble.computeroff.text: Bluetooth is off on {computer}. Turn it on there to link by Bluetooth.

pump.helper.ble.linked.note: The Bluetooth link row's state: linked and in reach.

pump.helper.ble.none.text: {computer} has no Bluetooth, so this phone follows the game on Wi-Fi.

pump.helper.ble.noperipheral.text: The Bluetooth on {computer} can't link phones, so this phone follows the game on Wi-Fi.
pump.helper.ble.noperipheral.note: ble no_peripheral: a Windows PC whose Bluetooth adapter cannot serve phones.

pump.helper.ble.refused.text: QuestPump on {computer} may not use Bluetooth. Its Phones page there says where to allow it.
pump.helper.ble.refused.note: ble no_grant: the computer refused QuestPump's Bluetooth (macOS's Privacy & Security, or Windows' privacy settings or a policy). The phone cannot tell a Mac from a PC, so the words send the player to the computer's Phones page, which names the place (2026-10-17).

pump.helper.ble.stopped.text: QuestPump on {computer} has its Bluetooth link off. Its Phones page turns it back on.
pump.helper.ble.stopped.note: ble stopped: the player turned the link off on the computer, or it could not start there.

pump.helper.blind.text: QuestPump on {computer} can't see the game, so no countdown comes. Its window there says why.
pump.helper.blind.note: On the helper's page under the link's state, while QuestPump on the computer cannot see World of Warcraft (its screen permission is missing, or its reading stopped). {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.helper.connecting.note: The helper page while the link comes up (right after pairing, or as a session starts), until the helper's first answer or a failure. {computer} is the computer's name.

pump.helper.linked.note: {computer} is the computer's name. Since 2026-10-13 also the line of Android's ongoing notification while the phone follows the game (LinkLine, one owner with the chip).

pump.helper.localnetwork.text: QuestPump can't use your Wi-Fi network. Turn on Local Network for QuestPump in Settings.
pump.helper.localnetwork.note: iPhone only. Local Network and Settings are iOS's names: use the iPhone's names in the language.

pump.helper.lookagain.note: Button: searches the network for the computer again.

pump.helper.looking.note: {computer} is the computer's name: the phone searches the network for it.

pump.helper.newcode.text: {computer} has a new pairing code. Scan the code QuestPump shows on it.
pump.helper.newcode.note: {computer} is the computer's name. QuestPump is the app's name.

pump.helper.noanswer.text: {computer} doesn't answer. Is it awake, with QuestPump open on it? A guest Wi-Fi or 'client isolation' keeps devices apart: use your main Wi-Fi.
pump.helper.noanswer.note: {computer} is the computer's name. QuestPump is the app's name. Client isolation is a router setting.

pump.helper.none.note: Status: the app is not connected to QuestPump on a computer.

pump.helper.othernetwork.text: {computer} was last on another network. Put this phone on the same Wi-Fi as that computer, not a guest network.

pump.helper.paired.note: {computer} is the computer's name: paired, but not connected right now. Since 2026-10-13 also the line of Android's ongoing notification while the phone follows the game (LinkLine, one owner with the chip).

pump.helper.phone.note: Status: each pump's countdown shows on this phone. Also the title of the phone's countdown notification on Android. Android's; the iPhone's is pump.helper.phone.ios.

pump.helper.phone.ios.note: Status: each pump's countdown shows on this phone. Also the title of the phone's countdown notification on Android. The iPhone's twin of pump.helper.phone. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

pump.helper.reaching.text: Can't reach {computer}: is it awake, with QuestPump open, on the same Wi-Fi?
pump.helper.reaching.note: {computer} is the computer's name. QuestPump is the app's name.
