pump.helper.scannew.note: Button: opens the scanner for the helper's new pairing code.

pump.helper.simulate.note: Button: plays a quest turned in, as the game would send it.

pump.helper.startfailed.text: Open QuestPump on your watch and tap Start session.
pump.helper.startfailed.note: The watch did not start. Start session is the watch app's button: keep its name.

pump.helper.startwatch.note: Button: starts a play session on the watch.

pump.helper.watch.note: Status: the watch shows each pump's countdown. Since 2026-10-13 also the title of Android's ongoing notification while the watch's play session holds the link and the phone follows the game (the phone keeps its service then, to take the link back).

pump.hold.ask.little.note: The hold ask's second answer (slice 52): a few more seconds were left.

pump.hold.ask.lot.note: The hold ask's third answer (slice 52): much more was left, so the ladder's next fresh goal leaps toward what the player can hold (never with Avoid breath-hold strain on).

pump.hold.ask.no.note: The hold ask's first answer (slice 52): the hold ended where the player could go no further.

pump.hold.ask.title.note: The hold ask (slice 52), after the count's Save and before the set is saved: a fresh hold of the wall sit, core, side or L-sit ladder whose time beat its goal by at most 5 s past the next multiple of 5 above it, while the Stamina Ledger is unsure of that hold, once a ladder a game day; never after a warm set, a max set, a miss or a power set. Its answer goes in the hold's row (No 1, A little 2, A lot 3).

pump.home.embers.note: Pump home's ember row (slice 55, the word ember left the screens on 2026-10-29: the count says what it counts; the game's HUD line): the embers lit this game day, {have} of the {need} a day lights (embers_day, 3), beside three ember glyphs, filled or hollow. An ember is a cardio move done in full: an all-out window that ran its time (a counted one saved Yes, to the end), a steady move paced at the player's own step or above (the step its dose was set at, whatever the form's own step) that ran its time without I eased off, or a Long Haul with a Yes. Its tap starts a cardio move of the player's step at once (its Ready view, the step's card's Start; since 2026-11-03, Rapha: the step's card it opened until then left the goal unclear), and the row carries that move's tile. No streak of embers, no loss words. Since 2026-10-29 also the Result's row on a pump with a cardio move, beside the same pips.

pump.home.start.note: The iPhone's Start a pump (Pump home, the empty Hero, Book and Saga): opens what the player finished (A quest, A match, A level, A boss fight, A work block) and its size, then the pump. Android and the computer start a Quick pump with a length there since slice 51; the iPhone follows on its own branch.

pump.home.streak.label.note: The caps label under the streak's day count (the big number), as in 12 / DAY STREAK, on Pump home, the widgets and since slice 45 the streak card.

pump.home.streak.line.note: The line over the streak on Pump, on the widgets and since slice 45 at the top of the streak card (David's pick, 2026-10-06). A quest is the game's task the player turns in; one pump a day keeps the streak.

pump.home.streak.resting.note: After I feel unwell: pumps are locked until the next game day, and that day keeps the streak without a rest token. On the widgets it stands in place of the today line while the lock holds and today has no pump yet.

pump.home.streak.resting.none.note: The line while the felt-unwell lock holds and no streak counts (pump.home.streak.resting names a streak, so it shows only while one counts).

pump.home.streak.share.note: The name of the StreakBoard's round Share button (read aloud, and the computer's tooltip), from a 7-day streak: opens the streak card in the Share window (slice 45).

pump.home.streak.today.done.note: Today's game day has a pump, so the streak counts it; also the Result's line over Apps open once that pump opened the apps that waited.

pump.home.streak.today.open.note: Today's game day has no pump yet. Never words of loss or a deadline.

pump.home.streak.tokens.note: The rest tokens held: each covers a day off so the streak goes on. Earned, never bought.

pump.joints.save.note: Button: flags the joints switched on.

pump.kind.boss.note: One of the six things a player finished that ask for an app pump (a fight against a boss finished): an item of You finished, and the first words of the pump's title (A match · two moves). Keep the article.

pump.kind.level.note: One of the six things a player finished that ask for an app pump (a level, a stage or a dungeon finished): an item of You finished, and the first words of the pump's title (A match · two moves). Keep the article.

pump.kind.match.note: One of the six things a player finished that ask for an app pump (a match or a round against other players finished): an item of You finished, and the first words of the pump's title (A match · two moves). Keep the article.

pump.kind.quest.note: One of the six things a player finished that ask for an app pump (a quest in a game (or a task) finished): an item of You finished, and the first words of the pump's title (A match · two moves). Keep the article.

pump.kind.stream.note: One of the six things a player finished that ask for an app pump (a live stream the player ran finished, such as on Twitch): an item of You finished, and the first words of the pump's title (A stream · two moves). Keep the article.

pump.kind.work.note: One of the six things a player finished that ask for an app pump (a block of work or study finished, away from any game): an item of You finished, and the first words of the pump's title (A match · two moves). Keep the article.

pump.leave.free.text: The moves you did are kept.
pump.leave.free.note: Leaving the player's own pump part way.

pump.leave.free.none.note: Leaving the player's own pump before any move was done: nothing is kept.

pump.leave.owed.text: The moves left wait for later.
pump.leave.owed.note: Leaving a catch-up pump part way, or a match pump on one of its riders (docs/plan.md slice 61): the moves done are paid, the others stay unfinished.

pump.leave.owed.none.text: The moves stay banked. Catch up later.
pump.leave.owed.none.note: Leaving a catch-up pump, or a match pump on one of its riders (docs/plan.md slice 61), before any move was done.

pump.leave.title.note: Title of the window before leaving a pump the phone runs.

pump.length.minutes.note: A length in the Menu's Quick pump length row (2026-11-03: 5 min, 10 min, 15 min, 20 min, 30 min, contract/library.json's expedition_lengths_min). The min is short for minutes and takes no plural.

pump.line.hint.note: VoiceOver's hint for a move's tooltip in the Book: a tap shows the move with its cue and when to stop (TalkBack's action there is ladders.tip.action).

pump.live.clockswitch.text: The clock switches sides for you.
pump.live.clockswitch.note: A line of the running notification on a one-sided timed move's first side: its clock starts the other side by itself (Switch sides still ends a side early).

pump.live.game.note: A game pump's move runs; the game ends it. Android's countdown notification, and the running screen's line on a timed game move, where nothing is typed (finding type-counts-copy).

pump.live.getready.note: Title of the phone's countdown notification before a move.

pump.live.pump.note: Title of the countdown notification when no move is named. A noun.

pump.live.ready.note: The short chip in the status bar before the countdown's first digit: one short word.

pump.live.save.note: The move waits for its count in the app.

pump.live.starts.note: The countdown notification's line when no move is named yet.

pump.live.switch.note: Title of the countdown notification between a move's two sides.

pump.live.tapdone.text: Tap Done in QuestPump when it ends.
pump.live.tapdone.note: Done is the app's button: keep its name as translated there.

pump.live.tapstart.text: Tap Start in QuestPump when you are ready.
pump.live.tapstart.note: Start is the app's button: keep its name as translated there.

pump.live.tapswitch.text: Tap Switch sides when this side ends.
pump.live.tapswitch.note: A line of the running notification on the first side of a one-sided move that runs until the player ends it (a hold counting up past its goal, a move of reps counting on): only the Pump tab's Switch sides button ends the side (use pump.running.switch's words).

pump.mark.ask.good.note: An answer to How close to the goal pose? (listed Perfect, Good, Okay, Not yet; on a keyboard each on the key of its code, 4 Perfect to 1 Not yet): almost the full pose; counts toward the next step, unless the next step's pose is risky.

pump.mark.ask.notyet.note: An answer to How close to the goal pose? (listed Perfect, Good, Okay, Not yet; on a keyboard each on the key of its code, 4 Perfect to 1 Not yet): far from the pose; practice, gentle: never a failure.

pump.mark.ask.okay.note: An answer to How close to the goal pose? (listed Perfect, Good, Okay, Not yet; on a keyboard each on the key of its code, 4 Perfect to 1 Not yet): about halfway to the pose; practice, the day counts toward nothing.

pump.mark.ask.perfect.note: An answer to How close to the goal pose? (listed Perfect, Good, Okay, Not yet; on a keyboard each on the key of its code, 4 Perfect to 1 Not yet): the full pose, as the figure and the mark show it; counts toward the next step, and on an orange step no hold has earned yet earns its colour.

pump.mark.ask.title.text: How close to the goal pose?
pump.mark.ask.title.note: Question after a pose of the player's own pumps whose step sets a goal pose ran its whole time (2026-10-09; once a game day, below the family's top or on an orange step no hold has earned yet): how close the player came to the goal pose, as the figure and the sentence under the Goal pose label show it. The answer decides whether the day counts toward the next step (2026-10-14: was How close did you get?, which named no goal).

pump.matches.ask.note: The question over the sheet's stepper.

pump.matches.match.note: The unit under the matches in the Good game! sheet's stepper when it is 1. The number stands over it.

pump.matches.matches.note: The unit under the matches in the Good game! sheet's stepper when it is not 1. The number stands over it.

pump.matches.played.note: The sheet's and Pump home's offer card's line under Good game!: the game's name and the session's minutes.

pump.matches.played.any.note: The same line when no game's name is known (the iPhone's automation named none).

pump.matches.size.note: The size the matches give, as a word: {size} is Light, Balanced or Extreme (pump.size.*; Small, Normal or Big, as "A {size} pump", until 2026-10-27; slice 48: the longer of the session's own minutes, where the phone knows them, and the matches times the game's minutes per match, one step per match_step_min, 12 minutes since slice 59 and 20 before it, half up, from Light to Extreme, so under 18 minutes Light, 18-29 Balanced, 30 or more Extreme; before slice 48 the matches alone, 1 Light, 2 or 3 Balanced, 4 or more Extreme); not shown while Moves per match is Light, where every size is the same one move; no move count or minutes before Ready.

pump.more.how.note: Row in a pump's More window after its Ready view, which shows the move in full itself: shows the move with its steps, tips and when to stop.

pump.more.pain.note: Row in a pump's More window on the watch, and on the phones and the computer an item of the menu of a pump's Pause on its Ready view (its submenu's title on the phones), in the game's words (its Pause menu's "Something hurts"): says where it hurts; moves that load it leave the pump.

pump.move.note: The name of a pump started from a step's card or a move's window (slice 36), as the game names it: the title of its Ready view, the first words of its title (A pump you asked for · 1 move) and its Log row, on the computer's Saga too (its own pump's row). It carries no unfinished moves.

pump.moves.count.note: How many moves a pump has, after the dot in its title (Game pump · 2 moves); always in digits. {count} is the number.

pump.moves.none.note: Fills {moves} in a pump's title, after the dot: Game pump · two moves.

pump.notice.body.text: First: {move}. Tap to follow your pumps on the Lock Screen.
pump.notice.body.note: {move} is the pump's first move's name; the tap opens QuestPump and shows the pump on the Lock Screen. Only while Live Activities are on for QuestPump (pump.notice.body.off otherwise).

pump.notice.body.off.text: First: {move}. Press Start in the game when you are ready.
pump.notice.body.off.note: The stand-in notice's body while Live Activities are off for QuestPump, when no tap can show the pump on the Lock Screen (2026-10-17). {move} is the pump's first move's name; Start is a button in the game: keep it as the game names it.

pump.notice.title.note: The notice a pump from the game posts on a locked iPhone while no Live Activity shows (slice 43).

pump.objective.heart.note: The helper saw the heart rate rise: read by a screen reader for the heart beside a move, and shown on a game pump's result before its peak.

pump.offer.caps.stream.note: Pump home's offer card's caps while a linked stream's finish offers the pump (docs/phone-games.md B8); a game's offer carries no caps since slice 57, its Start names the game (games.pump).

pump.pace.eased.note: The pace ask's third answer (slice 42; one of three since slice 52): the player slowed before the end (flag bits 14-15: 2). The Stamina Ledger shortens the player's steady moves and counts no full move.

pump.pace.easily.note: The pace ask's first answer (slice 52): the player kept the pace to the end with room to spare (flag bits 14-15: 3). The Stamina Ledger lengthens the player's steady moves the most; on the player's own timed step at its full 45 s it counts a full move.

pump.pace.easy.text: Easy and steady, just keep moving.
pump.pace.easy.note: The pace of a match pump's warm cardio move in words, in place of its rung's pump.pace.rung<r> on its Ready and Running views on every surface, the watches included (slice 48's double-check: after a long sit at the computer the first move runs easy, and asks no pace after it). The game's cadence.standup, the take the voice says at its go. No word of health or the heart (no medical claim).

pump.pace.held.note: The pace ask's second answer (slice 52; Yes, the whole time from slice 42 until then): the player kept the pace to the end with little to spare. It keeps the old held answer's code (flag bits 14-15: 1), so an older row reads as this cautious yes. The Stamina Ledger lengthens the player's steady moves a little; on the player's own timed step at its full 45 s it counts a full move.

pump.pace.rung1.text: Quick and steady, too out of breath for full sentences.
pump.pace.rung1.note: The pace of a steady cardio move in words, on its Ready and Running views on every surface, the watches included (slice 42's fix round, 2026-10-17: the pace ask's "that pace" stated without the voice, the talk test the cadence lines set; the game's cadence.rung1, the take the voice says at the go): a steady move of cardio rung 1. A move of rung r reads pump.pace.rung<r> up to rung 6, and rung 6's from rung 7 (slice 52: those steady moves are the forms of rungs 4 to 6); never an all-out window, a counted set or the stand-up move.

pump.pace.rung2.text: Fast, too out of breath for full sentences.
pump.pace.rung2.note: As pump.pace.rung1, a steady move of cardio rung 2 (the game's cadence.rung2).

pump.pace.rung3.note: As pump.pace.rung1, a steady move of cardio rung 3 (the game's cadence.rung3).

pump.pace.rung4.text: Fast and light, too fast to talk.
pump.pace.rung4.note: As pump.pace.rung1, a steady move of cardio rung 4 (the game's cadence.rung4).

pump.pace.rung5.text: Hard rhythm, land softly, too fast to talk.
pump.pace.rung5.note: As pump.pace.rung1, a steady move of cardio rung 5 (the game's cadence.rung5).

pump.pace.rung6.text: Strong and hard, too fast to talk.
pump.pace.rung6.note: As pump.pace.rung1, a steady move of cardio rung 6 (the game's cadence.rung6), and of every step above it (slice 52).

pump.pace.title.text: Did you keep that pace to the end?
pump.pace.title.note: The pace ask's question (slice 42, 2026-10-17; since slice 52 the Stamina Ledger's ask, ns.LedgerAsk): after a steady cardio move of any step that ran its time, once a pump, while the ledger is unsure of the player's pace, when the move could count a full move or when it has not asked for a week, and after every Long Haul (slice 55); never after an all-out window, a counted set, a warm move or the stand-up move. Its answers: Yes, easily, Yes, just and I eased off. The cadence lines set the pace by the talk test, and this asks whether the player kept it. The voice says it as the ask opens (ask.pace).

pump.phase.count.note: The phase of a counted set from its go (slice 42; Count every rep until then), with no count goal under it.

pump.phase.fast.note: Phase: as fast as you can.

pump.plist.motion.text: QuestPump counts your steps during a pump timed on this device.
pump.plist.motion.note: The system's question before the app reads the step counter. Says "this device", not "phone": an Info.plist string takes no placeholder, and the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

pump.questdone.kind.note: Label over the six plain kinds (A quest, A match, A level, A boss fight, A stream, A work block): what the player just finished, which the pump stands for.

pump.questdone.size.note: Label of the choice of the pump's size: Light, Balanced or Extreme (pump.size.*; Small, Normal or Big until 2026-10-27).

pump.questdone.start.note: Button: starts the pump for the quest picked.

pump.questdone.title.note: Title of the window that picks what the player finished and its size.

pump.questdone.watch.note: Button in Start a pump and the Good game! sheet: the watch composes and runs this pump, of the kind and size chosen here.

pump.questdone.watch.failed.text: Your watch didn't answer. Open QuestPump on it, then try again.
pump.questdone.watch.failed.note: Shown when the phone could not hand the pump to the watch (out of reach, the watch app closed or not installed).

pump.questdone.watch.sent.note: A short line once the phone has handed the pump to the watch, which composes it unless a pump is on the wrist already.

pump.quick.note: The one-tap pump's name (2026-10-07): the gold button of the Pump screen while Quick is picked in its length row (slice 51), of the empty Hero, Book and Saga (a quiet one under Catch up while moves wait) and of the watch's pick, the phones' widgets' gold capsule and Start form (Home Screen and Lock Screen), which start it as a reminder's tap does, and the first words of its title (Quick pump · two moves) where an app pump's title shows what the player finished. The app picks its moves from the player's records and plan: one move, or two when a strength or hold move is due. Nothing to choose, no window.

pump.quick.hint.text: Starts the moves you need most now
pump.quick.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint) for the Quick pump button: it starts at once a pump of the moves the app picks for the player, with nothing to choose. Apple's hints start with a verb in the third person.

pump.ready.allout.note: A counted set's goal on its Ready view over its seconds (30 s), and on the watch's Ready row (slice 42), no number to reach.

pump.ready.allout.clean.note: A counted set's goal on its Ready view (slice 42), no number to reach.

pump.ready.bank.note: Button on the Ready view of a pump a match sized while a move of its own is left at or after the one on Ready (the game's Bank all, docs/plan.md slices 58 and 61): one click, no confirm; every move of its own not done yet waits as unfinished and rides the next pump, and its riders stay unfinished. Shown only while the device links the desktop app.

pump.ready.bank.rest.note: Button on every catch-up's Ready view and on a match pump's rider once only its riders are left, and past Ready in End the pump here's place on both, and since 2026-11-02 on the watches' Ready of an unfinished move, where it leaves that one move unfinished and goes back to the unfinished list (the game's Bank the rest, docs/plan.md slices 17, 58 and 61): one click, the moves done count and the moves left wait as unfinished; a match pump ends done, with its Result.

pump.ready.best.note: Under a counted set's goal on its Ready view and over the form step's count row after the set (slice 42): the form's best clean count, a record, never a goal.

pump.ready.body.note: The title of the group in the menu of a pump's Pause that holds Something hurts and I feel unwell (the second where the device makes offers), in the game's words (Locales ui.pause.body).

pump.ready.carry.text: {seconds} s with a load that makes the last 10 s hard
pump.ready.carry.note: A carry: walking with a weight. {seconds} is a number of seconds.

pump.ready.carry.side.text: {seconds} s each side with a load that makes the last 10 s hard
pump.ready.carry.side.note: A carry on one side, then the other. {seconds} is a number of seconds.

pump.ready.end.note: Button: ends the pump without the moves left.

pump.ready.flow.side.text: {seconds} s each side at your own pace
pump.ready.flow.side.note: {seconds} is a number of seconds for each side of the body.

pump.ready.game.text: Press Start in the game when you are ready.
pump.ready.game.note: Start is a button in the game: keep it as the game names it. Also the body of the alert a game pump brings to a phone not in front (the iPhone's Live Activity or its time-sensitive notice, Android's pop-up; 2026-10-13).

pump.ready.game.locked.text: You said you felt unwell. Skip this pump: in the game, click Pause and pick I feel unwell.
pump.ready.game.locked.note: Pause and I feel unwell are the game's words for a button and its menu choice: keep them as the game names them.

pump.ready.goal.form.note: Why a goal reaches the record at most (the game's 'Your record: 12 · your best lately: 11'): the goal is one step past the best of the move's last three fresh sets, and the record came on a better day. {form} is that best, a count (11), a hold's time as a clock (0:38) or, on a loaded move with a weight planned, its set (10 kg × 12).

pump.ready.load.note: A move with a weight: the goal, {target} the reps to reach at least, at {kg} the weight planned for this set in kilograms (12.5).

pump.ready.load.each.note: A move with a weight in each hand: the goal, {target} the reps to reach at least, {kg} the kilograms of each weight.

pump.ready.load.heavier.text: Heavier now: you did {reps} reps twice at {kg} kg
pump.ready.load.heavier.note: Why the planned weight went up: the last two fresh sets reached {reps} reps, the move's top, at the old weight {kg} kg.

pump.ready.load.start.note: A move with a weight before the player has typed one: the weight most people start with, {lo} to {hi} kilograms.

pump.ready.load.start.each.note: A move with a weight in each hand before the player has typed one: the start weight of each, {lo} to {hi} kilograms.

pump.ready.locked.text: You said you felt unwell. Pumps are paused until {time}.
pump.ready.locked.note: {time} is a time of day, such as 4:00 AM.

pump.ready.mark.days.note: The Ready view's line under a pose's goal pose where its answer counts the family's day (Pump:toward kind step with `main` and `perfect` set, and the days not in): {days} the days toward the step so far (ns.PoseNeeds' have), {total} the days it takes (pose_unlock_days, 3); then ladders.step.short.main and .perfect where they are short. The game's ui.target.poseDays (Panel.lua poseDaysLine). Slice 47 (2026-10-19): any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day; the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days), at least pose_anchor_days of them on its main pose (pose_anchor_days_risky where only Perfect counts) and pose_perfect_days answered Perfect where Good counts too (ns.PoseNeeds).

pump.ready.mark.days.perfect.text: Perfect days toward your step: {days} of {total}.
pump.ready.mark.days.perfect.note: pump.ready.mark.days where only Perfect counts the day (the slot's ask Perfect: ns.MarkNeeds below a harder step); {days} and {total} as there. The game's ui.target.posePerfect. Slice 47 (2026-10-19): any goal pose of the player's step counts the family's day; the step opens after three such days (pose_unlock_days), at least pose_anchor_days of them on its main pose (pose_anchor_days_risky where only Perfect counts) and pose_perfect_days answered Perfect where Good counts too (ns.PoseNeeds).

pump.ready.new.note: A small tag beside the move's name on a pump's Ready view on the move's first appearance (a first max set, a placement, or a move never done), as the game's NEW.

pump.ready.pause.note: A button in the bar of a pump's Ready view on the phones and the computer, with its menu's arrow, in the game's words (its bar's Pause, Locales ui.panel.pause), and the name its menu is read by: how long the game offers pause, which ends the pump (where the device makes offers), then Your body's Something hurts and I feel unwell.

pump.ready.settings.note: A button in the bar of a pump's Ready view on the phones and the computer, in the game's words (its bar's Settings, Locales ui.panel.settings): opens Your setup over the pump, which waits on its Ready view.

pump.rest.arms.text: This pump rests your hands and arms for {game}.
pump.rest.arms.note: The line on a pump's Ready view (and the watch's size page) while the arms rest of slice 48 holds: {game} is the aim game's name as the offer carries it (Counter-Strike 2). No word of injury or recovery (no medical claim).

pump.rest.line.text: You said you felt unwell. Pumps are paused until {time}.
pump.rest.line.note: Pump home's line while the pumps rest after the player said they felt unwell (the phones' Pump tab, the computer's home, Hero and its place); a greyed Start says ladders.tree.rest. {time} is a time of day, such as 4:00 AM.

pump.rest.title.note: Title of the card shown after the player said they felt unwell: no pump starts until the next game day.

pump.reward.points.note: {count} is the stat points the pump earned.

pump.reward.rested.text: {count} rest tokens kept your streak going

plural.one: {count} rest token kept your streak going
plural.other: {count} rest tokens kept your streak going

pump.reward.rested.note: On an app pump's or a catch-up's result when rest tokens covered the game days without a pump before it (a paired player's from the streak board, 2026-10-09): {count} is the tokens spent, one a day. Never worded as a debt or a loss.

pump.reward.stars.note: {count} is the record stars the pump earned.

pump.reward.streak.note: On an app pump's result when it was the game day's first pump: the streak it continued, in days (the game's toast.streak). Never shown with pump.reward.welcome.

pump.reward.streak.new.note: On an app pump's result when it began a streak (the game day's first pump, a streak of one day: the game's toast.streak.new). Never shown with pump.reward.welcome.

pump.reward.token.text: Rest token earned: a day off keeps your streak
pump.reward.token.note: On an app pump's result when it earned a rest token (one every five active days, at most three held, since 2026-10-09): a later missed day is covered and the streak goes on.

pump.reward.welcome.note: On an app pump's result when it was the first pump after two or more whole game days without one (the game's Welcome back, slice 27: +50 XP and +2 Spirit). {xp} is the XP it paid, with the streak's share. A reward, never worded as a debt.

pump.reward.xp.note: {xp} is the experience points the game paid. XP is short for experience points.

pump.running.game.text: The game ends the move. Type your count there.
pump.running.game.note: A game pump's move of reps or hold: the move ends in the game, where the count is typed (a timed move says pump.live.game).

pump.running.game.side.note: A game pump's move on its first side: the game says when to switch. Also a line of Android's countdown notification.

pump.running.keepgoing.note: A button over Done (Done keeps its place) in the last 5 s of a steady cardio move whose time is under the full move's 45 s (slice 52; keep_going_s): pressed, the clock counts on past the move's time and stops by itself at 45 s; nothing asks after it (a move that ran to 45 s saves Yes, easily, one ended by Done between its plan and 45 s saves Yes, just). Only on a pump of the player's own device, never on a game pump the device follows, an all-out window, a counted set, a warm move, the stand-up move or a Long Haul.

pump.running.other.note: Under a side move's name while its second side runs.

pump.running.steps.note: {count} is the steps the phone counted during the move.

pump.running.switch.note: Button: the first side is done; the other side follows.

pump.saved.bar.best.note: Over the count bar's best post (slices 65 and 66): the move's record before this set in its unit, reps as a number (14), seconds as m:ss (0:42); no post once the record stands at the top or past it, none on a timed move. The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their moves pour the same way (owed, slices 65 and 66).

pump.saved.bar.goal.note: Under the count bar's goal post (slices 65 and 66): the move's goal in its unit, reps as a number (12), seconds as m:ss (0:30). The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their moves pour the same way (owed, slices 65 and 66).

pump.saved.bar.step.note: The hold bar's label on the phone (slice 65), lower case: the step whose range the bar spans; the computer puts kit.reward.step's ladder before it. The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their hold's seconds pour the same way (owed, slice 65).

pump.saved.bar.top.note: Under the count bar's top post (slices 65 and 66): the top of the step's range in the move's unit, reps as a number (15), seconds as m:ss (1:00), the count a day at the top needs; none on a counted set or a timed move. The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their moves pour the same way (owed, slices 65 and 66).

pump.saved.finish.note: The primary button of the seconds pour on the pump's last move (slice 65): the pump's Result at once. The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their hold's seconds pour the same way (owed, slice 65).

pump.saved.next.note: The primary button of a hold's seconds pour (slice 65, Rapha, 2026-11-03), live from the pour's start: the next move's Ready view at once (Enter on the computer); {move} is the next move's name. The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their hold's seconds pour the same way (owed, slice 65).

pump.saved.unlocked.note: The caption over the step-up reveal's new move (slice 65): the step of the ladder the hold just opened, in gold caps; the move's name and its quality word come under it. The iPhone and the Apple Watch show it once their hold's seconds pour the same way (owed, slice 65).

pump.side.first.note: {move} is a move's name: the first side of the body. Also the Android countdown notification's title.

pump.side.other.note: {move} is a move's name: the other side of the body. Also the Android countdown notification's title.

pump.size.big.note: A pump's size, one of Light, Balanced and Extreme: the quest's or the match's tier 1, 2 or 3, whose moves the pace then sets (pace_moves). Rapha, 2026-10-27: one language with Moves per quest and Moves per match ("it has different wording than the other make it speak one language"); Small, Normal and Big until then.

pump.size.normal.note: A pump's size, one of Light, Balanced and Extreme: the quest's or the match's tier 1, 2 or 3, whose moves the pace then sets (pace_moves). Rapha, 2026-10-27: one language with Moves per quest and Moves per match ("it has different wording than the other make it speak one language"); Small, Normal and Big until then.

pump.size.small.note: A pump's size, one of Light, Balanced and Extreme: the quest's or the match's tier 1, 2 or 3, whose moves the pace then sets (pace_moves). Rapha, 2026-10-27: one language with Moves per quest and Moves per match ("it has different wording than the other make it speak one language"); Small, Normal and Big until then.

pump.size.suggested.note: What VoiceOver and TalkBack say of the size an offer suggests (slice 48's double-check), which gold marks for the eye too: the gold size on the watches' size page, and on the phones' Start a pump a small gold pip under the computer match offer's size in the size control, which stays there whichever size the player then picks. Read as the size's value (state), never shown.

pump.source.check.note: The title of a pump started as a stretch check (ns.StartFor's kind check, slice 42); a caps label over the Ready view until 2026-10-22.

pump.streak.best.note: Caps over the longest streak the player has had.

pump.streak.month.earlier.note: The streak page's step back to the month before.

pump.streak.month.later.note: The streak page's step on to the month after (none past this).

pump.streak.next.note: Caps over the next milestone's words (30-day streak, or a 2-year streak from 730) and its bar.

pump.streak.next.none.note: In place of the next milestone past the last one (1,825 days).

pump.streak.next.togo.note: Under the next milestone's bar: the days from today's count to it.

pump.streak.open.note: The hint of the StreakBoard and of Hero's streak chip, both buttons since slice 51: they open the streak page.

pump.streak.share.note: The streak page's primary: opens the Share window on the streak card as the streak stands (none at 0 days).

pump.streak.title.note: The streak page's title (slice 51), from the StreakBoard and Hero's streak chip.

pump.streak.tokens.note: Caps over the rest tokens' slots: each token held keeps the streak through a day off.

pump.streak.tokens.earn.text: Every {days} active days earn a rest token, up to {max}. Each one keeps your streak through a day off.
pump.streak.tokens.earn.note: How a rest token is earned (token_days 5, token_max 3) and what it does. Earned, never bought; every player starts with one.

pump.streak.tokens.full.note: In place of the next token's line while the most are held.

pump.streak.tokens.held.note: Beside the rest tokens' slots: {count} held of the most there can be ({max}, 3).

pump.streak.tokens.next.note: While fewer than the most are held: the active days still to come before the next token.

pump.swap.more.note: The arrow at the right of the swap row on a pump's Ready view (the game's swap row menu, Locales ui.backup.menu), and on the watch the quiet word under the swap's own: opens every other move that can be swapped in.

pump.timed.ask.clock.note: Under the question: {clock} is the time the move ran before the player stopped, {full} the move's whole time, both as minutes and seconds, such as 0:05 and 0:45.

pump.timed.ask.no.note: Answer button: the player stopped early; the move is saved with the time the clock shows.

pump.timed.ask.title.text: Did you do the whole move?
pump.timed.ask.title.note: Question after a timed move was ended long before its time: the clock may have started late, so the player says whether they did all of it. Also Android's pump notification while the move waits for the answer.

pump.timed.ask.yes.note: Answer button: the whole move was done; it is saved with its full time.

pump.title.catchup.note: A catch-up pump's title as the Log keeps it. {moves} is how many moves, such as 2 moves.

pump.title.free.note: Title of an app pump. {kind} is what the player finished, such as A match, or Quick pump for the one-tap pump, or A pump you asked for (on the computer's Saga, a move started from its Book); {moves} is how many moves, such as two moves.

pump.title.game.note: A game pump's title as the Log keeps it. {moves} is how many moves, such as 2 moves.

pump.today.xp.note: Caps label under or beside a game day's experience points (the number drawn large): a day's on the Saga's XP tile and on the shared day and week cards. XP is the game's experience.

pump.today.xp.value.note: {xp} is the experience points a game day gained, shown with a plus: the Saga's XP tile and the shared day and week cards.

pump.unfinished.header.note: Section header over the moves the game still waits for. {count} is how many.

pump.unfinished.held.text: Your pain flags rest these moves.
pump.unfinished.held.note: Under the waiting moves when the player's own pain flags hold every one of them back.

pump.unfinished.skip.note: The button beside each unfinished move (the Pump tab's waiting card, the watch's unfinished list, Pump home on the computer) and on a catch-up's Ready view: one click takes the move off the unfinished list for good, as the game's Skip does; it earns nothing and costs nothing. Never a confirm (David, 2026-10-04).

pump.unfinished.skip.hint.text: Drops this banked move for good. It earns nothing and costs nothing.
pump.unfinished.skip.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver's hint, the computer's screen reader) for Skip: the game's own words for its Skip.

pump.unfinished.skip.named.note: Read out only: a Skip's name to a screen reader where each unfinished move has one beside it. {move} is the move's name.

pump.unsent.text: {count} moves not on your computer yet

plural.one: {count} move not on your computer yet
plural.other: {count} moves not on your computer yet

pump.unsent.note: Under Pump home's card while moves done on this phone have not reached the paired computer yet (it was out of reach): they go by themselves, in the background too. {count} is how many moves.

pump.unwell.note: Last row of a pump's More window (on a Ready view of the phones and the computer the last item of the menu of its Pause; a game pump's Ready view on the phones keeps it in its More window), in the stop colour with the heart: stops the pump at once and rests every pump until the next day; also the door's quiet last button, which opens the unwell window (title and its confirming primary are this key, then the line Apps open for the day), whose primary writes the same lock without a pump, so every app opens for the day.

pump.unwell.game.text: Stop in the game too: click Pause, then I feel unwell.
pump.unwell.game.note: After I feel unwell on a game pump: the game's pump goes on until the player stops it there. Pause and I feel unwell are the game's words for a button and its menu choice: keep them as the game names them.

pump.unwell.hint.text: Stops the pump. Pumps rest until 4 in the morning.
pump.unwell.hint.note: Read by a screen reader after I feel unwell in a pump's More window (on a Ready view of the phones and the computer, in the menu of its Pause).

pump.waiting.catchup.note: Main button while owed moves wait: starts a catch-up pump that pays them.

pump.waiting.game.text: The game is running: these come in its next pump.
pump.waiting.game.note: Under the waiting moves on the phone's Pump tab, in Catch up's place, and on the watch in the unfinished row's place and over the unfinished moves; on the computer on Pump home, under Hero's Start a pump, under the game on the welcome's On this computer card, on the first start's last page and on its place step: while World of Warcraft with QuestPump runs on the computer (or, on the welcome, once QuestPump found it), the game asks the pumps and puts the unfinished moves into its next pump itself.

pump.waiting.held.text: {count} more come with your next quest in the game

plural.one: {count} more comes with your next quest in the game
plural.other: {count} more come with your next quest in the game

pump.waiting.held.note: {count} is how many more owed moves the game puts into its next pump instead.

pump.waiting.title.note: {count} is how many owed moves wait for a catch-up pump on the phone. The heading of Pump home's banked card (its first moves with their tiles, the whole card opening the list) and of the window listing every one with its Skip (2026-11-03, Rapha: "unfinished moves should be called banked moves"; the Skip left Pump home itself).

pumpfirst.access.off.text: Usage access is off, so no app can wait.
pumpfirst.access.off.note: Android: the usage access card's line on Pump first's page while usage access is off (Games on this phone's card says no offer can show).

pumpfirst.add.note: Android: the quiet button that opens the picker of every launchable app.

pumpfirst.apps.note: Android: the label over the apps that wait for today's pump.

pumpfirst.battery.note: Android: the battery hand-off row and its priming window's heading; Unrestricted is Android's own word.

pumpfirst.channel.note: Android only: the channel of Pump first's quiet service notification in the system's settings, and that notification's title.

pumpfirst.channel.about.text: Shows while apps wait for today's pump
pumpfirst.channel.about.note: Android only: Pump first's channel's description in the system's settings.

pumpfirst.done.back.note: Android: the Result's button in Continue's place, which starts the app that waited; {app} is its name.

pumpfirst.done.line.note: Android: under Apps open; {count} is how many apps waited, {time} the game day's turn (4:00 AM).

pumpfirst.done.line.any.note: Under Apps open where the phone cannot count the apps (the iPhone).

pumpfirst.done.title.note: The Result's heading once today's pump opened the apps that waited.

pumpfirst.door.caps.note: Caps label of Pump home's Pump first card.

pumpfirst.door.open.note: The door's way out, one tap with no count and nothing unfinished, and the Way out row's value on the Pump first page; {minutes} is pump_first_open_min (15).

pumpfirst.door.play.note: The door's way out at a game's new session: the game stays open until it closes.

pumpfirst.door.pump.note: The door's gold primary over Quick pump: starts the Quick pump.

pumpfirst.door.session.note: The door's title when a game asks at a new session (Games ask each time they open).

pumpfirst.door.title.note: The door's title when an app that waits opens before today's pump.

pumpfirst.everytime.text: Games ask each time they open
pumpfirst.everytime.note: The switch that makes a game ask for a Light pump (tier 1) at each new session, even after today's pump.

pumpfirst.games.text: Games on this phone wait too
pumpfirst.games.note: The switch that makes the games of Games on this phone wait for today's pump too.

pumpfirst.home.line.note: Android: Pump home's Pump first card before today's first move; {count} is how many apps wait.

pumpfirst.home.line.any.text: Your apps wait for today's pump
pumpfirst.home.line.any.note: Pump home's Pump first card where the phone cannot count the apps (the iPhone).

pumpfirst.intent.note: The iPhone's App Intent in Shortcuts that the player's Is Opened automation runs for an app that waits for today's pump.

pumpfirst.notice.open.note: Android only: the line of Pump first's service notification while the apps are open; {time} is when they wait again: the game day's turn (4:00 AM) after today's pump or a felt-unwell stop, the end of quiet hours while they hold.

pumpfirst.notice.waits.note: Android only: the line of Pump first's service notification while apps wait; {count} is how many.

pumpfirst.overlay.note: Android: the hand-off row and its priming window's heading, before the system's Display over other apps setting.

pumpfirst.overlay.off.text: QuestPump can't show over other apps yet.
pumpfirst.overlay.off.note: Android: the page's line while Display over other apps is off, so the door cannot show.

pumpfirst.pick.note: Android: the heading of the picker window of the apps that wait.

pumpfirst.rule.out.note: The rules card's row whose value is Open for 15 minutes: one tap, always.

pumpfirst.rule.quiet.note: The rules card's row for the Reminders page's quiet hours.

pumpfirst.rule.quiet.value.note: Its value: in quiet hours nothing waits.

pumpfirst.rule.unwell.note: The rules card's row for the felt-unwell lock.

pumpfirst.rule.unwell.value.note: Its value on Pump first's page, and the line of the door's unwell window: I feel unwell opens every app until the next game day and asks no pump.

pumpfirst.rules.note: The label over the rules card.

pumpfirst.shortcut.step1.text: Add an automation: App, pick the apps that should wait, Is Opened, Run Immediately.
pumpfirst.shortcut.step1.note: Step 1 of 3: the Shortcuts app's own words, as it shows them.

pumpfirst.shortcut.step2.note: Step 2 of 3: the intent's title, as Shortcuts lists it.

pumpfirst.shortcut.step3.text: Open one of those apps to try it.

pumpfirst.switch.note: The page's master switch (Pump first): the apps the player picks wait each day until the first pump.

pumpfirst.usage.body.text: To ask for today's pump, QuestPump needs to see when an app you picked opens, also while it is closed. While Pump first is on, it checks which app is in front, keeps only the opens of your picked apps and games, and never tells us which apps you use. Android asks next.
pumpfirst.usage.body.note: Android: the line of that window, Play's prominent disclosure for Pump first: what is read (which app is in front, about once a second while an app waits, also in the background) and what is kept.

pumpfirst.usage.title.note: Android: the heading of the window before Android's usage access settings when Pump first's page asks for it.

reminders.alarm.note: iPhone only: a switch that makes the reminder ring as an alarm (AlarmKit).

reminders.alarm.off.text: Alarms are off for QuestPump. Allow them in Settings.
reminders.alarm.off.note: Under As an alarm once AlarmKit was refused or revoked; the reminder then comes as a notification.

reminders.alarm.open.note: iPhone only: the alarm's button that opens QuestPump.

reminders.alarm.priming.title.note: The heading of the window before iOS asks about alarms (AlarmKit): its question, over Continue (2026-10-22: no body).

reminders.alarm.short.note: iPhone only: the meta of a reminder that rings as an alarm.

reminders.alarm.stop.note: iPhone only: the alarm's stop button on iOS 26.0.

reminders.cap.note: The most reminders of every kind on one day, 3 at first.

reminders.cap.reminder.note: The unit under the reminders a day when it is 1, in the window's stepper. The number stands over it.

reminders.cap.reminders.note: The unit under the reminders a day when it is not 1, in the window's stepper. The number stands over it.

reminders.channel.note: Android only: the notification channel's name in the system's settings.

reminders.channel.about.text: Your streak reminder, your own reminders and the sitting reminder
reminders.channel.about.note: Android only: the channel's description (the game offers have their own channel, links.channel).

reminders.edit.note: The title of one reminder's page.

reminders.notify.answer.many.note: The question's third answer, an action on the notification: 4 or more matches, which opens Ready for the pump those matches give (slice 48: the matches times the game's minutes per match, one step per match_step_min, half up, Light to Extreme).

reminders.notify.answer.one.note: The question's first answer, an action on the notification (and on the Apple Watch's): 1 match, which opens Ready for the pump those matches give (slice 48: the matches times the game's minutes per match, one step per match_step_min, half up, Light to Extreme).

reminders.notify.answer.some.note: The question's second answer, an action on the notification: 2 or 3 matches, which opens Ready for the pump those matches give (slice 48: the matches times the game's minutes per match, one step per match_step_min, half up, Light to Extreme).

reminders.notify.game.body.closed.text: You closed {link}. Ready for a pump?
reminders.notify.game.body.closed.note: The offer's line after a program the player picked on the computer closed (slice 35): {link} is the program's name as the player picked it. A session's end, never a match's. A phone's notification and a watch's notice on its session screen say it for a match_end with no kind, which a desktop app sent after a program's close until 2026-10-28; since then every game's offer carries the match kind, and the desktop app's card and Pump home say the match's words for it.

reminders.notify.game.body.computer.note: The offer's line after a game on the computer ended (slice 35; these words since slice 48's double-check): {link} is the game's name as the match_end command carries it (Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, League of Legends or TFT, Rocket League). Never a win or a loss. Pump home's offer card on the computer, a phone's notification and a watch's notice on its session screen say it alike; the computer's match-over card names the game alone since 2026-10-22.

reminders.notify.game.body.match.text: You finished a game on {link}. Ready for a pump?
reminders.notify.game.body.match.note: The offer's line. {link} is the site's name (Lichess, Chess.com, Steam).

reminders.notify.game.body.played.text: You played {game} for {minutes} minutes. How many matches?

plural.one: You played {game} for {minutes} minute. How many matches?
plural.other: You played {game} for {minutes} minutes. How many matches?

reminders.notify.game.body.played.note: The question's line after a session of a game on this phone ended (docs/phone-games.md §3): {game} is the game's own name, cut to 40 characters, {minutes} the session's minutes; its three answers stand under it as actions.

reminders.notify.game.body.played.any.text: You played for {minutes} minutes. How many matches?

plural.one: You played for {minutes} minute. How many matches?
plural.other: You played for {minutes} minutes. How many matches?

reminders.notify.game.body.played.any.note: The question's line when the iPhone's automation names no game: {minutes} is the session's minutes.

reminders.notify.game.body.stream.text: You finished a stream on {link}. Ready for a pump?
reminders.notify.game.body.stream.note: The offer's line. {link} is the site's name (Twitch).

reminders.notify.game.late.match.text: You finished a game on {link} {minutes} minutes ago. Ready for a pump?

plural.one: You finished a game on {link} {minutes} minute ago. Ready for a pump?
plural.other: You finished a game on {link} {minutes} minutes ago. Ready for a pump?

reminders.notify.game.late.match.note: The offer's line when the site showed the finished game late: {minutes} since it finished, {link} the site's name.

reminders.notify.game.late.played.text: You played {game} {minutes} minutes ago. How many matches?

plural.one: You played {game} {minutes} minute ago. How many matches?
plural.other: You played {game} {minutes} minutes ago. How many matches?

reminders.notify.game.late.played.note: Android's question when its look found the session late (link_late_min or more after it ended): {minutes} since the game left the front, {game} its name.

reminders.notify.game.late.stream.text: You finished a stream on {link} {minutes} minutes ago. Ready for a pump?

plural.one: You finished a stream on {link} {minutes} minute ago. Ready for a pump?
plural.other: You finished a stream on {link} {minutes} minutes ago. Ready for a pump?

reminders.notify.game.late.stream.note: The offer's line when the stream's end showed late: {minutes} since it finished, {link} the site's name.

reminders.notify.game.title.match.note: The offer's title after a game on a linked site finished, and after a match or a picked program on the computer ended (slice 35): a phone's notification and a watch's notice on its session screen; the heading of the Good game! sheet and the question's title after a game on this phone (docs/phone-games.md). It names finishing, never winning or losing.

reminders.notify.game.title.stream.note: The offer's title after the player's stream on a linked site finished.

reminders.notify.own.body.text: A short pump is ready when you are.

reminders.notify.own.title.note: A reminder the player set; also the alarm's title on the iPhone.

reminders.notify.sitting.body.text: An hour of sitting. A short pump is ready.

reminders.notify.sitting.title.note: The sitting cue, after an hour of sitting.

plural.one: One pump today makes your streak {days} day.
plural.other: One pump today makes your streak {days} days.

reminders.notify.streak.body.note: The streak reminder for a player without the game: the count the next pump makes.
reminders.notify.streak.body.text: One pump today makes your streak {days} days.

plural.one: One pump in the game or here makes your streak {days} day.
plural.other: One pump in the game or here makes your streak {days} days.

reminders.notify.streak.body.game.note: The streak reminder for a player with the game paired: a pump in the game or in the app counts.
reminders.notify.streak.body.game.text: One pump in the game or here makes your streak {days} days.

reminders.notify.streak.start.text: One pump today starts your streak.
reminders.notify.streak.start.note: The streak reminder's body on a game day no streak counts yet (docs/plan.md slice 32, D13, 2026-10-07: the reminder comes on every game day without a pump, so a broken streak still gets its daily nudge).

reminders.notify.streak.start.game.text: One pump in the game or here starts your streak.
reminders.notify.streak.start.game.note: reminders.notify.streak.start while Hero shows the game's sheet (D7).

reminders.notify.streak.title.note: The streak reminder's title. It offers a pump; never words of loss, debt or a deadline.

reminders.notify.watch.note: Android only: the reminder's action shown on a Wear OS watch, which opens the watch's pump.

reminders.off.ask.text: Allow notifications to get your reminders.
reminders.off.ask.note: The card's line while a reminder is on and the iPhone has not asked for notifications yet (a restore or a privacy reset); its button asks.

reminders.own.note: The section of the reminders the player sets, each at a time of its own, every day.

reminders.plist.alarm.text: QuestPump rings the reminders you mark as alarms, even on silent.
reminders.plist.alarm.note: The iPhone's question before AlarmKit rings the player's alarms (Info.plist).

reminders.quiet.note: Hours with no reminder of any kind.

reminders.quiet.inside.note: The meta of a reminder whose time lies in quiet hours, so it never comes; the Menu's Reminders value when every reminder that is on lies there.

reminders.sitting.note: A switch: after an hour of sitting, a reminder offers a short pump (the sitting cue in the code).

reminders.sitting.denied.text: QuestPump cannot read your steps. Allow it in Settings.
reminders.sitting.denied.note: The sitting cue's line when the phone's health store denies the steps.

reminders.sitting.nosteps.text: No app on this phone counts your steps yet.
reminders.sitting.nosteps.note: Under the sitting cue while no step sample is seen in 7 days (Apple Health or Health Connect), which nothing the player refused explains. Android's; the iPhone's is reminders.sitting.nosteps.ios.

reminders.sitting.nosteps.ios.text: No app on this {device} counts your steps yet.
reminders.sitting.nosteps.ios.note: Under the sitting cue while no step sample is seen in 7 days (Apple Health or Health Connect), which nothing the player refused explains. The iPhone's twin of reminders.sitting.nosteps. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

reminders.sitting.priming.body.apple.text: QuestPump reads your steps and stand hours from Apple Health to notice an hour of sitting. They stay here. Your {device} asks next.
reminders.sitting.priming.body.apple.note: iPhone only: the window before HealthKit's question. Apple Health is the app's name. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

reminders.sitting.priming.body.connect.text: QuestPump reads your steps from Health Connect, also while it is closed, to notice an hour of sitting. They stay on this phone. Android asks next.
reminders.sitting.priming.body.connect.note: Android only: the window before Health Connect's question. Health Connect is the app's name.

reminders.sitting.unavailable.text: This phone cannot read steps in the background.
reminders.sitting.unavailable.note: Android only: Health Connect on this phone has no background reads, so the sitting cue cannot run.

reminders.span.note: Two clock times: quiet hours, or on Android the window a reminder comes in. Keep the en dash, or the language's sign for a range.

reminders.streak.note: A switch: one reminder a day, only on a day with no pump yet, while the streak counts.

reminders.time.note: A value row with a clock time, which opens the system's time picker.

reminders.time.taken.text: You already have a reminder at this time.
reminders.time.taken.note: Said when a reminder is added or moved to a minute another reminder already has; the time is not taken.

saga.best.note: The tag of a game day with more moves than any day before it, once 7 earlier days had a move. Shown, never a reward: no XP or title comes with it. In caps on a gold tag with a star.

saga.chapter.note: A chapter's tag in caps: a game day with a move, numbered from the player's first such day (Chapter 12 is the 12th day with a move; it never goes back). Also an earlier day's page title.

saga.chapters.note: Section label over the earlier days with moves, newest first, each opening its page.

saga.chapters.more.note: At the foot of the Saga's earlier chapters on the computer while older days are not shown yet.

saga.day.note: Caps title of the Saga's tile with the day's strip, alone (Your day; Your day · 22 pumps until 2026-10-27, the day's moves the hero's number above it).

saga.hero.spoken.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the day's hero when the day has no word (before 7 earlier days had a move, or with no day of the 8 weeks before it): its chapter, its date said in full (Tuesday 14 October) and its moves.

saga.hero.spoken.quality.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the day's hero: its chapter, its date said in full, its moves and its word ({quality}: Best day ever, Epic day, Rare day, Uncommon day or Common day).

saga.home.note: Caps title of Pump home's card with today's moves and strip, which opens the Saga.

saga.kind.cardio.note: A kind of move under the day's kinds bar, with its count: the cardio moves.

saga.kind.mobility.note: A kind of move under the day's kinds bar, with its count: the stretching and mobility moves.

saga.kind.strength.note: A kind of move under the day's kinds bar, with its count: the strength moves (push, pull, legs, trunk).

saga.kind.yoga.note: A kind of move under the day's kinds bar, with its count: the yoga poses.

saga.level.note: Caps label on the Saga's XP tile before the character's level: the level at the day's start, and when it rose an arrow glyph and the level at its end (Level 23 → 24), the numbers drawn after the word.

saga.level.up.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for the Saga's XP tile when the character's level rose that day: its level at the day's start and at its end.

saga.move.note: Caps label beside a day's big number when it is 1: saga.moves' singular (the Saga, an earlier day's shared card, the Quest Bill's total).

saga.move.today.note: Caps label beside today's big number when it is 1: saga.moves.today's singular (Pump home's Today's chapter, the shared day card).

saga.move.week.note: Caps label beside the week card's big number when it is 1: saga.moves.week's singular.

saga.moves.note: Caps label beside a day's big number: the moves done that game day, on the Saga, on an earlier day's shared card in place of Moves today, and the Quest Bill's total.

saga.moves.today.note: Caps label beside today's big number: the moves done this game day (from 04:00), on Pump home's Today's chapter and on the shared day card.

saga.moves.week.note: Caps label beside the week card's big number: the moves done this game week.

saga.muscles.note: Caps title of the tile with the body figure: the muscles the day's moves worked.

saga.muscles.most.note: Legend of the body figure's gold: muscles a move of the day worked as a main muscle.

saga.muscles.some.note: Legend of the body figure's faint gold: muscles the day's moves worked only as a helping muscle.

saga.new.moves.note: The pill at the top of the Saga, and of an earlier day's page, while the player reads further down and newer moves came in: nothing on the page moves until the player taps it, which scrolls to the top, where they show. {count} is how many moves were done since the page was drawn. Read by VoiceOver, TalkBack and screen readers as it is, once as it appears.

saga.nomove.note: An earlier game day whose pumps were all banked or ended before a move: its quiet row in Earlier chapters (no chapter tag, the date and No moves; its pumps' count until 2026-10-27) and its page's head, which lists those pumps.

saga.none.title.note: In place of today's big number before the game day's first move.

saga.plan.note: The legend of the white ticks on the day's kinds bar: the share of each kind the player's focus plans. {focus} is the focus's name from the game (Balanced, Strength, Endurance or Flexibility).

saga.pumps.note: Section label over the day's pumps on the Saga, each opening its page.

saga.quality.common.note: A game day's word in its quality's colour, ranked only against the player's own days with a move of the 8 weeks before it: half or more of the window's days had more moves. Never shown before 7 earlier days had a move. Since 2026-10-29 a Common day shows no word in the game, on Android and on the computer (an ordinary day needs no tag, and Common read as a put-down); the iPhone's moves to the same on a Mac. In caps on a slanted tag, and under the Quest Bill's seal.

saga.quality.epic.note: A game day's word in its quality's colour, ranked only against the player's own days with a move of the 8 weeks before it: fewer than a tenth of the window's days had more moves. Never shown before 7 earlier days had a move. In caps on a slanted tag, and under the Quest Bill's seal.

saga.quality.rare.note: A game day's word in its quality's colour, ranked only against the player's own days with a move of the 8 weeks before it: fewer than a quarter of the window's days had more moves. Never shown before 7 earlier days had a move. In caps on a slanted tag, and under the Quest Bill's seal.

saga.quality.uncommon.note: A game day's word in its quality's colour, ranked only against the player's own days with a move of the 8 weeks before it: fewer than half of the window's days had more moves. Never shown before 7 earlier days had a move. In caps on a slanted tag, and under the Quest Bill's seal.

saga.record.note: Caps line over an earlier day's highlight when it holds a record and no unlock.

saga.record.today.note: Caps line over the day's highlight when it holds a record and no unlock: the move under it with its new best.

saga.share.day.note: The gold button at the top of an earlier day's page: opens the Share window on that day's card.

saga.share.today.note: The Saga's one gold button at its top: opens the Share window on today's day card.

saga.share.week.note: A quiet button on the Saga's Week tile: opens the Share window on the week's card.

saga.strip.spoken.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack for a part of the day's strip or a day of the week's bars: {part} is the time of day (Morning) or the weekday (Monday).

saga.time.afternoon.note: Caps word under the day's strip: 12:00 to 16:59, the time of day the pumps over it started, its moves' total over them.

saga.time.evening.note: Caps word under the day's strip: 17:00 to 21:59, the time of day the pumps over it started, its moves' total over them.

saga.time.morning.note: Caps word under the day's strip: 04:00 to 11:59, the time of day the pumps over it started, its moves' total over them.

saga.time.night.note: Caps word under the day's strip: 22:00 to 03:59, the time of day the pumps over it started, its moves' total over them.

saga.unit.move.note: The unit word when the count is 1, beside an earlier chapter's moves in its row, the number drawn large (Chapter 11 · Mon 13 Oct · 44 moves). The number stands before it.

saga.unit.moves.note: The unit word when the count is not 1, beside an earlier chapter's moves in its row, the number drawn large (Chapter 11 · Mon 13 Oct · 44 moves). The number stands before it.

saga.unit.record.note: The unit word when the count is 1, beside the day's records, the number drawn large (the Saga's 3 records · 1 unlock, Pump home's line). The number stands before it.

saga.unit.records.note: The unit word when the count is not 1, beside the day's records, the number drawn large (the Saga's 3 records · 1 unlock, Pump home's line). The number stands before it.

saga.unit.unlock.note: The unit word when the count is 1, beside the day's unlocks, the number drawn large (3 records · 1 unlock): steps reached for the first time. The number stands before it.

saga.unit.unlocks.note: The unit word when the count is not 1, beside the day's unlocks, the number drawn large (3 records · 1 unlock): steps reached for the first time. The number stands before it.

saga.unlocked.note: Caps line over an earlier day's highlight: a step the player reached for the first time that day.

saga.unlocked.today.note: Caps line over the day's highlight on the Saga and the day card: a step the player reached for the first time today, its move named under it with its quality word.

saga.was.note: After a record's new best on the Saga: the move's best before that day (31 was 30). {value} is a count, a hold's time (1:35) or a weight with reps, as the Log writes it.

saga.week.note: Caps title of the Saga's tile with the game week's seven bars of moves.

saga.week.best.note: The legend of the dashed line across the week's bars, before its number drawn beside it: the most moves of one day before the day shown.

saga.week.of.note: The week card's line under My saga: {date} is the game week's first day (13 Oct).

saga.xp.note: A game day's experience points as one line (+1,240 XP): the Quest Bill's line under its total of moves, and how VoiceOver and TalkBack read the Saga's XP tile. XP is short for experience points.

setup.add.get.note: Step 1 of 2 on Add the game. A tap sends the web address of QuestPump for the computer to the player's computer (the phone's share sheet). QuestPump is the app's name.

setup.add.get.hint.text: Sends the link to your computer
setup.add.get.hint.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack after step 1: a tap shares the helper's link, to send it to the computer.

setup.add.get.where.note: Under step 1: the web page where QuestPump for the computer downloads. Keep it as written.

setup.add.open.note: Step 2 of 2 on Add the game: start the helper on the computer.

setup.add.paste.note: Quiet button under Scan the QR code, and the title of its window: paste the helper's pairing link (or a sheet code from the game) instead of scanning.

setup.add.scan.note: Button on Add the game, and the scanner page's title: opens the camera to scan the pairing code in the helper's window.

setup.add.title.note: Title of the first-start page that connects the game through the helper on the computer.

setup.ble.link.note: The button that links this phone to the computer by Bluetooth (the iPhone's accessory picker, Android's Nearby devices and companion-device dialog).

setup.ble.picker.note: The item's name in iOS's accessory picker and in Settings, Accessories; QuestPump is the app's name.

setup.camera.failed.title.note: iPhone only: the scanner page when the camera did not start (another app holds it).

setup.camera.off.line.text: Turn it on in Settings, or paste the link.
setup.camera.off.line.note: iPhone only: under The camera is off; Paste a link follows.

setup.camera.off.title.note: iPhone only: the scanner page when QuestPump may not use the camera.

setup.experience.continue.note: The experience page's button: on to the first pump. On the computer also the place step's button while the game, a felt-unwell rest or a failed start holds the first pump back (on to Done), and the place window's (the pump goes on).

setup.failure.broken.text: That text is cut off or mistyped. Copy it again from the game.
setup.failure.broken.note: An imported sheet text that does not read.

setup.failure.localnetwork.text: Local Network access is off for QuestPump. Turn it on in Settings, Privacy & Security, Local Network.
setup.failure.localnetwork.note: iPhone only. Local Network, Settings and Privacy & Security are names of iOS's own settings: use the iPhone's names in the language.

setup.failure.localnetwork.android.text: Nearby devices is off for QuestPump. Turn it on in Settings, Apps, QuestPump, Permissions.
setup.failure.localnetwork.android.note: Android only. Nearby devices, Settings, Apps and Permissions are Android's names: use the phone's names in the language.

setup.failure.newer.text: This sheet comes from a newer addon (save {save}; this app reads {reads}). Update the app.
setup.failure.newer.note: An imported sheet the app is too old for. {save} and {reads} are version numbers. The addon is QuestPump's part in the game.

setup.failure.refused.text: That QR code is not a QuestPump pairing code.
setup.failure.refused.note: A scanned or pasted code that is no pair link.

setup.failure.stale.text: {computer} has made a new code since. Scan the one its window shows now.
setup.failure.stale.note: Pairing failed: the scanned code is an old one. {computer} is the computer's name the code gives.

setup.failure.toolarge.text: That text is too long to be a sheet from the game.
setup.failure.toolarge.note: A pasted, scanned, linked or shared text far longer than any sheet the game exports (over about a million characters, or one that unpacks to over about 4 MB), refused before it is read.

setup.failure.unknown.text: That is not a QuestPump link or sheet.
setup.failure.unknown.note: A scanned, pasted, linked or shared text the app cannot use: neither the helper's pairing link nor a sheet from the game.

setup.failure.unreachable.text: {computer} did not answer. Keep the phone on the same Wi-Fi as the computer, with QuestPump running on it.
setup.failure.unreachable.note: Pairing failed: nothing answered at the computer's address. {computer} is the computer's name the code gives. QuestPump is the app's name.

setup.import.failed.title.note: Title of the window when a scanned, linked or shared sheet from the game does not import; the reason follows it.

setup.localnetwork.title.text: Find your computer on your Wi-Fi
setup.localnetwork.title.note: The heading of the window before the phone asks about the local network: its one line, over Continue (2026-10-22: no body).

setup.motion.body.text: QuestPump counts your steps while a pump runs here. When your {device} asks about motion and fitness, choose Allow. Pumps work without it too.
setup.motion.body.note: iPhone only: the window before iOS's Motion & Fitness question. Allow is the name of iOS's button: use iOS's name in the language. {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad: the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15.

setup.motion.title.note: iPhone only: title of the window before iOS asks for Motion & Fitness, the steps of a pump the phone times.

setup.pairing.ble.failed.text: Could not link by Bluetooth. Keep this phone near {computer}, with Bluetooth on there and QuestPump showing its pairing code, then try again.
setup.pairing.ble.failed.note: The computer advertises while a phone is paired or its pairing code shows (its Phones page or its pairing window), and the pairing code's page asks the Mac's Bluetooth grant in context, so showing the code is the step that always works (2026-10-17).

setup.pairing.ble.instead.text: {computer} did not answer on this Wi-Fi. Pair by Bluetooth instead: keep this phone near it while QuestPump shows its pairing code there.
setup.pairing.ble.instead.note: Over Pair by Bluetooth after the pairing failed on the LAN; the computer advertises while its pairing code shows (its Phones page or its pairing window) and asks the Mac's Bluetooth grant there (2026-10-17).

setup.pairing.ble.later.note: Skips the Bluetooth step; Pump's follow card and the Helper page offer it again. On Pump's follow card (2026-10-19, the program's double-check) it puts away the card's Bluetooth reason (the link, Nearby devices or Bluetooth refused or off, the computer's ask, its Bluetooth refused or off) for this pairing; a new pairing or Link on the Helper page brings it back, and the Helper page still offers the link.

setup.pairing.ble.line.text: Connect this phone to {computer} by Bluetooth. Then pumps reach it away from your Wi-Fi too, and QuestPump restarts on its own if Android closes it.
setup.pairing.ble.line.note: The Bluetooth step's line on Android; {computer} is the computer's name. Android follows the game with the screen off on Wi-Fi already: the line names only what Bluetooth adds (2026-10-17).

setup.pairing.ble.line.ios.text: Link this {device} to {computer} by Bluetooth. Then each pump shows on your Lock Screen, also while it's locked or away from your Wi-Fi.
setup.pairing.ble.line.ios.note: The Bluetooth step's line on the iPhone and the iPad; {computer} is the computer's name, {device} the device's own word, iPhone or iPad (AboutPage.device; 2026-10-19).

setup.pairing.ble.location.text: Turn on Location while you link. Then Android starts QuestPump again by itself if it ever stops it.
setup.pairing.ble.location.note: While the phone's Location is off: Android's companion-device link needs it on to find the computer.

setup.pairing.ble.nearby.text: Next, Android asks if QuestPump may find nearby devices. QuestPump looks only for {computer}.
setup.pairing.ble.nearby.note: Before Android's own Nearby devices question; QuestPump never asks for location.

setup.pairing.ble.other.text: The QuestPump that answered is not {computer} with this pairing code. Try again and pick the other one in the list, or scan its pairing code again.
setup.pairing.ble.other.note: The computer picked over Bluetooth is not the one this phone is paired with. The list (the iPhone's accessory picker, Android's companion-device dialog) cannot tell two QuestPump computers apart by name, so the words point to the other entry (2026-10-17). Since 2026-11-01 the Bluetooth hello proves only the key (the release security review of 2026-10-31, L3), so the paired computer with a new pairing code reads as another computer, and the words name both ways out.

setup.pairing.ble.pair.note: Pairs over Bluetooth after the computer did not answer on the Wi-Fi.

setup.pairing.ble.pick.text: In the list that opens, pick QuestPump on {computer}.
setup.pairing.ble.pick.note: Under the line, before the system's accessory picker opens; QuestPump on {computer} is the picker's item (setup.ble.picker).

setup.pairing.ble.title.note: The pairing window's step after Paired, before the game's step (slice 43): it links this phone to the computer by Bluetooth.

setup.pairing.confirm.again.note: Title of the window when a pairing link opened from outside the app carries a new code of the computer paired now. {name} is its name.

setup.pairing.confirm.pair.note: Button: pairs with the computer the window names.

setup.pairing.confirm.replaces.note: Under Pair with the computer: the computer paired now, which pairing would replace. {replaces} is its name.

setup.pairing.confirm.title.note: Title of the window when a pairing link opened from outside the app would pair a computer, paired or not (another one while a computer is paired). {name} is that computer's name.

setup.pairing.done.title.note: Title of the pairing window once the phone is paired. {computer} is the computer's name, as the helper gives it.

setup.pairing.failed.kept.note: Under a failed pairing, when the phone was paired before: the older pairing stays. {computer} is that computer's name.

setup.pairing.failed.title.note: Title of the pairing window when a pair link did not pair: true whether or not an older pairing stays (a link from another computer that failed keeps the old one).

setup.pairing.next.text: Next, in the game, press Check again.
setup.pairing.next.note: Under Paired with the computer while the helper's step is check_again: the game's setup window shows its Check again right now (the strip's setup word, 2026-10-13). Check again is a button in the game's setup screen: keep it as the game names it.

setup.pairing.next.done.text: All set. Pumps from the game come to this phone while you play.
setup.pairing.next.done.note: Under Paired with the computer on Android while the helper's step is none: nothing is left to do, since the phone follows the game by itself while paired. The game's pumps reach the phone through QuestPump on the computer with no reload, and the game reads the pairing at its next start by itself (2026-10-13).

setup.pairing.next.done.ios.text: All set. When you play, tap Follow the game on Pump, and each pump comes to your Lock Screen.
setup.pairing.next.done.ios.note: Under Paired with the computer on the iPhone while the helper's step is none (2026-10-14): the iPhone follows the game only once Follow the game starts it, or once the app is opened while the game runs. Follow the game and Pump are the button's and the tab's own words.

setup.pairing.next.done.ios.ble.text: All set. Each pump from the game comes to your Lock Screen, also while this {device} is locked.
setup.pairing.next.done.ios.ble.note: The pairing window's last step on an iPhone or iPad linked by Bluetooth (setup.pairing.next.done.ios without it). {device} is the device's own word, iPhone or iPad (AboutPage.device; 2026-10-19).

setup.pairing.next.either.text: Next, in the game, type /reload, or press Check again if its setup window is open.
setup.pairing.next.either.note: Under Paired with the computer while the helper's step is either, or absent (QuestPump on the computer cannot tell yet what the game shows, or is older than 2026-10-13): both ways make the game read the pairing, so the text never names only a button that may be closed. Check again and /reload are the game's own words: keep them.

setup.pairing.next.grant.text: Next, open QuestPump on {computer} and allow screen reading, so it can see the game.
setup.pairing.next.grant.note: Under Paired with the computer while the helper's step is grant: QuestPump on the computer still needs the system's screen permission (a Mac) to see the game. Nothing in the game is needed after it (2026-10-13). {computer} is the computer's name.

setup.pairing.next.phone.text: Your pumps from this phone are on {computer} now.
setup.pairing.next.phone.note: Under Paired with the computer, when the computer has no World of Warcraft with QuestPump: nothing to do in a game, the phone's pumps reach the computer. {computer} is the computer's name.

setup.pairing.next.reload.text: Next, type /reload in the game once, so it loads your saved progress.
setup.pairing.next.reload.note: Under Paired with the computer while the helper's step is reload: a game that showed at a /reload that it does not read its own save back loaded before QuestPump on the computer ran, so one /reload brings its saved progress back. /reload is the game's chat command: keep it as typed.

setup.pairing.progress.note: {computer} is the computer's name, as the helper gives it.

setup.pairing.title.note: Title of the window that shows a pairing with the helper.

setup.paste.label.note: Label of the field for a pasted pair link or sheet text.

setup.paste.use.note: Button: reads the pasted pair link or sheet text.
