setup.permissions.activity.note: Android only: the name of Android's permission. Use Android's name in the language.

setup.permissions.activity.meta.text: Counts your steps and keeps this phone's own pumps going with the screen off
setup.permissions.activity.meta.note: Android only: what Physical activity does for a pump: the steps, and the clock of a pump of the phone's own off screen (following the game off screen needs no permission since 2026-10-13).

setup.permissions.fix.note: Android only: a button at the foot of the Helper page while Nearby devices is off; it asks Android again, and where Android no longer asks, the window that follows or the foot offers Open Settings (the Physical activity line it also served went on 2026-10-13, when the phone began to follow the game without that permission).

setup.permissions.notifications.note: Android only: the name of Android's permission. Use Android's name in the language.

setup.permissions.title.note: Android only: title of the window before Android asks for two permissions the phone's pumps use.

setup.plist.bluetooth.text: QuestPump links to QuestPump on your computer by Bluetooth, so each pump from the game reaches this device while it is locked.
setup.plist.bluetooth.note: The Bluetooth usage string of the iPhone app (apple/project.yml), on iPads too. Says "this device", not "iPhone": an Info.plist string takes no placeholder, and the iPhone app runs on iPads too since 2026-10-15 (2026-10-19).

setup.plist.camera.text: QuestPump scans the QR code on your computer to pair, and the sheet code the game shows.
setup.plist.camera.note: The system's question before the app uses the camera. The QR code is the one QuestPump on the player's computer shows.

setup.plist.localnetwork.text: QuestPump talks to QuestPump on your computer for your sheet and each pump's countdown.
setup.plist.localnetwork.note: The system's question before the app talks to the computer on the local network. QuestPump is the app's name; QuestPump on your computer is the app for macOS and Windows that the phone pairs with.

setup.scanagain.note: Button: opens the scanner again after a code that did not work.

setup.scanner.camera.text: Scan it with the phone's camera instead.
setup.scanner.camera.note: Android only: the app's scanner could not start; the phone's own camera app opens the pair link too.

setup.welcome.computer.note: The first start's second button: goes to the steps that add QuestPump on the player's computer, for World of Warcraft with QuestPump's addon or for other games there.

setup.welcome.start.note: The first start's main button: starts the app on its own, without the game.

share.brag.colour.note: A share card's headline when its pump opened a step of a colour the player had not reached before: the colour's name (Rare, Epic). The seal stands beside it.

share.brag.colour.step.note: Under a colour headline: the main move of the step that opened.

share.brag.day.note: A timed pump card's headline when nothing else stands out: the streak's day the pump kept.

share.brag.day.line.note: Under the Day headline: the streak the pump kept.

plural.one: The first day of a streak

share.brag.longest.note: Under the minutes headline of a timed pump card.

share.brag.minutes.note: A timed pump card's headline when it was the player's longest timed pump yet.

share.brag.record.note: A share card's headline when its pump set a record (slice 51 share cards, Rapha, 2026-10-21): the move's name and the new record as the record row writes it (22, 45 s). The seal stands beside it.

share.brag.record.new.note: Under a record headline when there was no record before it.

share.brag.record.up.note: Under a record headline: the record it beat, written as the record row writes it (19, 40 s).

share.brag.streak.best.note: Under the streak card's headline when this streak is the player's best.

share.brag.streak.was.note: Under the streak card's headline when the player's best streak is longer.

share.card.note: Label in caps over the Share window's choice of card for a day: the Saga or the Quest Bill.

share.card.bill.note: The Share window's day card drawn as a paper receipt of the day's moves, a joke on a bill paid in full.

share.card.saga.note: The Share window's day card in the Saga's look: the big number, the figure, the day's strip and stats.

share.chooser.save.note: An action in the Android share sheet: saves the card's picture to the phone's photos.

share.chooser.save.video.note: Android 14 and later: the share sheet's own action beside the apps for a reel, putting it into the phone's videos (Movies/QuestPump).

share.chooser.saved.note: Android's own toast after the player chose Save image in the Android share sheet: the card's picture is now in the phone's photos.

share.chooser.saved.video.note: Android's own toast after the player chose Save video in the share sheet: the reel is now in the phone's videos.

share.chooser.unsaved.text: The card could not be saved.
share.chooser.unsaved.note: Android's own toast when Save image in the Android share sheet could not put the card into the phone's photos (no room, or the photos refused it).

share.chooser.unsaved.video.text: The reel could not be saved.
share.chooser.unsaved.video.note: Android's own toast when Save video in the share sheet could not put the reel into the phone's videos.

share.copy.note: The Share window's second button on the computer: puts the card's picture on the clipboard, to paste into a chat or a post.

share.failed.text: The card could not be made. Try again.
share.failed.note: Under the share window's buttons when drawing the card failed (no figure still, no memory, the system refused): the window stays open so the player can try again.

share.format.note: Label in caps over the Share window's picture sizes.

share.format.post.note: A picture in 4:5, for a feed post (1080 by 1350).

share.format.reel.note: The last chip of the Share window's Format row for a day's Saga card (slice 45): the card as a short vertical video of the day's moves, 1080 × 1920 and a few seconds long. The format's name, never a service's.

share.format.sticker.note: The day's number and words on a clear ground, to lay over the player's own picture.

share.format.story.note: A tall picture, 9:16, for a story (1080 by 1920).

share.import.done.title.note: Title in the iPhone's share sheet after Import: the sheet waits for the app, which takes it in at its next opening. QuestPump is the app's name.

share.import.empty.note: Under Not imported: the app that shared sent no text, or only spaces.

share.import.inbox.failed.text: QuestPump could not keep the sheet. Copy it, then paste it in QuestPump under Import a sheet.
share.import.inbox.failed.note: Under Not imported in the iPhone's share sheet: the sheet could not be saved for the app (no room on the phone). Import a sheet is the Menu's own button: keep it as the app names it. QuestPump is the app's name.

share.import.pairlink.text: That is a pairing link, not a sheet. To pair, scan the QR code QuestPump shows on your computer.
share.import.pairlink.note: Under Not imported: a pairing link was shared, and a share only imports sheets; the QR code in the window of QuestPump on the computer pairs. QuestPump is the app's name on the phone and on the computer.

share.import.preview.note: Under Import this sheet?: what the sheet holds. {level} is the character's level, {date} the day the game saved the sheet, in the phone's short date (16 Oct).

share.import.title.note: Title of the window that shows a sheet another app shared with QuestPump, or a questpump:// link opened, before anything is imported. A sheet is the character sheet from the game.

share.plist.photos.text: QuestPump saves a card or reel you share to your photos when you choose Save Image or Save Video.
share.plist.photos.note: The system's question before the share sheet's Save Image or Save Video puts a shared card (the Saga's day, a record, an unlock, the streak) or the day's reel into the photos: add-only access, nothing is read.

share.rare.colour.text: Only {percent} of QuestPump players have reached {colour}.
share.rare.colour.note: The rarity line under a colour headline, from questpump.com's standing (contract/standing-api.yaml): the share of players whose highest colour is this one or above, written as a percentage (0.8%, 6%), and the colour's name. Shown only for a share from 0.1% to 25%.

share.rare.colour.few.text: Fewer than 1 in 1,000 QuestPump players have reached {colour}.
share.rare.colour.few.note: The rarity line under a colour headline when the share is under 0.1%.

share.rare.streak.text: Only {percent} of QuestPump players have kept a streak of {days} days.
share.rare.streak.note: The rarity line under a streak or Day headline, from questpump.com's standing: the share of players whose best streak reached the highest threshold (3, 7, 14, 30, 60, 100, 180, 365 days) at or under the player's streak, and that threshold. Shown only for a share from 0.1% to 25%.

share.rare.streak.few.text: Fewer than 1 in 1,000 QuestPump players have kept a streak of {days} days.
share.rare.streak.few.note: The rarity line under a streak or Day headline when the share is under 0.1%.

share.reel.failed.text: The reel could not be made. Try again.
share.reel.failed.note: Under the preview when making the reel failed; Share (on the computer Save video or Copy video) makes it again.

share.reel.left.text: The reel stopped when you left QuestPump. Share makes it again.
share.reel.left.note: The phones: a reel being made stops when the player leaves the app (the system pauses its video work there); back in the Share window, Share makes it again.

share.reel.making.note: Under the busy Share (on the computer Save video and Copy video) while the day's reel is made, a few seconds (slice 45).

share.reel.none.text: No move of this day has its film yet.
share.reel.none.note: In the reel's place when none of the day's moves has its moving figure on this device yet (the computer before its figures came, a move newer than the app); the cards still work.

share.reel.pause.note: The preview's action while it plays: a tap holds it.

share.reel.play.note: The preview's action while it is held: a tap plays the reel again, muted.

share.reel.ready.note: Announced to VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's screen readers as the made reel takes the still card's place in the preview.

share.reel.spoken.note: How VoiceOver, TalkBack and the computer's screen readers read the reel's preview: a video and its length in whole seconds, rounded (4, 6, 8 or 10), never 1.

share.reel.unsupported.note: The computer only: its system offers no H.264 video encoder (a Windows N edition without its Media Feature Pack), so Reel cannot be made; the cards still can.

share.save.note: The Share window's gold button on the computer: saves the card as a PNG file where the player picks, through the system's save dialog (a computer has no share sheet).

share.sound.note: Label in caps over the Share window's choice of the reel's sound (slice 45): On or Off. The sound is the app's own short sounds, never music.

share.sound.off.note: A chip under Sound: the reel has no sound at all.

share.sound.on.note: A chip under Sound: the reel carries the app's own sounds (on by default).

share.streak.tag.note: The slanted tag on the streak card when the streak's count is one of its milestones (7, 30, 100, 365 or 1,000 days, or 2 to 5 years): shown, never awarded.

share.streak.years.label.note: The caps label under the streak's count on the streak card when the streak is a whole number of years from two (2 / YEAR STREAK); Day streak otherwise (slice 45).

share.style.gilded.note: A style of the shared card: the parchment page in a wide gold band. Part of QuestPump Pro.

share.style.locked.note: Read by VoiceOver and TalkBack on a card style the player has not unlocked: it comes with QuestPump Pro, and a tap opens Pro's offer. Pro is a product name.

share.style.night.note: A style of the shared card: a dark iron page in a gold edge with light words. Part of QuestPump Pro.

share.style.parchment.note: A style of the shared card: the light parchment page, free for everyone.

share.style.title.note: Label in caps over the card's styles in the Share window: the look of the shared picture.

share.text.day.note: The text the share sheet gets with the day card's picture and, since slice 45, with the day's reel. Keep questpump.com as written.

share.text.expedition.note: The text the share sheet gets with a timed pump card's picture. The min is short for minutes and takes no plural. Keep questpump.com as written.

share.text.streak.note: The text the share sheet gets with the streak card's picture: the streak's days. Keep questpump.com as written.

share.text.streak.years.note: The text the share sheet gets with the streak card of a whole number of years, always 2 or more. Keep questpump.com as written.

share.text.week.note: The text the share sheet gets with the week card's picture. Keep questpump.com as written.

share.title.note: Title of the window that shows the card a player is about to share (a record or a step unlocked), with its styles and Share.

share.video.copy.note: The Share window's second button on the computer while Reel is chosen: puts the reel on the clipboard as a file, to paste into a chat.

share.video.save.note: The Share window's gold button on the computer while Reel is chosen: saves the reel as an MP4 file where the player picks, through the system's save dialog.

watch.complication.streak.note: The Streak complication's name in the watch face editor.

watch.count.cap.note: Under the watch's count while it stands at its most (slice 66): half again what the watch counted; {max} in the move's unit, reps as a number (45), seconds as m:ss (1:00). The Apple Watch shows it once its count moves onto the dial (owed, slice 66).

watch.count.form.note: The watch's question after a counted set (slice 42; since slice 53 it asks the effort too), over the optional clean count.

watch.count.held.note: A hold's count in seconds on the count's number (45 s).

watch.count.less.note: Read out only: the button that lowers the count by one.

watch.count.more.note: Read out only: the button that raises the count by one.

watch.count.record.note: Under the count: the player's record on this move ({count} reps, or seconds on a hold).

watch.count.record.hold.note: Under a hold's count: the player's record on this hold, in seconds (Record 45 s).

watch.count.record.load.note: Under the count on a move done with a weight: the player's weighted record, {record} as the weight and the reps read (10 kg × 20).

watch.countdown.ready.note: The countdown's first word, before 5-4-3-2-1. One short word in the title face.

watch.ending.saving.note: Under a spinner while the ended session is saved.

watch.figure.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint): a tap plays the figure's move once.

watch.figure.label.text: The move, shown by the armour figure
watch.figure.label.note: Read out only: the animated figure that shows the move. The armour figure is the app's knight in armour.

watch.glance.stat.agility.note: Agility, short, shown in capitals over its number.

watch.glance.stat.intellect.note: Intellect, short, shown in capitals over its number.

watch.glance.stat.spirit.note: Spirit, short, shown in capitals over its number.

watch.glance.stat.stamina.note: Stamina, short, shown in capitals over its number.

watch.glance.stat.strength.note: Strength, short, shown in capitals over its number.

watch.glance.title.note: The glance's title and the row that opens it: the muscles worked today and the five stats.

watch.goal.hold.note: A hold's goal in seconds: the least the pump asks, with a plus for more (26+ s). Keep the plus after the number.

watch.heart.none.note: Read out only: no heart-rate reading yet, or the last one is too old (a dash shows).

watch.heart.rate.note: Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the heart rate beside its heart glyph. {bpm}: beats a minute.

watch.idle.closed.text: The game closed. The session ends and is saved in {time}.
watch.idle.closed.note: Under Still playing? after the game quit. {time}: the time left, minutes and seconds, counting down ("9:58"; on the Apple Watch in Always On whole minutes, "5 min").

watch.idle.end.note: Button, and the notification's action: the session ends and is saved now.

watch.idle.keepgoing.note: Button, and the notification's action: the session goes on.

watch.idle.notap.text: No tap for a while. The session ends and is saved in {time}.
watch.idle.notap.note: Under Still playing? after a long time without a tap. {time}: the time left, minutes and seconds, counting down (on the Apple Watch in Always On whole minutes, "5 min").

watch.idle.title.note: The idle rule's question: the game closed, or no tap for a while. Also the notification's title and, on Wear OS, its notification channel's name.

watch.intent.pump.note: The Action button's action during a session, in Shortcuts and the Action button settings: start the next pump.

watch.intent.session.note: The name of the start action's parameter in Shortcuts: which kind of session (there is one, the play session).

watch.label.avgbpm.note: A label under a number: the average heart rate in the move, in beats a minute (bpm).

watch.label.avgbpm.short.note: The short form of average bpm where the long one does not fit: the average heart rate in beats a minute.

watch.label.cadence.note: A label under a number: the steps a minute in the move.

watch.label.distance.note: A label under a number: the distance walked in the move. Lower case, as a unit.

watch.label.time.note: A label under a number: how long the move took. Lower case, as a unit.

watch.legend.continue.note: The gold button of the wrist's Legendary moment: goes on as the move's card would (the next move, or close).

watch.legend.step.note: On the wrist's Legendary moment, under the move: the ladder and its step on the one scale of fourteen (Push · step 13).

watch.link.connected.note: The helper link is up. {name}: the computer's name ("David's MacBook Pro"). Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the link's dot in the session screen's top row.

watch.link.connecting.note: The helper link's first request is on its way. {name}: the computer's name. Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the link's dot in the session screen's top row.

watch.link.localnetwork.text: Allow Nearby devices for QuestPump in the watch's settings.
watch.link.localnetwork.note: The watch may not use the local network (Android's Nearby devices permission was refused), so its link to the helper waits. Nearby devices is the name of the permission in the watch's settings: use the watch's name in the language.

watch.link.looking.note: Read out only: the watch looks the computer up by its name on the network. {name}: the computer's name.

watch.link.newcode.iphone.text: New code on {name}. Pair again on your iPhone.
watch.link.newcode.iphone.note: The helper on the computer has a new pairing code, which only the iPhone can scan. {name}: the computer's name.

watch.link.newcode.phone.text: New code on {name}. Pair again on your phone.
watch.link.newcode.phone.note: The helper on the computer has a new pairing code, which only the phone can scan. {name}: the computer's name.

watch.link.unreachable.iphone.text: Can't reach {name}. Open QuestPump on your iPhone to find it.
watch.link.unreachable.iphone.note: The helper does not answer; the iPhone app, open in front, searches the network for it. {name}: the computer's name.

watch.link.unreachable.phone.text: Can't reach {name}. Open QuestPump on your phone to find it.
watch.link.unreachable.phone.note: The helper does not answer; the phone app, open in front, searches the network for it. {name}: the computer's name.

watch.localnetwork.continue.note: Wear OS only: the button under the page before Android asks for local network access; Android's question follows.

watch.notify.idle.body.note: The idle notification's text, its two sentences together: {why} is why it asks (watch.notify.idle.closed or watch.notify.idle.notap), {ending} when the session ends (watch.notify.idle.ends.phone). Join them as the language joins two sentences (no space in Japanese or Chinese).

watch.notify.idle.closed.note: The idle notification's first sentence after the game quit; the sentence on when the session ends follows.

watch.notify.idle.ends.health.text: QuestPump ends the play session in {minutes} minutes and saves the workout.

plural.one: QuestPump ends the play session in {minutes} minute and saves the workout.
plural.other: QuestPump ends the play session in {minutes} minutes and saves the workout.

watch.notify.idle.ends.health.note: The idle notification's second sentence: unless the player taps, the session ends and is saved.

watch.notify.idle.ends.phone.text: QuestPump ends the play session in {minutes} minutes and sends it to your phone.

plural.one: QuestPump ends the play session in {minutes} minute and sends it to your phone.
plural.other: QuestPump ends the play session in {minutes} minutes and sends it to your phone.

watch.notify.idle.ends.phone.note: The idle notification's second sentence: unless the player taps, the session ends and goes to the phone.

watch.notify.idle.notap.note: The idle notification's first sentence after no tap for a while; the sentence on when the session ends follows.

watch.notify.move.count.text: Set your count, then tap Save.
watch.notify.move.count.note: The play session's notification while a pump of the watch's own asks the count of the move just done: the count is set with the crown or its keys, Save is the button (pump.count.save).

watch.notify.move.start.text: Tap Start when you are ready.
watch.notify.move.start.note: The play session's notification while a pump of the watch's own waits on its Ready: Start is the button that counts its next move down (pump.ready.start).

watch.notify.pump.note: The notification's title, and its short text on the watch face, while a pump runs (a pump: the moves a quest turn-in costs).

watch.notify.ready.text.note: The notification's line while a pump counts down; the system shows the seconds left beside it.

watch.notify.ready.title.note: The notification's title while a pump counts down to its start.

watch.notify.running.done.text: Tap Done when the move ends.
watch.notify.running.done.note: The notification's line while a move runs. Done is the button's name.

watch.notify.running.sides.text: The other side starts by itself at zero.
watch.notify.running.sides.note: The notification's line while the first side of a timed move done on each side runs on the watch's own pump: its clock counts down and the other side's countdown starts when it reaches zero (the system shows the time left beside it).

watch.notify.running.switch.text: Tap Switch sides when this side ends.
watch.notify.running.switch.note: The notification's line on a one-sided move's first side in a pump of the watch's own whose side runs until the player ends it (a hold, a move of reps, or a catch-up's timed move, which the watch times with its stopwatch), so the player taps the running screen's Switch sides button (use watch.running.switch's words) when the side is done.

watch.notify.running.timed.text: The move ends by itself at zero.
watch.notify.running.timed.note: The notification's line while a timed move of the watch's own pump runs: its clock counts down and the move ends when it reaches zero (the system shows the time left beside it).

watch.notify.session.solo.text: Tap Pump when you finish a quest, a match or a level.
watch.notify.session.solo.note: The play session's notification without a computer paired: a pump after each thing the player finishes.

watch.notify.status.countdown.note: The ongoing activity's status on the watch face while a pump counts down. Keep #t# as written: the system puts the seconds left there.

watch.notify.status.running.note: The ongoing activity's status on the watch face while a pump runs. Keep #t# as written: the system puts the move's time there.

watch.notify.switch.text.note: The notification's line while a one-sided move's other side counts down.

watch.pace.eased.note: The watch's pace answer 3 (slice 42; one of three since slice 52), as pump.pace.eased.

watch.pace.easily.note: The watch's pace answer 1 (slice 52), as pump.pace.easily: kept to the end with room to spare.

watch.pace.held.note: The watch's pace answer 2 (slice 52; The whole time from slice 42 until then), as pump.pace.held: kept to the end with little to spare, the old held answer's code.

watch.pace.title.text: Kept the pace to the end?
watch.pace.title.note: The pace ask's question on the watch (slice 42, 2026-10-17; since slice 52 the Stamina Ledger's ask, as pump.pace.title): on the wrist's own pumps (a game pump the wrist follows, a Long Haul too, the game asks; slice 55).

watch.phoneapp.failed.text: Your phone didn't answer. Try again.
watch.phoneapp.failed.note: Wear OS: under Open on phone when the phone did not open the listing.

watch.phoneapp.open.note: Wear OS: opens Play's listing of QuestPump on the paired phone (Wear OS's own words for the action).

watch.phoneapp.sent.note: Wear OS: under Open on phone once the phone opened Play's listing.

watch.phoneapp.title.note: Wear OS: the start page's card while the paired Android phone has no QuestPump (2026-10-09).

watch.pick.place.note: A quiet line on the watch's pick page (slice 51): {place} is the place in use on the phone (its name, or its template's words), whose equipment and switches the watch's pumps follow. Never a button.

watch.plist.healthshare.text: QuestPump reads your heart rate, steps and distance during a play session to show them for every pump.
watch.plist.healthshare.note: The Apple Watch's Health permission sheet: why the app reads health data.

watch.plist.healthupdate.text: QuestPump saves each play session as a workout in Apple Health, with a segment for every pump.
watch.plist.healthupdate.note: The Apple Watch's question before it saves play sessions to Apple Health (Info.plist).

watch.plist.motion.text: QuestPump counts your steps and distance during each pump.
watch.plist.motion.note: The Apple Watch's Motion & Fitness permission alert: why the app reads the pedometer.

watch.reading.cadence.note: Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the name of the steps-a-minute number.

watch.reading.distance.note: Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the name of the distance number.

watch.reading.steps.note: Read out only (VoiceOver, TalkBack): the name of the steps number.

watch.report.title.note: The small capitals over the reasons a coach line can be reported for. A noun.

watch.resting.line.text: You felt unwell. Pumps start again at {time}.
watch.resting.line.note: Why pumps rest after the player stopped for feeling unwell, and until when. {time}: the time of day as the watch shows it ("04:00", "4:00 AM").

watch.result.clean.note: The watch summary's line after a clean counted set under the form's best (slice 42): {count} the clean reps, {best} the best that stands (31 clean · best 34).

watch.result.game.text: {goal} · type your count in the game
watch.result.game.note: A game move's result on the watch: its goal ({goal}, like 16+), and that the count is typed in the game.

watch.result.join.note: Joins two parts of one line (+45 XP · +1 Strength; Unlocked: Archer push-up · Rare; Count every rep · 16+). Keep the middle dot or use your language's list separator.

watch.result.level.note: In the rewards line: the level the pump reached when it rose.

watch.result.saved.note: A move's result on the watch: the count saved, then its goal ({goal} is like 16+): 18 · goal 16+.

watch.result.typecount.text: Type your count in the game
watch.result.typecount.note: A game move without a goal (a max set): the count is typed in the game.

watch.rows.phone.text: Open QuestPump on your phone, then try again.
watch.rows.phone.note: When the phone's rows did not come: the watch needs them once before its first pump, so the goals are the player's own.

watch.rows.waiting.text: Getting your records from your phone…
watch.rows.waiting.note: While the watch waits for its phone's rows before its first pump (a new watch app, or a pump started from the phone): the pump's goals come from them.

watch.running.done.note: Button: the player finished the move (not a dismiss button).

watch.running.end.note: Button beside The game switches sides: ends the move on this side when the game's countdown for the other side never comes. End move, never End alone, which ends the session (watch.session.end).

watch.running.end.hint.text: Ends the move on this side
watch.running.end.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint) for the small End button.

watch.running.gameswitches.note: On a game move's first side: the game starts the other side by itself, so no Done shows. Also Wear OS's notification text then.

watch.running.go.note: Shown for the move's first second in place of the clock: start now.

watch.running.minutes.note: A clock in whole minutes: the session's minutes in the session screen's top row (both watches), and on the Apple Watch a clock in Always On at a minute's cadence, where seconds would stand still. {count}: whole minutes.

watch.running.switch.note: Button on a one-sided move's first side: this side is done, the other starts.

watch.running.target.note: Under the running clock of a catch-up from the watch: the move's target time on this side, which the clock counts up to (the wrist gives one haptic there). {time}: minutes and seconds ("0:45").

watch.running.time.note: Read out only: the move's clock. {time}: minutes and seconds, or whole minutes in Always On.

watch.session.anymove.note: Stands for a move's name where this app does not know the move (one a newer game added): a row of the watch's own pump, a Swap option or an unfinished move.

watch.session.blind.text: QuestPump on your computer can't see the game yet.
watch.session.blind.note: On the watch's session screen in place of the line that countdowns come from the game, while QuestPump on the computer cannot see World of Warcraft: no countdown comes until it can.

watch.session.clock.note: Read out only (VoiceOver): the session's stopwatch. {time}: minutes and seconds ("14:12"), or whole minutes in Always On.

watch.session.end.note: Button at the foot of the session screen: ends the play session (a confirmation follows). End session, never End alone, beside the running move's End move.

watch.session.end.health.text: The workout goes to Apple Health with a segment for every move.
watch.session.end.health.note: The confirmation's line: the session is saved as one workout with a part for each move.

watch.session.end.phone.text: The session goes to your phone for Health Connect.
watch.session.end.phone.note: The confirmation's line: the watch sends the session to the phone, which saves it in Health Connect.

watch.session.end.save.note: Button in the confirmation: ends the session and saves the workout.

watch.session.end.send.note: Button in the confirmation: ends the session and sends it to the phone.

watch.session.end.title.note: The confirmation's question before the session ends.

watch.session.extra.note: Button with a computer paired: a pump of the watch's own (an app pump), beside the game's pumps.

watch.session.extra.hint.text: Starts a pump now, without the game. The game gets it when it next loads.
watch.session.extra.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint) for the extra pump button: its counts reach the game's records when the game next loads (a login or a reload of its interface).

watch.session.fromgame.note: With a computer paired: the session's state while the game sends each pump's countdown to the watch, so the player need not tap Pump. On the session screen and in Wear OS's session notification.

watch.session.moves.note: The session's count of moves done in the screen's top row, beside the session clock.

watch.session.pump.note: The big button: starts the countdown of the next pump (a pump is the set of moves a quest turn-in costs). One short word.

watch.session.pump.hint.text: Opens Quick pump, or pick what you finished; the watch picks the moves
watch.session.pump.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint) for the Pump button: it opens the page that starts a Quick pump or picks what the player finished and the size of an app pump; either way the watch picks the moves. Apple's hints start with a verb in the third person.

watch.session.resting.note: The session screen's title while pumps rest after the player stopped for feeling unwell.

watch.session.resting.game.text: To pause the game too: Pause, then I feel unwell.
watch.session.resting.game.note: How to skip the game's own pump while resting: Pause is the game panel's button, I feel unwell the choice in its menu. Keep both as the game reads them.

watch.session.unfinished.note: Row: opens the moves the game still owes the player. {count}: how many.

watch.session.unfinished.hint.text: Opens the banked moves from the game
watch.session.unfinished.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint) for the unfinished row.

watch.side.first.note: Over a one-sided move: the first side runs now.

watch.side.other.note: Over a one-sided move's clock: the other side runs now.

watch.side.switch.note: Over the countdown of a one-sided move's other side, and Wear OS's notification title then: the player turns to the other side now.

watch.start.button.note: Button: starts a play session (the watch's workout while the player plays).

watch.start.disclosure.text: QuestPump reads your heart rate during a session to show whether a pump raised it. It never blocks a pump and is not a medical device.
watch.start.disclosure.note: Shown before the watch asks for the heart-rate permission (Google Play's health apps policy). Legal wording: keep "not a medical device" whole.

watch.start.pairedwith.note: A line under the start button: the computer the watch's helper link is paired with. {name}: the computer's name, as the helper reports it ("David's MacBook Pro").

watch.start.problem.ended.text: The workout ended before it started.
watch.start.problem.ended.note: A start problem: the system ended the workout while its permission sheet was up (another workout app started).

watch.start.problem.failed.text: The session did not start. Try again.
watch.start.problem.failed.note: A start problem without a known cause (the system's own description goes to the log only).

watch.start.problem.nogrant.text: Allow heart rate or physical activity for QuestPump in the watch's settings.
watch.start.problem.nogrant.note: A start problem: the player refused both permissions. Heart rate and physical activity are the names of the two permissions in the watch's settings.

watch.start.problem.nohealth.text: Apple Health is not available on this watch.
watch.start.problem.nohealth.note: A start problem: this watch has no Apple Health (the session cannot start).

watch.start.problem.notallowed.text: QuestPump needs to save workouts in Apple Health. Allow it when asked, or in the Health app on your iPhone (Profile, Apps, QuestPump).
watch.start.problem.notallowed.note: A start problem: the player refused saving workouts. Profile, Apps and QuestPump name the Health app's own screens in its order: use the Health app's words in the language.

watch.start.problem.notsaved.text: The workout was not saved to Apple Health.
watch.start.problem.notsaved.note: A problem on the start screen: the ended session's workout could not be saved, or the session that ran when the app quit could not be taken up again (the system's own description goes to the log only).

watch.start.problem.otherapp.text: Another app runs a workout on this watch. End it first.
watch.start.problem.otherapp.note: A start problem: another app's exercise holds the watch's sensors.

watch.start.problem.refused.text: The watch did not start the session.
watch.start.problem.refused.note: A start problem: the watch's sensors refused the session (Health Services failed to register it).

watch.start.saved.health.note: The start screen's line after a session ended: the workout was saved to Apple Health. {length}: the session's length as the system formats it ("1 hr, 12 min"); {count}: the moves done in it.

watch.start.saved.phone.text: Saved: {length}, {count} moves. Your phone gets it when it is near.

plural.one: Saved: {length}, {count} move. Your phone gets it when it is near.
plural.other: Saved: {length}, {count} moves. Your phone gets it when it is near.

watch.start.saved.phone.note: The start screen's line after a session ended: the watch keeps the session until the phone is in reach, which then writes it to Health Connect. {length}: the session's length as the system formats it ("1 hr, 12 min"); {count}: the moves done in it.

watch.summary.next.note: Button on a move's card while the pump has moves left: its next move's Ready.

watch.summary.peak.note: The highest heart rate in the pump. {peak}: beats a minute.

watch.summary.peakrise.note: The highest heart rate in the pump and its rise over the minute before. {peak}: beats a minute; {rise}: the rise with its sign, formatted by the app ("+27").

watch.summary.rest.note: Under Felt unwell, once the lock has ended.

watch.summary.restuntil.text: Rest now. Pumps start again at {time}.
watch.summary.restuntil.note: Under Felt unwell: rest, and when pumps start again. {time}: the time of day as the watch shows it ("04:00").

watch.summary.unwell.note: The card's title after the player stopped the pump for feeling unwell (in place of the verdict).

watch.system.about.text: Heart rate and steps for every pump
watch.system.about.note: What a play session gives: the Start tile's main line (Wear OS) and the session's subtitle in Shortcuts (Apple Watch).

watch.system.playsession.note: The name of the watch's session while the player plays: the session notification's title and status, its notification channel's name (Wear OS), and its name in Shortcuts and Siri (Apple Watch).

watch.system.start.note: The start action's name: the Start tile's name in the tile picker (Wear OS); the complication's name, its line and the Shortcuts action (Apple Watch).

watch.system.startshort.note: One short word on a corner of the watch face: start a play session (the Apple Watch's Start complication). Wear OS's Start tile shows watch.tile.pump on its button since slice 32.

watch.tile.pump.note: The tile's gold chip and the complication's word in its Start form (no streak yet): it opens the watch's pump.

watch.tile.resting.note: The watch surfaces while the felt-unwell lock holds: no Pump, this line in its place.

watch.tile.streak.note: Under the streak's count on the tile and the complication.

watch.unfinished.elsewhere.text: {count} all-out moves: on your phone or in the game

plural.one: {count} all-out move: on your phone or in the game
plural.other: {count} all-out moves: on your phone or in the game

watch.unfinished.elsewhere.note: Under the unfinished moves, and on the session in the unfinished row's place when only these are owed: the all-out windows, which the watch leaves to the phone or the game. {count}: how many.

watch.unfinished.held.text: Skipped: a joint you marked as hurting
watch.unfinished.held.note: Under an unfinished move the watch will not run: a pain flag the player set rests a joint it loads.

watch.unfinished.row.hint.text: Opens this move from the game. The game takes it the next time it loads.
watch.unfinished.row.hint.note: Read out only (VoiceOver hint) for an unfinished move's row: a tap opens the move's Ready (since 2026-11-02, with Swap), and the game sees the move when it next loads (a login or a reload of its interface).

watch.unit.cadence.note: A unit beside a number: steps a minute (cadence). Short, as a unit.

watch.unit.steps.note: A unit or label beside or under a number: the steps counted in the move. Lower case, as a unit.

watch.unwell.button.note: The stop button on a pump of the watch's own, between pumps and on a pump's card: the pump stops and every pump rests until 4 in the morning. The player's own words, first person.

watch.unwell.hint.text: Stops and rests every pump until 4 in the morning.
watch.unwell.hint.note: Read out after I feel unwell (VoiceOver hint; TalkBack reads it in the button's description). 4 in the morning: the game day's turn, 04:00.

watch.unwell.spoken.note: Read out only (TalkBack): the I feel unwell button's description, its words ({button}: watch.unwell.button) and then what it does ({hint}: watch.unwell.hint), as VoiceOver reads a button's label and then its hint. Join them as the language joins two sentences.

watch.verdict.checking.note: The card's verdict until the minute after the go has passed: the heart rate is still being read.

watch.verdict.nohr.note: The card's verdict: there was no heart-rate reading.

watch.verdict.proven.note: The heart rate rose enough for the pump's check mark (the phones' Heart rate counted). Never says the count was saved.

watch.verdict.unproven.note: The card's verdict: the heart rate did not show the rise, so the pump gets no heart-rate mark; it still counts in the game. Gentle, never a judgement (David, 2026-10-04: it replaced Not proven).

watch.widget.description.text: Starts QuestPump's play session: heart rate and steps for every pump.
watch.widget.description.note: The complication's description in the watch face editor.

watch.widget.inline.note: The one-line complication over the watch face's time: starts a play session.

watch.widget.label.note: Read out only: the complication's spoken name.

watch.widget.wear.description.text: Your streak and a pump in one tap
watch.widget.wear.description.note: Wear OS only: the Wear Widget's description.

watch.wifi.add.note: Button: opens the watch's settings to add a Wi-Fi network (none saved is in range).

watch.wifi.check.text: Check that QuestPump runs on your computer and the watch is on its Wi-Fi.
watch.wifi.check.note: On the watch's own Wi-Fi and still no answer: QuestPump on the computer is closed, or on another network. QuestPump is the app's name.

watch.wifi.finding.note: The watch looks for a saved Wi-Fi network in range.

watch.wifi.use.note: Button: the helper link moves onto the watch's own Wi-Fi.

widget.streak.description.text: A pump in one tap, and your streak.
widget.streak.description.note: The widget's description in the gallery.

widget.streak.name.note: The widget's name in the system's widget gallery.
